Left empty, no preview is saved; a value the daemon refuses is shown at its field. After setup the preview is changed from Settings, under "How to open your app", which is there while the team has a Designer that is not retired, the change shown before it is saved (added in 0.33). Under its fields a line says whether the owner's environment file for the app is there, from `team.get`'s `preview_env_present`: "Your app’s settings file is in place. <designer> starts your app with it." or "No settings file for your app. If it needs keys or addresses, put them in .catervas/local/preview.env in your project folder.", with an ⓘ saying one `NAME=value` per line without quotes, that only the app gets it while it runs, that no agent can read it and it is never committed, to use keys for testing, and to write `host.docker.internal` for a service on this computer. Settings never shows, takes or uploads its contents; the owner puts the file there. The start command's hint says the app can reach the internet and this computer while it runs (added in 0.120; ADR 0067). The wizard's steps after the computer, the account and the project are these (added in 0.26). Step 4 is the read-back of the scan, which the user confirms, or corrects in a few words that Catervas keeps in `.catervas/project.md`, dated, under "The user says", across every rescan, `catervas init`'s and an integration's alike; it lists what the project is, how it is tested and checked, its last change, and the files kept private, the folder Catervas keeps its own files in left out. Step 5 is the team; step 6 the two permission questions; step 7 the daily budget; step 8 the last screen, which says that finished work opens a pull request on GitHub for the owner to merge when the project is online (`team.get`'s `online`), and that it stays on the computer for the owner to merge otherwise, with nothing to choose (changed in 0.124) (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061), and Start the team. A team started from a saved one skips step 6, so its wizard has seven steps (added in 0.35). Setup can be gone back through (added in 0.106): each step in the step list before the current one is a link to it, and the list's links are off while the project page is moving the team (4.4) or opening a project, since they would mislead there; the scan has Back to the project step; and the project step, while a project is already chosen and setup is pending, offers "Keep <name>" as its main button, beside Continue. The team's answers are kept for the browser tab while the project is the same, and forgotten when the team starts; going to an earlier step from the daily budget keeps the typed limit. The daily budget shows an example of a limit under its amount field: what a day at 64% of it looks like, and that at the limit everyone pauses and the user gets a message (added in 0.106). Under the last screen's "Show advanced settings" button, opened in place on that screen and not at an address of its own (changed in 0.106; `/setup/advanced` goes to the last screen), are the team's rules, the checks (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: the plan check and who checks it are gone, 5.3) (added in 0.36). Setup asks no question about how work is planned and its last screen has no box about it (changed in 0.116; ADR 0062). Before it saves, the wizard asks the daemon to validate the team, and a refusal is shown at the agent it concerns. The team starts paused, and Start the team saves the team and the checks, removes the marker and resumes the team, in one call; the page opens on the setup screens for as long as the marker is there. The marker is `.catervas/local/setup-pending`, which the setup host writes when it made the project a Catervas project; only a start while it is there resumes the team, so a team paused by a budget's stop or by the user stays paused (changed in 0.26).

The user is shown the default permissions for each role and asked to confirm two things explicitly: whether agents may run commands, and whether they may push to git. The user is also offered a daily budget in dollars, which is optional: left empty, the team has no daily dollar limit (ADR 0015). Both start at the recommended answers, `settings.defaults`' (run commands: yes; push: no), which the user may change, here or later in Settings; the page asks for no answer before Continue (changed in 0.106).

The team appears on the board, and in the desktop app the office populates and agents walk to their desks (changed in 0.18). The Product Manager posts in the channel a first reading of the project and asks the user two or three questions. For a new project it does not: once setup ends and the team runs, the Product Manager opens an interview of the owner in its one-to-one chat, one question at a time (4.3; added in 0.99), and the product plan follows from it. The user's first request, typed in reply, is filed, triaged, and contracted (5.16).

**A new project's Today (added in 0.100; ADR 0051; phase 8 step 06b; changed in 0.115).** While a project started in Catervas has no accepted product plan task (`product_plan.state`'s `new_project` is not null and `approved` is false), the team band's first line on Today is "<Project>: your team waits for your product plan", <Project> being the folder's name with each `-` a space and each word's first letter in upper case (`little-oak-cakes` is "Little Oak Cakes"). `team.activity` words the agents' lines the same while the plan waits, in the daemon: an idle agent says "Nothing to do until your plan is approved", an idle Scrum Master "Nothing to plan until your plan is approved", and an agent waiting on the product plan's task "Waiting on you: your product plan"; a working, resting or paused agent keeps its line. The web app shows a waiting agent's line as "Waiting on you" alone (changed in 0.123). Once the plan's task is accepted the lines are the team's own again (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061).

While a project is being left (4.4), the project page says "Moving your team from <folder>" and offers "Stay on <folder>" beside open and create (added in 0.83, ADR 0053). Opening or creating a folder then runs the same checks as in setup. Opening the project being left is taking it on as it is: no copy, no reset. A folder that already has a Catervas team (`.catervas/team.yaml`) is refused with `has_team` unless `project.open` carries `replace: true` (`project.create` makes a new folder and takes no `replace`); the page asks "<folder> already has a Catervas team. It will be replaced by yours, starting fresh; your code is not touched." and retries with `replace: true` when the user confirms. Any other folder, and a replaced one after its `.catervas/` is deleted (a `.catervas/` with no `team.yaml`, a leftover, is deleted too, with no confirmation, so none of its memory carries into the new team), gets `init` and then the team the user is leaving, carried as 4.4 says, written over the starter team and recorded as `team.updated`. That take-on has no setup marker and does not pause the team, so the page lands on Today with the team ready. A take-on that fails goes back to the project page with the reason and leaves the old project as it was, so Stay on still works.

**A project of several repositories (added in 0.110; ADR 0057; phase 9 step 01).** `project.create_folder { parent, name, repos: [{ name, path, integration_branch? }], no_sandbox }` makes the project folder `parent/name`, relative to home, of two to sixteen existing repositories (one repository is not a project folder of one: it is opened with `project.open`), and answers the folder as `project.create` does. `name` follows `project.create`'s rule; `parent` need not exist yet, so the wizard's default `Catervas` under home works for a first project folder, and a `parent` with a `..`, a root or a prefix, or whose nearest existing folder lies outside home once its links are followed, is refused as `outside_home`. Every check runs before anything is made, in this order: the name, the parent, that `parent/name` is not there, each member against the folder and the members before it, the account, git. A member is refused with one sentence, lower case with no full stop, that the wizard shows (`SetupError::Refused`) and the daemon's `repo.*` answer with `data.errors` of `{ path, message, code }` (a JSON pointer as in 5.17's `files.save`): from the file system `not_there`, `outside_home`, `home_itself`, `not_a_repository`, `not_the_top` (it is inside a repository whose top folder is inside home; the sentence names the top folder; inside one whose top is home itself or above it, a home folder kept in git, it is `not_a_repository` instead, so that no refusal points at home or outside it) and `has_team` (it has a Catervas team of its own; a repository with one cannot join), all at `/path`; from the rules on names and paths `repo_name` and `name_taken` (`/name`), `path_taken`, `nested` (inside a member or holding one), `inside_project_folder` and `holds_project_folder` (`/path`) and `too_many_repos` (`/name`, a seventeenth); and `no_such_branch` (`/integration_branch`, an integration branch that is not a local branch of the member). `create_folder` ends a refused member's sentence with `: ` and the member's path as sent, so that the page names the folder. Then it makes the folder with `git init -b main`, a `README.md` and the commit "Start the project", writes `.catervas/repos.yaml` (8.4), takes the folder on as `project.create` does (`init`, then the carried team while a project is being left, else a paused team with the setup marker), and records `repo.added` for each member in request order (8.5). It records no `project.started` and files no first request: its members are existing repositories, so the project is not new, and the Catervafication is offered as for any existing repository.

A project folder is opened with `project.open` as any project is. While a project is being left, a folder whose `.catervas/` holds both `repos.yaml` and `team.yaml` is refused whatever `replace` says, with "that folder is a project of several repositories; it cannot take your team", so that the page never offers Replace for it; a leftover `.catervas/` with `repos.yaml` and no `team.yaml` keeps `repos.yaml` alone when the rest is deleted, and the folder is taken on with the carried team.

**A project folder's scan (added in 0.112; ADR 0057; phase 9 step 02b).** The scan of a project folder is its members', never its own, because the folder holds documents and a scan of it would find nothing to run and replace what the members found. It runs when the folder is made (`catervas init`, as `project.create_folder` takes the folder on), when `repo.add` or `repo.locate` joins or moves a member (that member alone is reseeded, under the integration lock and after the event that records the change) and when `repo.remove` takes one away (its found checks are dropped and `criteria.updated` is recorded by `catervas` when anything went, then the others are scanned again, so `project.md` no longer names it). The scan reads each present member in `repos.yaml` order with the member's own scan (5.8) and joins the read-backs as `<name>: <read-back>`, separated by `; `: `project.md` leads with that, and `project.scanned` carries it with every check found, by its renamed name. A member whose folder is not where `repos.yaml` says it is reads `<name>: not found`, and one whose scan failed `<name>: not read (<why>)`; neither is an error, and each keeps its entries. A failure of the files or the log answers `INTERNAL_ERROR` with its sentence, and the member stays added, moved or removed. The `project.scan` query keeps the facts, checks and `app_start` of the project's root, and gains `repos`: one row `{ name, facts, checks, error }` per member in `repos.yaml` order, each from a scan of that member alone, with `facts` null, `checks` empty and `error` `not found` or the scan's sentence for a member that is missing or whose scan failed, and `error` null otherwise; it is null for a project of one repository.

**Catervafication offered (added in 0.101; ADR 0051; phase 8 step 07).** After setup, an existing repository's team is offered a Catervafication (3). `catervafication.get {}` answers `{ offered, roles }`: `offered` is true while the log holds neither `catervafication.started` nor `project.started` and a Start would not be refused for want of a Product Manager and someone to check its notes (5.17), and `roles` are the roles that would get a task, in the order they are filed. The owner's word `catervafication_start` begins it (5.17). A new project's Catervafication begins by itself once its product plan's task is accepted, and the epic needs no approval (5.16; changed in 0.115; ADR 0061). The offer's screens are described below.

**The offer on screen (added in 0.102; ADR 0051; phase 8 step 07b; changed in 0.117; ADR 0063).** "Start the team" ends on `/setup/ready`, beside `/setup/scan` and outside the team screens' shared draft. The page asks `catervafication.get` and `team.get`; when `offered` is false (a new project, or one already started) it goes to Today, replacing its place in the history, so a new project lands where it did. Otherwise it is the setup's two-panel page with every step done (the stepper says ", done" to a reader for each step behind the current one, so the earlier pages say it for the steps behind them too): the title "Your team is ready", the lead "<names> have joined <team>. They know what Catervas found in your project; next, they can learn it properly.", <names> the active agents' display names in team-file order joined by ", " and, before the last, " and ", and a section, "Recommended", headed "Start with a Catervafication": "Your team reads your project, writes down what it learns, looks for bugs and starts your marketing. You can read all of it in Files." Then one row for each role of `roles`, in its order, for the first active agent of that role in team-file order: its face, its name in bold, its role tag and the role's line. The Product Manager "writes what your product is and what comes next, as your product plan to approve.", the Architect "writes how your project is put together, with diagrams.", the Software Developer "writes how your project is built and worked on, and looks for bugs in the code.", the UI/UX Designer "writes down every screen your project has, and looks for what is broken on them." and the Marketing Specialist "writes your marketing plan and starts on it; anything that costs money waits for you."; the Scrum Master has no row, since it writes the cadence at the retro. The section ends "Your team adds its notes and files each bug it finds as a request; nothing in your code changes yet.", "Start", "Later" and "Later keeps this on Today." Start sends `catervafication_start` and goes to Today; a refusal is said under the buttons as an alert, `catervafication_started` as "Your team is already documenting this project.", `catervafication_new_project` as "A new project's documenting work starts by itself once its product plan is written.", `catervafication_no_product_manager` as "Your Product Manager is paused. Resume them on the Team page, then start." and `catervafication_no_writers` as "No one on your team can both write and have their notes checked. Add an Architect or a Scrum Master on the Team page, then start." Later sends nothing and goes to Today. The "What moved" lines about setup that the mockup draws ("You finished setting up your team.") are context and not built: no event marks setup's end.

**Several teams in one serve (added in 0.144; ADR 0059; phase 10 step 05).** `catervas serve` drives every team on the computer at once, the project it is run in and each project `state.json` lists (8.4), each with its own run lock, `daemon.json`, orchestrator, idle tick and log as a single team has them. A project another process drives (`catervas start` in a terminal) is not driven, shows as elsewhere and is tried again every minute; a project with no team any more shows as missing and stays one of the teams until it is removed. A team that fails, or is stopped with `catervas stop`, ends alone and the others go on; `catervas serve` ends when no team is driven, with 130 after Ctrl-C (the first press stops every orchestrator, the second the sessions of every team), else 1 when a team failed and 0 otherwise. The wizard's project step adds a team: choosing a project starts its drive beside the others, and choosing one that is a team already is refused `team_already_here` ("that project is already one of your teams"). The browser connects once, with one session for every team.

**Finding the owner's projects in the first run (added in 0.146; ADR 0059; phase 10 step 06).** Whether there is history to look through is `finding.offer`: `claude_code` when `<claude folder>/projects/` holds a `.jsonl` file, counted without reading one, else `none`. The first scan starts only when the owner presses "Look for my projects" (`finding.start`); it runs in the background, one at a time, publishing its counts at most every 250 ms, and the owner may stop it (`finding.stop`) and start it again, since what was read stays in the index. While serve runs, finding is not paused and the index exists, serve scans again at start and every 24 hours.

**The first run's pages for finding (added in 0.147; ADR 0059; phase 10 step 06c).** When `finding.offer` says `claude_code`, the computer check shows, below its rows, the card "We found your Claude Code history · Find your projects?" with what is read, kept, never kept and never read behind an info button; "Look for my projects" calls `finding.start` and opens `/find/scanning`, and "Skip" keeps the setup of one team as it was. Once a scan has run or runs, the card is not shown again. When it says `none`, Continue opens `/setup/where`, "Where do you use Claude?", with three choices: Claude Code on this computer (a scan, to look again), claude.ai or the Claude app (`/find/export`, 4.4) and "I'm new to Claude" (the setup of one team, `/setup/account`). While a scan runs, every page of the setup shows the strip "Still looking · N projects so far" with a link to the found list, and the scan's page asks `finding.status` every second; the owner may go on with the setup meanwhile.

### 4.2 The working loop

The user opens the app in the morning. The board shows what moved overnight. The channel shows the review and the retro of the last delivery that the Scrum Master posted (changed in 0.116; ADR 0062). Two tasks are waiting on the user: one is finished work whose pull request waits for the user to merge it (5.14; changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: no contract waits for the user's approval), the other is an escalation from the developer who hit the iteration limit on a flaky test. The escalation's row in "Waiting on you" is headed "<name> needs your help" and its "Answer" opens the task's help page at once (changed in 0.116; ADR 0062), which lists every choice the user has as a button, each with its words about what happens next, naming the agent, and the team's suggestion marked "Suggested" (5.7). One press makes the choice; no status is typed. The user reads both, merges one, and answers the developer directly from their desk. A change to the product's spec or roadmap is written at a delivery's review and lands as a folder change like any other document, with no card to approve (5.17; changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: the card "Product plan changes to approve" and the `folder_doc_decide` flow serve only the proposals an older log still holds). A new project's product plan is the Product Manager's first task, accepted by Catervas on its criteria, and comes to Today as no card (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: the card "Your product plan to approve" is gone, the plan's task being checked by Catervas and its documents reaching the owner in the pull request the task opens, 5.14); its documents are read in Files (4.5).

**Attaching documents to a request (added in 0.131; ADR 0076; standalone plan `attached-documents`).** Beside "Send" Today's request box has "Attach a document", a button that opens the computer's file picker for `.md`, `.markdown`, `.txt`, `.pdf` and `.docx` files. A picked file asks "What is it about?" with "The product (a spec or a description)", pressed first, and "The architecture", and "Attach" sends it with `document.attach` (5.17). While it is sent its chip, the file's name, is shown with a spinner and "Send" waits; when it is in, the chip stays above the box with a button "Take <name> off this message", which takes the document off the message and leaves it in the team's folder. A refusal is said under the box in plain words ("Catervas reads Markdown, text, PDF and Word files.", "This PDF has no text Catervas can read. It may be a scan.", "Catervas could not open this file.", "This file is too large. Catervas takes up to 10 MB, and up to 256 KB of text.", "No one on the team keeps these documents. Add a Product Manager or an Architect."); a sixth file is refused with "A message holds up to five documents." before any call. "Send" then calls `request.file { text, attachments }` with the chips' paths, and the box is emptied. The box's words are still needed: a request is its text, and a document alone sends nothing.

**The Catervafication's quiet card (added in 0.102; ADR 0051; phase 8 step 07b; changed in 0.117; ADR 0063).** While `catervafication.get` answers `offered`, Today shows, after the request box and outside "Waiting on you" and its count, a card with a dashed border: "Your team hasn’t documented this project yet", "A first piece of work where your team reads your project, writes down what it learns, looks for bugs and starts your marketing." and "Start", which sends `catervafication_start` as the offer does, says a refusal under the card, and asks `catervafication.get` again when it is done, so the card goes. The Files page (4.5) heads its page with the same card, across both columns. The card is not a waiting item and not part of F3's request box, which does not change. A task's history names the epic's filing: "Catervas filed it to document the project."

**The goal card (added in 0.130; ADR 0075).** Today shows one goal card, after the request box and outside "Waiting on you" and its count: it is the team's aim, not a question. With no goal it is a quiet card with a dashed border, "Give your team a goal" and "They keep working on it, day after day, within your daily budget." with **Set a goal**, and, after a goal ended, one line under it: "Reached on <date>: <words>" ("Ended on" for a dropped one). **Set a goal** opens a dialog: "What should your team achieve?" (with an info button saying the team plans towards it round after round, spends only within the daily budget, counts progress from a connected service or asks the owner, and that only the owner marks it reached), "A number to reach" and "What it counts" (both optional, filled in from the words as they are typed until the owner changes either: "Reach 10 paying customers" gives 10 and "paying customers", "10k downloads" gives 10000 and "downloads"), and, with a number, "How do we count it?": "You tell us" first, then "From <Service> (<Name> reads it)" for each connector an active agent has but the built-in ones; **Set goal** sends `goal_set`. A team with no daily budget is refused in words that link to Settings: "Set a daily budget first: a goal keeps your team working every day." With a goal the card shows the words, a bar and "4 of 10 paying customers" with "From Stripe, read by Finn 3 hours ago" or "You told us 2 days ago" ("Not counted yet" with no reading; "Reached when you say so" for a goal with no number), one line for what the team does now ("<Name> is planning the next steps", "5 tasks under way, 3 done", "Waiting on you (2)", "Paused"), and the buttons **Mark reached**, **Update the number** (with a number) and **More** (**Edit**, **Pause** or **Resume**, **End goal**); a goal read from a service nobody has connected says so. When the count reaches the target the team plans no more and the card asks "Your team counts 10 of 10 paying customers. Is the goal reached?" with **Mark reached** first. When the goal is stalled the card says why ("Five rounds of work and the count hasn't moved.", "Five rounds of work since you last checked in." for a goal with no number, or "<Name> found nothing more to plan. Tell <Name> more?") and offers **Keep going**. **Mark reached** and **End goal** each ask once. The card reads `goal.get` and sends `goal_set`, `goal_edit`, `goal_pause`, `goal_resume`, `goal_end` and `goal_report` (5.18).

**The agents open their pages (added in 0.107).** Wherever Today draws an agent's picture (the team band, a row or card waiting on the user, What moved, Going out and the channel preview), the picture is a link to that agent's page, `/team/<id>`, named by the agent's name; Catervas's mark and the user's own figure are not links. The agent's page shows the agent's picture beside its title, "<Name>, your <Role>".

**What waits, in groups (added in 0.123; standalone plan `ux-pass`).** "Waiting on you (n)" counts every row as before and shows them in up to three groups, each with its own heading and count and drawn only when it has a row: "Needs setting up" (the AI account's key, how to open the app, Docker's sandbox, the Designer's browser; changed in 0.137: while the team has a Designer and no preview, a `ready` task of the Designer's role lists "Tell Catervas how to open your app", the row `preview_missing` of `waiting.list`, linking to Settings, Your app, as the design review's does), then "Needs your answer" (questions, stuck tasks, connector calls, posts, orders, data sources, marketing plans and their budgets, document changes), then "Ready for you to merge" (finished work whose pull request waits), which shows three rows and "Show all n". A question's or a stuck task's row says "About “<task title>”" and shows at most three lines of the agent's words; the page its Answer opens shows them all. On the team band, and on the agent's card on the Team page, an agent waiting on the owner says only "Waiting on you"; every band line is at most two lines tall, the whole line in its tooltip. After "Waiting on you" come the seller mail, the renewals, the posts going out, "What moved", then "Suggested connections" (6.7). A "Ready for you to merge" row of a task has the button "I merged it", which sends `task_integrate` where it stands: with no event recorded the row says the merge is not seen yet ("GitHub doesn’t show it merged yet", or, with no `origin`, `not_merged` in words); its title opens the task's page (changed in 0.124).

**Autopilot on Today (added in 0.138; ADR 0082).** `autopilot.today` answers whether autopilot is on, what the team flagged and what it did on its own. While it is on, "Flagged by the team" comes before "Waiting on you": a row for each flagged task, folder change and stalled goal, with its title, what only the owner can give, when and who flagged it (an agent, or Catervas). "Done on its own" lists the last seven days' autopilot acts, each with its agent and reason: questions the team answered, decisions, plans and results it approved or accepted, approved spend, messages sent and merges. While the team decides, "Waiting on you" lists no question, escalation, block, approval or acceptance, and no data source, that the Product Manager takes; turned off, they wait on the owner again. Settings, Allowed actions, holds the switch with its confirmation (5.12).

**A question in one press (added in 0.123).** A task's question page shows the agent's question in its own paragraphs and each answer the agent suggests as a button that sends that answer at once, its hint under it; "Or answer in your own words" has its own box and "Send answer"; "Let <Name> decide" sends the agent's call. Why a question is no problem sits behind the info button beside the title.

### 4.3 Asking an agent a question

Clicking on an agent opens a one-on-one. This conversation is outside the task system: the agent answers using its memory and read access to the project but cannot change anything. As built (changed in 0.34; ADR 0026), the user opens "Chats" on the rail and picks the agent (F8). The agent answers by itself: each message of the user's gets one `chat` session of that agent (8.2), which the governor, not the prompt, holds to the read tier, and whose one write is its reply. A chat answers at once, beside the agent's work (5.9; added in 0.118; ADR 0064). The chat session asks for the reply in Markdown: a summary of one or two sentences, then the points as a bulleted list, then a one-line conclusion (a greeting or a one-line answer needs no list), and to name a file or a folder in plain words, never by its path (added in 0.107); the prompt holds this, not code. If the conversation produces something actionable, the reply carries a proposed request, a title and a text, and nothing is filed until the user presses "Send as a request", which files the words, edited or not, as the user's own request, triaged and contracted like anything else (5.16); the agent files no request itself (changed in 0.117; ADR 0063: it may take work its role does as its own task, and the owner may give it a task, below). A chat is answered while the team is paused and while its agent is paused (4.4); it waits while the day's budget is spent (5.5), while its agent sleeps at its provider's limit, and while the provider refuses the key, and the chat says why. Nothing said in a chat reaches the channel or another agent (5.9).

**A task from a chat (added in 0.117; ADR 0063; standalone plan `catervafication-work`).** Beside "Send" the one-to-one's box has "Send as a task", with an info button saying that the agent turns the message into a task, plans it and starts on it, and that changes to code are still checked before they reach the owner. It sends the same command, `chat_message_post { agent_id, text, as_task: true }` (`as_task` is optional and written only when true), and the message is recorded as `chat_message.posted { as_task: true }`. No chat session answers such a message, so the chat shows no "thinking" for it and no session proposes the same work again. It is refused, in this order and with nothing recorded, with `agent_not_active` for an agent that is not active ("<Name> is paused; resume them on the Team page to give them a task") and with `task_too_short` for a text under 20 characters, once trimmed ("say a little more: at least 20 characters"), after the checks that the agent is on the team and has not retired. Otherwise the same command files a request given to that agent, in this order: the message; `task.created { created_by: human, from_chat_message: <that message>, given_to: <agent> }`; and `request.triaged { small, reason: "a task the owner gave <agent> in their chat", triaged_by: catervas }`. The contract is `request_from_text` of the message, so the message is its intent, with the agent's role as its `assignee_role` and the usual reviewer role (`reviewer_for`); the answer is "given to <Name> as <id>". The store refuses a link to any message that is not the owner's own in that agent's chat (the message may be a plain one), a contract whose intent is not that message's text, and a message already made a task ("was already sent, as <id>"), so a given task's work is only ever the owner's words, whoever files it. The chat shows under the message "Given to <Name> as <id>", linked to the task. The refusals are said in words, "This teammate is paused. Resume them on the Team page to give them a task." and "Say a little more: a task needs at least 20 characters."

**Attaching documents in a chat (added in 0.131; ADR 0076; standalone plan `attached-documents`).** A one-to-one chat's box has the same "Attach a document" and chips as Today's (4.2). "Send" calls `chat_message_post { agent_id, text, attachments }`; "Send as a task" sends `as_task: true` with them, and the task it files records the same `attachments` on its `task.created`, so its sessions read them as a request's do. A sent message shows its documents under its words as chips, each a link to the document's page on Files (`/files/<path>`), named by the file the owner attached, from `chat.messages`' `attachments` (5.17). The Product Manager's interview of a new project (below) lists the documents attached at setup, and its chat session reads them like any chat session (5.17).

The chat session decides as well (added in 0.117; ADR 0063). A request for work its role does it takes with `catervas_take_task { text }`, offered in a chat session alone, which files the same given task from the message the session answers (`in_reply_to`), created by the agent. `text` is only the task's title, one line of 3 to 80 characters; the intent is read from that message in the log, never from the agent's words, so nothing the session read elsewhere (a file, a task, a seller's reply) can become the work. The session then replies in one line naming the task. A question it answers, and work for another role it proposes as a request in its reply, for the owner to send. The tool's refusals, checked in this order with nothing recorded, are `take_task_refused` (not a chat session, or no message answered), `agent_not_active` (a paused agent's chat still runs, but it takes no work), `task_title`, `task_too_short` (the message is under 20 characters) and `already_a_task: <id>` (after "Send as a task" or a second call); its answer is `{ task_id, next }`. The chat stays otherwise read-only: it writes nothing in the project and moves no task. Answering quickly beside the agent's current work is ADR 0064's, not built here; until it lands, the chat is answered at the start of a tick as before.

**A new project's interview (added in 0.99; ADR 0051; phase 8 step 06).** While the product plan's task of a project started in Catervas is not accepted (5.3; changed in 0.115; ADR 0061), its Product Manager's chat is an interview. Once setup ends and the team runs, not while it is paused, setup's pause included, a Product Manager whose chat holds no message and that never started a `chat` session, awake and on a day whose budget has room, gets one `chat` session with no `in_reply_to`, whose first message is "<Name>, the owner has just started this project. Open your interview in your one-to-one chat: greet them and ask your first question."; a session that ends without a reply is not tried again, and the owner can write first. Every chat session of that Product Manager is given `INTERVIEW_INSTRUCTION` as its closing, in place of the chat's, and as its human's message what the owner wrote when they started the project, then the chat so far, the owner's lines as their own and its own inside an `untrusted` block, its older messages dropped first to fit 16 KiB, the paragraph and the newest message always kept. Its replies too name a file or a folder in plain words, never by its path (added in 0.107). It finds out, one question at a time and only what the chat has not answered, who the customers are, the problem, what the product must do, what is out for now, any constraints and how the owner will know it works; when it knows enough, or the owner asks, it sums up in `heard` and says they can correct it or have it draft the plan. It puts no request in its reply, and the chat stays read-only on the read tier. `catervas_chat_reply` takes `heard { customers, problem, must, not_now, works_when }`, each part 1 to 1,000 characters, counted in code points, not blank, with line breaks kept; any agent may send one, a blank part is refused with `blank_heard` and a long one with `heard_out_of_bounds`, and later sessions are shown it after the reply's text as "What I heard:" with the labels "Your customers", "The problem", "It must", "Not now" and "It works when". The owner's word `product_plan_draft {}` files the task that drafts the plan (5.16). It is refused, in this order, with `not_a_new_project`, `product_plan_approved`, `product_plan_open` (a product plan task that is not `cancelled`, and not `accepted`), `product_plan_no_writer` (no active Product Manager) and `product_plan_no_reviewer` (no active Architect or Scrum Master to check the plan before the owner reads it; it cannot occur since 0.103, a lone Product Manager reviewing its plan itself); two presses at once file one task. The query `product_plan.state {}` answers `{ new_project: { name } | null, approved, task: { task_id, status, created_at } | null, documents: [{ path, text }] }`: `task` is the newest product plan task that still drafts the plan, and `documents` the two documents as its branch has them while it is `verifying`.

**The interview lists attached documents (added in 0.131; ADR 0076; standalone plan `attached-documents`).** When the log holds a `document.attached` (8.5), the first paragraph of the interview text a chat session is given, the owner's own words from when they started the project, ends with a line "They attached: <path>, <path>.", every attached document's path in the order they were attached, whether or not they were attached at setup; no line when there is none.

**The interview in the web app (added in 0.100; ADR 0051; phase 8 step 06b).** While the project is new and its plan not approved, the Product Manager's chat says under its title "Before your team builds anything, <Name> asks what you want to make. This chat only talks: your product plan is written next, and your team builds once it is done (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: you no longer approve it first)." in place of the usual line, on a phone too; every other chat, and this one once the plan is approved, keeps the usual line, and no other chat asks `product_plan.state`. A reply whose `heard` is not null shows under its text a section "What I heard" with "Your customers", "The problem", "It must", "Not now" and "It works when" and the five parts as text with their line breaks, whichever agent sent it. While interviewing, the Product Manager's newest message ends with "Draft the product plan" and "I write it as my first task: a product description and a roadmap. It comes to you on Today to approve.", inside its "What I heard" when it has one and under its text when it has not, so a summary the model never sent cannot strand the owner. Pressing it sends `product_plan_draft {}`; once the state names the task, the place says "Drafting it as <id>. It comes to you on Today to approve." in place of the button. A refusal is said in words under the button: "This project was not started here, so it has no product plan to draft." (`not_a_new_project`); "Your product plan is approved already." (`product_plan_approved`); "<Name> is drafting your product plan already." (`product_plan_open`); "Your team has no Product Manager at work to write it." (`product_plan_no_writer`); "An Architect or a Scrum Master checks the plan before you read it. Add one on the Team page." (`product_plan_no_reviewer`).

### 4.4 Changing the team

The user can pause, retire, or replace an agent at any time. Retiring an agent keeps its memory in the project so a successor can read it. Replacing an agent retires it and adds its successor in one change to the team file, checked as a whole, so a team is never left for a moment without a role it needs; pausing or retiring the last active agent of a role the team needs, or of the role it named to check plans, is refused in words that say what to do first (added in 0.26). Changing a role's permissions takes effect on the next session that agent starts, never mid-session (changed in 0.26: a session is held to the tiers it started with, whatever the team's file says by then; whether an agent is paused or retired is still read on every call, so pausing stops it at once). A paused agent still answers its one-to-one chat: a `chat` session is the one whose calls a paused agent may make (8.2), and a retired agent's chat is read-only. Pausing an agent aborts every session it is running except a chat session under way, which runs to its end and answers its message, since a paused agent still answers its chats; retiring an agent aborts that too (F8; added in 0.34; changed in 0.37). Retiring an agent blocks each task it holds `in_progress` or `assigned`, with the blocker "agent retired by the user", so the user sees it and no task waits on an agent that will not start it; pausing blocks only its `in_progress` tasks, since a resumed agent starts what it was assigned (changed in 0.37). After setup, the answers setup asked for (what agents may do, the daily spending limit, how finished work is added, and how plans are checked) are changed from Settings, each part on its own, with its effect shown before Save and "Put back the default" beside it; a change starts with each agent's next session (added in 0.27). Settings has no "Planning work" part (changed in 0.116; ADR 0062).

**An added agent's defaults (added in 0.122; ADR 0069).** When the Team page saves an agent that the saved team does not have yet and it comes with no persona (missing or blank), it gets its role's shipped persona, and a UI/UX Designer that comes with no connectors gets the built-in browser (`playwright`), as the suggested team's agents have them. An agent already saved is never touched, so a persona the owner cleared stays cleared.

The Team page saves the team as a template and uses a saved one (added in 0.35). "Save as a template" asks for a name and saves what section 3 says a template holds; a name a saved team already has, by its slug, is refused with `template_exists` and the words "A saved team is called <name> already. Replace it, or choose another name.", and Replace saves over it. Saving records no event. A save or a rename to the name of a ready-made team, by its slug, is refused with `template_builtin` at `/name` and the words "Catervas comes with a team called <name>. Choose another name.", whatever Replace says (added in 0.103). The list answers `builtin`, the three ready-made teams, and a `folder` that is null when Catervas has no state folder, where it no longer refuses `no_state_folder`; a saved file whose slug is a ready-made team's is listed as unreadable, so Settings offers to delete it, and a preview or use by that slug reaches the ready-made team (added in 0.103). "Use a saved team" lists the ready-made teams under "Ready-made", above the saved teams under "Saved teams", with one selection across both (changed in 0.103), then shows what using one would do before anything is saved: who stays, who joins, who is retired and who is removed, each with face, name and role, and the change in words under "What changes": first, for each agent retired, the unfinished (`in_progress` or `assigned`, changed in 0.37) task its retirement puts on hold, by id and title ("Sol is retired. Sol's unfinished task, T-18 “Fix the sign-in page”, is put on hold until you give it to someone."), then each agent who stays and whose model or effort changes, in the words the Team cards use ("Kai's model changes from the strongest model to the everyday model.", "Kai now works carefully."; never a model id, unless no family Catervas names the model), words `catervas-core` keeps so that this preview, Settings and `team.validate` say the same, then the team's answers (added in the 0.35 fix wave); "Use this team" applies it and the Team page reads the team again at once, not on the next event, so "Add someone" and the cards act on the team as written, giving the digest of the template file its preview read, so a template whose file changed since (Replace from another tab, say, or an edit by hand) is refused with `template_changed` and the words "This saved team was saved again since you looked at it. Go back and look at what changes once more.", and its answers are applied only as a preview showed them; going back and looking again shows the file as it is now and gives its digest, so using it then applies (added in the 0.35 fix wave). The rules, which `apply_template` in `catervas-core` works out with no I/O:

- **Stays**: an agent of the template whose id and role match a project agent that is not retired. It takes the template's name, and its persona, picture and model where the template has them, and keeps its status, grants, revokes and connectors, its work and its chats; a paused match stays paused.
- **Retired**: every other agent that is not retired and has worked, meaning the log holds an event that names it, a one-to-one chat with it among them (8.5), or a task names it as its assignee or reviewer, so no task is left with nobody (changed in 0.37). The same rule decides whether saving the team may drop an agent or must retire it. Its retirement has the effects a retirement from its card has (F1).
- **Removed**: every other agent that never worked, taken off the team file. A removed agent's id is free, so a joining agent may take it.
- **Joins**: every template agent that does not stay, active, with no grants or revokes, and its role's suggested persona, picture, model and connectors where the template has none (the UI/UX Designer its browser connector, 5.6). Its id takes `-2`, `-3`… when an agent left on the team holds it, cut short to stay within 64 characters.
- The team takes the template's permissions, how finished work is added, and daily limit (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: no plan check), none clearing the project's (changed in 0.116; ADR 0062: a template's older answer about planning is read and ignored); everything else, the rules among it, is the project's. Agents already retired are left as they are.

The result is held to the team's rules (F1). It can fail where a match that stays is paused: a project with two Product Managers, one paused and one active, and a template whose Product Manager is the paused one, leaves the team with no active Product Manager once the active one is retired (changed in 0.103; the example was a paused Developer). The preview then shows why in words, naming the paused agent and saying to resume it first or choose another team, and "Use this team" cannot be pressed. Using a template works the result out again rather than taking the preview's, under the one lock that every write of the team file in a daemon holds from its read to its write (`team.save`, `team.start`, a status change from a card, `agent.replace`, connecting and disconnecting a connector (changed in 0.38), and using a template), so what is written is checked against the team it replaces, `agent.replace`'s newcomer among it; a result refused then writes nothing and is answered as a refusal (-32005) with the team's errors. It writes the team file once, then records each retirement's effects in order, then one `team.updated` naming the template (8.5). Settings has "Saved teams": each saved team with its faces, renamed in place or deleted after "Delete it" ("Keep it" keeps it); a file that is not a template is listed with Delete alone and the words "This saved team cannot be read. Delete it, or fix the file by hand."; and the folder they are kept in is named. A ready-made team is not listed there, and cannot be renamed or deleted (added in 0.103). Renaming keeps when the team was saved and moves the file to the new name's slug, refused when another saved team holds it; deleting removes the file; neither records an event, and neither changes a project's team.

Change project (added in 0.83, ADR 0053). Settings, "This computer" (`/settings/computer`), has "Change project…" under the project folder, (changed in 0.145; ADR 0059: the rail's foot no longer names the project or offers "Change", since the team switcher names the team there, and the phone's top bar shows the switcher in the same place). Confirming "The team stops working on <old>. Its work there is kept, and it is all there if you come back." calls `project.leave`, which stops the team as `catervas stop` does and returns the page to the project page (4.1). Choosing there moves the team to the new project in the same `catervas serve`; with several teams (changed in 0.144; ADR 0059) "Change project" stops and removes the team it is asked on, and the others go on, and the wizard is served on its own only when the last team has left. The old project is left as it is, and choosing it again drives it as it was.

Several teams in the web app (added in 0.145; ADR 0059; phase 10 step 05b). The browser holds two connections: the hub's, `/hub/rpc`, open for as long as the session lives, which answers `teams.list`, `computer.get`, `computer.set`, `teams.current`, `teams.remove` and the wizard's first steps (the computer, the AI account, the project), and the socket of the team in the address, `/t/<team>/rpc`, which is closed and replaced when the address changes team; the wizard's later steps (the scan, the team, the checks, the spending, the finish and the offer to document the project) talk to the current team through `/rpc`. Each team's pages are under `/t/<team>/` with the paths they had (`/t/<team>/board`, `/t/<team>/tasks/<id>`, `/t/<team>/settings/work`, and so on), and its documents come from `/t/<team>/documents/raw`. An address with no team (`/board`, a bookmark, `/` after setup) goes to the same page of the team viewed last, which the browser keeps in `localStorage` as `catervas.lastTeam`, when that is still one of the teams, else to the only team when there is one, else, with two or more and none remembered, to All teams; a project the wizard has just taken on opens at once, since it is the current team. With no team and no project chosen the first run starts at `/setup/computer` as before. The rail's top is a switcher, a button named for the team in the address ("All teams" on All teams and This computer) that opens a menu labelled "Teams": "All teams", one item for each team with a second line ("N waiting", "working", "paused", "driven from a terminal", "can't be found" or "stopped:" and the first 40 characters of its sentence) and "Add a team", which goes to the wizard's project step. Choosing a team calls `teams.current` on the hub, so that `/rpc` and `catervas open` follow the owner, and opens the same page of that team, or its Today from a page that names the old team's task, request, document, agent or chat. A team that is gone or not driven here shows a notice with a link to All teams. All teams (`/teams`) has a card for each team in `teams.list`'s order: its name (a link to its Today), a badge ("N waiting on you", "Working", "Paused", "Driven from a terminal", "Can't be found" or "Stopped" with its sentence beneath), how many agents are working, and what it spent today and this month; a paused team has "Start", which sends `team_resume` to it on a short-lived socket of its own, and a team that cannot be found has "Remove", which asks "Remove <name> from Catervas? Its folder isn't touched." before it sends `teams.remove` with `confirmed`. Below the cards "Waiting on you" lists each team that has something waiting, and a line says when the AI account's limit resets while the teams wait for it. This computer (`/computer`) sets "Agents working at once" ("No limit", or 1 to 16) and "Daily limit for this computer" (empty for none) with `computer.set`, and shows what all the teams spent today; the daemon's refusals are said in plain words. All teams is asked again after a hub event and every 10 seconds.

Finding projects behind the hub (added in 0.146; ADR 0059; phase 10 step 06). The hub's socket, `/hub/rpc`, answers the methods the finding screens call, all about the computer and none about a team: `finding.offer {}` answers `{ history, sessions_dir_exists }`; `finding.start {}` answers `{ started }` (false, with nothing done, while a scan runs); `finding.stop {}`; `finding.status {}` answers the phase (`idle`, `running`, `stopped`, `done`), the live counts (`files_total`, `files_read`, `sessions`, `projects`, `jobs`, `reading`, `unreadable`), `seconds_left` (only after 20 files, the files left at the mean time per file so far), `error`, the times, `paused`, `index_exists`, `export_dismissed` and a `version` that counts the publications; `finding.list {}` answers the found list in sections `main` (newest first), `explored`, `gone`, `home` (how many sessions ran at home and the connector projects they formed), `computer_jobs` and `ignored`, each row `{ key, name, kind, folders, last_at, jobs, services, suggested, choice, already_team, gone }` with `kind` one of `folder`, `connector`, `claude_ai`, `hand` or `job`, and `already_team` the slug of the team whose project folder is one of its folders; `finding.ignored {}` answers the ignored rows alone, and choosing Team or Watch for one brings it back; `finding.choose { key, choice }`; `finding.separate { key, folder }` ("These are different"); `finding.locate { key, path }` for a gone folder; `finding.declare_services { ids, other? }`; `finding.add_project { name, folder?, repository? }`; `finding.add_routine { name, project_key?, schedule }` with a schedule of at most 100 characters of free text; `finding.retention {}` answers `{ cleanup_period_days, default }` as Claude Code's settings say (30 when absent); `finding.keep_longer { days }` with 90, 365 or 3650; `finding.pause { paused }`, while which no scan starts, one that runs ends and the daily rescan stops; `finding.export_dismissed {}`; and `finding.forget { confirmed }`, which stops a scan that runs, deletes `machine.db`, clears `export_card` and sets `finding_paused`, so finding is paused after it ("Finding projects pauses."). Its refusals are `finding_paused` ("finding is paused: turn it on in This computer"), `unknown_project` ("Catervas doesn't know that project"), `not_gone` ("that project's folder is still there"), the member path refusals of `repo.add` for a Locate path, `not_the_same_repository` ("that folder holds another repository"), `unknown_service`, `cannot_add`, `retention_not_offered` ("Catervas keeps Claude Code's history for 90 days, a year or ten years") and `forget_needs_confirming` ("say yes to forget everything Catervas found"). `POST /hub/export` takes claude.ai's export as the request body and answers the summary `{ conversations, new_conversations, projects, new_projects, skipped, skipped_projects, content_at }`, or `{ error, message }` with `not_an_export`, `damaged`, `unsupported`, `encrypted`, `nothing_dated` (422) or `export_too_large` (413); a dismissed export card is `finding.export_dismissed`, and a drop clears it. The screens are the next step's.

The finding pages (added in 0.147; ADR 0059; phase 10 step 06c). The hub also answers `finding.catalog {}`, the services the owner can tap, `{ services: [{ id, name, kind }] }` in the catalog's order (`kind` is bookkeeping, spreadsheets, payments, selling, marketing, code or other). The pages of finding talk to the hub's socket and have no rail, as the setup's: `/find/scanning` shows the three counts (projects, scheduled jobs, sessions), the time left once `finding.status` gives it, what is being read, "Continue setup meanwhile" (to All teams when the owner came from there) and "Stop", and when the scan is done "Here's what we found." with "See what you work on", and "Couldn't read N sessions" with its three bullets and no update button when `unreadable` is above 0. `/find/found`, "Here's what you work on", lists a row for each `main` project: its name, "N folders" with an info button saying they are the same GitHub repository and "These are different" (`finding.separate`), a badge of its jobs, when it was last worked on and the services used through Claude, and Team, Watch or Ignore with the suggested one already chosen (`finding.choose`); a project found through Claude's connectors says it is not a folder and where a team for it would live (`~/Catervas/<name>`), a claude.ai Project or a job is Watch or Ignore only, and a project that already has a team says "Already a team" with its name. "Explored", "No longer on this computer" (each with Locate…, a folder picker calling `finding.locate`, and "Not mine"), "Your home folder" and "Jobs on this computer" open on a click. With nothing found it says "We didn't find any projects" and offers "I use claude.ai", "Set up one team" and "Add a project by hand" (`finding.add_project`). Continue goes to All teams until the page that asks whether projects work together exists. `/find/export` takes claude.ai's export dropped on the page or chosen as a file, posts it as the body of `POST /hub/export` and says "N conversations and M Projects brought in", or why it was not read ("That isn't a claude.ai export" with the help for a link that expired, a damaged, newer, locked, undated or too large file); "I'll do it later" keeps `catervas.exportPending` in the browser and a card, "Waiting for your claude.ai export" with "Choose file…" and "Dismiss" (`finding.export_dismissed`), waits on All teams and on the found list until a file is brought in or dismissed. `/find/services` shows a tile for each service of `finding.catalog` to tap and "Something else" to type a name, and Continue calls `finding.declare_services` and opens the found list. All teams shows, above the cards, "Find your other projects" while the index is empty and finding is not paused ("Not now" is kept in the browser), "We stopped looking halfway" with "Keep looking" after a scan that was stopped, and "N new projects found" for the projects worked on since the owner last opened the found list that have no answer and no team. This computer gains "Finding projects": a switch for the daily look (`finding.pause`) with when it last looked, "Scan now", the ignored with "Bring back…" as a team or a watch, "Keep a year of history?" while Claude Code keeps its default (`finding.keep_longer { days: 365 }`) and "Forget everything…", which asks once and then calls `finding.forget { confirmed: true }`.
GitHub for an owner who uses Claude on the web (added in 0.148; ADR 0059, ADR 0044; phase 10 step 06d). The owner connects GitHub once for the computer, with a fine-grained, read-only token they paste (Contents, Metadata, Pull requests, Actions and Deployments read), until Catervas Cloud's single click. `github.connect { token }` checks it with GitHub's `GET /user`, keeps it, reads the owner's repositories and answers `{ login }`; a token GitHub does not accept is refused with -32005 and `github_token_refused`, a spent limit with `github_rate_limited` (with when it resets), an unreachable GitHub with `github_unreachable`, and a computer with no place to keep it with `no_secret_store`, and a refusal holds no part of the token, as the schema's errors for this method are not quoted either. `github.status {}` answers `{ connected, login? }` and `github.disconnect {}` deletes the token. The client speaks only to `https://api.github.com`, with `Accept: application/vnd.github+json`, `X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28`, a 15-second timeout, no proxy and no redirect; it reads the first hundred repositories pushed to in the last 90 days that the owner owns or collaborates on, and for each its branches named `claude/…` and its open pull requests from such branches (title, number, draft, when it changed), and nothing else of GitHub's answers. It reads once after `github.connect`, in every scan when connected, and at the daily rescan; a repository a later read does not list is kept and marked not seen lately. `finding.list` rows gain `claude_work`, `[{ kind: "branch" | "pull", name, number?, draft? }]`, and a repository that is on this computer (a found folder or a project added by hand with its remote) is that project, not a second one; one that is not is a row of `kind: "github"`, with `github: { full_name, private, default_branch, pushed_at, not_seen_lately }`, suggested Watch, which offers Watch or Ignore and **Copy to this computer**. `github.copy { full_name, parent, name? }` clones `https://github.com/<full_name>.git` into `~/<parent>/<name>` (the name is the repository's, lowercase, unless given; `parent` and the name are held to the rules of `project.create`: inside home, a name that is not taken, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens), gives git the token through the environment alone (`GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1`, `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=http.https://github.com/.extraheader`, `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=AUTHORIZATION: bearer <token>`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`), adds the folder as a project by hand with the repository's address, starts a scan unless finding is paused, and answers `{ folder }`; it is refused with `github_not_connected`, `unknown_repository`, `outside_home`, `bad_name`, `folder_taken`, or `copy_failed` with git's last line, the token cut out of it. The page `/find/github` ("Connect GitHub", "2 of 3 · optional", between `/find/export` and `/find/services`; "I'll do it later" and Next on the export page both lead to it) has the three bullets of its mockup, a token field with the link "Make a token on GitHub" (`https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens/new`), **Connect GitHub** and **Skip**, and after connecting says "Connected as <login>." and offers Next. On "Here's what you work on" a `github` row says "On GitHub, not on this computer", when it was pushed and, for example, "2 branches from Claude on the web · 1 pull request (draft)"; **Copy to this computer** opens a dialog with the folder browser for the parent and then says "Copied to ~/…". This computer gains "GitHub: connected as <login>" with **Disconnect**, or **Connect GitHub**.

Linking with proof (added in 0.149; ADR 0059; phase 10 step 06b). The hub answers four methods over the projects the owner chose as teams (the choice made, else the suggestion the found list showed) and the teams already driven, apart from a folder that is gone. `linking.pairs {}` reads their committed files again and answers `{ pairs }`: every pair with a proof that holds now and no answer, the pairs with a `shared_work` proof before the others (added in 0.154), and every pair answered No for which a proof of a kind that was not among the proofs shown with that No is now found, a pair touching a project already asked about following the pair that reached it, and never a pair whose two projects are already one group through other Yes answers. Each is `{ a, b, proof, also, hints }`: `a` and `b` are `{ key, name, last_at, folder }` (the folder with the home folder written `~`), `proof` is `{ kind, a, b, sentence, ends }` with one to four `ends`, each `{ project, name, file, line, text }` (the line, trimmed to 160 characters; a `shared_work` proof's ends are its sessions, newest first, up to three and then "and N more", each with the session's id as `file`, `line` 0 and its title and day as `text`), `also` the sentences of the pair's other proofs (the `shared_work` proof is shown first, the file proofs under it), and `hints` the hints besides, from `same_owner`, `same_days`, `similar_names` and `wrote_both`. `linking.maybe {}` answers `{ maybe }`, the pairs with hints only and no answer, each `{ a, b, hints }`. `linking.groups {}` answers `{ groups }`, the connected groups of the Yes answers alone, each `{ projects, names, why }`, `why` the sentence of each Yes and then of any other proof among the group's projects; a Yes whose proofs no longer hold, found again with the same kind in the same files, joins nothing. `linking.answer { a, b, answer, from_maybe? }` keeps the owner's answer, `yes` or `no`, for the pair in either order, with the proofs shown; a Yes needs a proof that holds now, found again from the files, else -32005 and `proof_no_longer_holds` (a `shared_work` proof holds while two sessions still changed files under both, and a Yes or a No kept with it is not asked again for more sessions), except that `from_maybe`, sent by the choice "One team" on a pair of the Maybe list, keeps a Yes for a pair with hints and no proof; an unknown key is -32005 and `unknown_project`. A link with a team already driven is the same Yes; adding the project to that team is step 06e. `/find/together`, "Do these work together?" (step 2 of 3), asks one pair at a time, "Question n of N" counting the pairs asked and still to ask, with the two projects (last worked on and folder), the proof in one plain sentence, an info button listing each end as `<project>/<file>, line <n>: <text>` and "Checked again just now." (for shared work the heading reads "These look like one team" and the button lists each session as its title and day, with no file or line, and **Yes, one team** comes first and has focus), "Also: …" for each other proof and each hint, **Yes, one team**, **No, keep separate** and "Not sure? Keep them separate. You can change it later." After the last pair, or at once when there is none, it says "That's all we could prove", one line for each group ("a, b and c: one team."), "Everything else stays separate." and "Maybe related (n)", collapsed, each pair there with its hints in words and **Separate** (chosen) or **One team**; **Back** goes to the found list, and **Continue** to All teams until the proposal of teams exists. "Here's what you work on" now leads on to this page.

The proposal and creating teams (added in 0.150; ADR 0059, ADR 0055, ADR 0057; phase 10 step 06e). After "Do these work together?" the hub answers `proposal.get` with a card for each group of linked projects that has a project chosen as a team and no driven team, for each project chosen as a team in no group, and, as an "Add to <team>" card, for each such project linked to a project of a team that is driven; a project that is a member of a project folder, or was made a team from the proposal, counts as that team's. A card is `{ id, kind, projects, jobs, why, name, purpose?, template, folder?, from_claude, team?, team_name? }` with `id` a hash of the sorted keys of its group, so it is the same on every call; the name is the first project's folder name, or "Bookkeeping" for a bookkeeping connector project, whose folder is `~/Catervas/<name>`; the template suggested is `financial-analysis` for a bookkeeping connector project and `software-product` for any other; and cards go by the newest work first. `proposal.get` also answers `templates`, the ready-made teams and the owner's saved ones. `proposal.edit { id, name?, template?, purpose? }` keeps the owner's change in `machine.db` (a template that is neither is refused `template_unknown`), `proposal.move_out { id, key }` makes the project a card of its own and keeps No between it and each project that stays, `proposal.revert { id }` forgets a card's edits (Keep the folder name), and `linking.reject { key, others }` keeps No between a project and others without asking for a proof. `/find/teams`, "Your teams" (step 3 of 3), shows "Check each one. Change anything.", then "Better names?" with what Claude sees and **Suggest names with Claude (about $0.02)**, the estimate from `proposal.names_estimate` (the prompt's length in characters over four as input tokens, and 400 output tokens, at the price table's Haiku rates), then one card for each team with its name and Rename, its projects as tags, why they are together with a button that says they are checked again, "Jobs: ...", the **Team** select, **Move a project out** for a card of several projects, and for work done through connectors "New folder: ~/Catervas/bookkeeping"; "Watched, no team: ..." for the projects chosen to be watched; and Back, "They start paused. Nothing is spent until you start one." and **Create N teams**. After the names, "Names from Claude · cost $0.02" says the cost once, and each card changed by Claude shows **Keep the folder name**. `proposal.create { confirmed: true, ids?, only? }` is refused `confirmation_needed` without `confirmed`; it makes the cards `proposal.get` last showed (`ids` names others, `only` makes the cards whose projects are all among the keys given), each alone, and answers `{ made, added, failed, split }`. It reads the proofs of every link again first: a card whose proof no longer holds is not made and is told in `split`, its projects being cards of their own the next time. A team of one folder is made where the folder is: `catervas init` there, the team paused with the setup marker, the template applied, the team named as the card says, and the marker removed, so that nothing starts; a team of several repositories is a project folder at `~/Catervas/<name>` made as `project.create_folder` makes one; a team of work done through connectors is a new git repository at `~/Catervas/<name>` with a README and one commit of Catervas's, made the same way. The team is driven at once, paused, and `state.json` remembers it. A card that fails stops only itself and is told in `failed` with a reason that begins with its code (`has_team`, `no_folder`, `mixed_projects`, `conversion_not_available`, `team_did_not_start`). An "Add to <team>" card adds each project to the team through `repo.add`; a team of one repository cannot take a second until phase 9's conversion exists, and the card is refused `conversion_not_available`. All teams then shows "N teams created. They're paused until you start them."; a team made from the proposal whose log has no `session.started` has `undoable: true` in `teams.list` and shows **Start**, **Document it first** (the documenting offer, `catervafication_start` on the team's socket) and **Undo**. `teams.undo { slug }` stops the team's drive, removes it from the hub and `state.json`, and deletes what Catervas made for it, the `.catervas` folder it made in the owner's folder, or the project folder or new folder it made, but only when the git log of that folder holds commits of Catervas's own and nothing is changed beside `.catervas`; otherwise it removes the team and answers `left`, "Catervas left <folder>: it has changes of yours." The projects go back to the proposal. After the first session it is refused `team_has_started`, and a slug Catervas did not make `team_unknown`. Below the cards All teams lists the projects chosen to be watched, each with **Not mine** (ignore) and **Make a team** (Team, then `/find/teams`). In a team's Settings, **Repositories** lists the project folder's members (`repos.list`), and **This doesn't belong here** asks "Take <repository> out of <team>?", with **Watch it** chosen or **Make it its own team**: **Take it out** sends `repo.remove`, keeps No between the repository and each that stays with `linking.reject`, and chooses Watch, or Team and creates that one project's team.

What is carried is the team as the user left it: `team.yaml` with retired agents dropped and every other agent active (names, roles, personas, pictures, models, grants, connectors, pinned skills, policy, budgets), the uploaded pictures under `.catervas/team/avatars/`, the sandbox setting, and the pinned skills' folders, each skill asking to be confirmed again in the new project because a confirmation is recorded in the project's own log. The criteria are not carried: the new repository keeps the checks its own `init` scan found (the founder, 2026-10-09). Nor are memory, the channel and its summary, one-to-one chats, tasks, contracts, decisions, the retro, sessions, costs or worktrees: the new project starts with its own log.

Each kept agent's connector keys are copied under the new project's id (8.6), an OAuth sign-in among them, and the Procurement Specialist's mailbox moves whole, with its settings and its read position, so it stays connected with the same address and does not read old mail again. The old project keeps its own. A service that rotates its refresh token on use may ask the other project to sign in again after one of them refreshes. When at least one key was copied, the shell shows a notice, on every page, under the paused banner's place: "Your agents' connections were copied from <old> (N services). Use different keys for this project?", with "Keep them" and "Choose different keys" (to the Team page, where each agent's page connects a service again). The notice stays, across pages and reloads, until one is chosen; `keys_copied.dismiss` removes it.

**One agent alone (added in 0.125; ADR 0071).** A project may have one agent instead of a team: setup's "One agent" card, a team file whose `policy.solo` is true. It holds exactly one agent that is not retired, of any role but the Scrum Master and the UI/UX Designer (`validate_team`: `solo_one_agent`, `solo_role`); no Product Manager is required. It works outside every team function:

**Documents kept on this computer (added in 0.129; ADR 0074).** The last screen's "Show advanced settings" has a group "Documents" with one switch, "Keep documents on this computer", off, with the same three bullets behind its info button as Settings (5.12), and no dialog: nothing is committed yet that a dialog would warn about. `team.start` carries the choice as `policy.documents_local` and runs `documents.set_local { local: true }` (5.17) once the team is written, its refusals coming first, at `/team/policy/documents_local`; an existing repository's committed documents are taken out by the same pull request (5.14). A project folder has no switch.
- The owner's request (`request.file`, Today's box, which then says "What should <name> do next?") is filed as a task given to the agent, as "Send as a task" files one (ADR 0063, 5.2): triaged small, the agent writes its own contract, and Catervas assigns it to the agent with no assigner.
- No agent reviews it: readiness's reviewer rules do not apply, and Catervas verifies the contract's criteria alone and accepts it (5.4); the pull request Catervas opens is the owner's review, and Catervas never merges.
- Epics, deliveries and their review and retro, the product plan's interview and wait, the Catervafication and the document refresh do not run.
- Pausing the agent is allowed and retiring it is refused. The Team page shows its card and editor without "Add someone" or the template buttons; a team is made from it by a new setup or "Use a saved team" from a project that has one.

The daily reminder (added in 0.151; ADR 0059; phase 10 step 07). Once a day, at `reminder_time` (`HH:MM` in the computer's local time zone, 9:00 when it is not set), `catervas serve` computes a digest of what needs the owner and keeps it in memory; `reminders.get` answers it, computing one at once when there is none yet. The rules are `catervas_core::reminders`, a pure function over the facts the store, GitHub and the teams give it, and an item's `key` is `<rule>:<thing key>`, the same from one day to the next. Its groups, in order: `forgotten`, a session of the owner's whose last activity was 1 to 14 whole days ago and that left something undone (a last `TodoWrite` with items not completed, uncommitted changes, unpushed commits, a draft pull request Claude made quiet for 3 days, or a background job waiting for input), worded "<title> · <project>" under "<n> days ago · <reasons>"; `ending`, a session cron that ends within 24 hours ("ends tomorrow") or ended within 7 days while recurring ("ended"), named by its schedule because its prompt is never read; `schedules`, a scheduled run whose last conclusion was a failure ("<job> failed"), one that has not run for twice its interval ("<job> hasn't run since <time>"), a workflow GitHub turned off after 60 days without changes (`disabled_inactivity`, "GitHub turned off <job>"), and a latest deployment whose last state is `failure` or `error` ("Last deploy failed"), and without GitHub connected one item, "Connect GitHub to see its runs.", with **Connect GitHub**, and no failure rule applied; `teams`, a team's oldest thing that waits on the owner for over a day ("<team>: <agent> has waited <n> days for your answer") and each escalation `escalation.aged` recorded that still waits; `services`, a connector Claude Code lists as needing sign in again ("<service> needs you to sign in again in Claude"); and `runs`, today's scheduled runs that succeeded, collapsed and not counted. An item has a `fingerprint`, a hash of the fields that make it what it is (a session's last activity and what it left undone, a run's start and conclusion, a cron's end). `reminders.snooze { key, for: "day" | "week" }` hides the item until then; `reminders.dismiss { key }` hides it until its fingerprint changes; both keep the answer in `machine.db` and take the item out of the digest at once, and an item that is not in the digest is refused `unknown_item`. `reminders.give { key }` files a request in the team whose project, or member repository, the item is about, with `request.file` on that team's daemon, for its Product Manager to sort: for a session "Finish “<title>” in <project>. The work was left <n> days ago with <reasons>, on the branch <branch>."; an item no team can finish is refused `cannot_give`, and one in a project with no team this serve drives `no_team_for_this` ("make a team for <project> first"). `reminders.set { time?, browser?, system? }` keeps the time (`HH:MM`, else `bad_time`) and the two switches, both on by default, in `state.json`. A team's own socket answers `reminders.mine`, the items that are its own, which its Today shows as "Needs you today". An item offers, as it can: **Copy resume command** (`cd ~/<folder> && claude --resume <session id>`, the folder quoted for a shell), **Open on claude.ai** (a web session known from the export), **Open on GitHub** (the repository's `actions` or `deployments` page), **Give to the team**, **Answer** (the team's Today), **Connect GitHub**, **Snooze** with "For a day" and "For a week", and **Dismiss**. One notification is sent for a digest, at its time. If any page is connected, a socket of `/hub/rpc` or `/t/*/rpc`, and the owner's browser switch is on, the hub pushes `reminders.due { at, count, headline, time }` to the sockets of `/hub/rpc` and each shows one browser notice ("Catervas · 09:00", "9 things need you. A price check failed, and Tidepool's last deploy failed.") for that digest, the permission asked on "Needs you today" by **Allow notices** (or **Not now**), a click bringing the tab to `/needs-you`; if no page is connected and the computer switch is on, the computer is notified (8.6); a program that is missing or fails is recorded in the digest as `notified: "none"`, and the digest stays on All teams. The `headline` is the first two items' short words by urgency (a failure first). The pages: `/needs-you`, "Needs you today", with "<n> things · from your <time> reminder", the notice offer, the groups under "Sessions you may have forgotten", "Ending soon", "Schedules and deploys", "Your teams" and "Services", and "Today's runs (<n>)" collapsed, an item that needs explaining (a cron, a workflow GitHub turned off) with an info button, and **Give to the team** opening "Give to <team>" with the request that would be filed and **Send to the team**; on All teams the band "<n> things need you today." with the headline and **See all**; and in This computer "Reminders": "Daily reminder at <time>", "In the browser" ("When a Catervas tab is open.") and "From the computer" ("When no Catervas tab is open."). The notice's **Snooze a day** button of the mockup is dropped: a toast's buttons need a registered app.

Analytics (added in 0.152; ADR 0059; phase 10 step 08). `analytics.get { period: "week" | "month" }`, which the hub answers, and `analytics.mine { period }`, which a team answers for itself, read what is kept and write nothing; an answer is kept for 60 seconds per scope and period. The week is Monday to Sunday and the month the calendar month, in the computer's local time. Usage is in US dollars and has two parts that never overlap.
