Catervas pushes the branch to `origin` and opens a pull request with the `gh` program, titled `<Type>: <title>` (`Feat: Add a login page`; changed in 0.119, ADR 0066), whose body is short (changed in 0.122; ADR 0069) and composed by Catervas with no session, in exactly two sections: "## What changed", the contract's `summary` (else its title) cut to three sentences and 600 characters, and "## How it was verified", one line for each exit criterion by its text (the task is accepted, so each passed) and, for a reviewed task, "Reviewed by <name>: <the first sentence of the last review note an agent wrote>" cut to 200 characters; no intent, no completion note, no evidence, and the whole at most 1500 characters, past which criterion lines are dropped from the end and "- and <n> more checks" closes the list; each task id that is not part of a path is replaced by that task's title in quotes, or by "another task" when the board does not know it, so that nothing Catervas sends to the forge names a task id; every such pull request needs the human's merge on the forge unless the owner allowed Catervas to merge it (0.128, below), and the task is integrated when it merges, the local integration branch then brought up to the forge's. One pull request is opened for each accepted task and each folder change, none batched. Catervas reads each open pull request's state once a tick, and an idle Catervas ticks at least every 15 seconds while a finished task waits for its merge, else every minute (changed in 0.124); one closed without merging is an integration escalation, and the human's `catervas integrate` then records it as integrated if the branch is in the integration branch all the same (merged by hand, or through another pull request) and otherwise says to reopen it. A repository with no remote named `origin` has no forge: the accepted branch waits for the human to merge it by hand, a tick asks only whether the branch is already in the integration branch and records the integration when it is (`integrated_by` `human`, `sha` the integration branch's head), and the human's `catervas integrate`, `task_integrate` or `folder_change_integrate` is refused `not_merged: <branch> is not in <into> yet; merge it, then ask again` until it is. `catervas integrate` never merges: it reads the forge or, with no `origin`, the integration branch. `gh` picks the base repository itself, which in a fork with an `upstream` remote can be `upstream`; `gh repo set-default` settles it. Catervas's pushes are its own act on the host, with the user's own git credentials; no agent is acting, so no agent's `git_remote` is asked (ADR 0012; added in 0.8). An agent's own push is the tool `catervas_git_push` and is the owner's to widen (added in 0.136; ADR 0080): it pushes the assignee's own task branch to a remote named in `policy.push_remotes`, an array of remote names (1 to 20, each starting with a letter or digit, then letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`), which is `["origin"]` when the key is left out. The tool takes an optional `remote`, the first one listed when it is left out; a remote that is not listed is refused `remote_not_allowed: <remote> is not a remote the owner allows; push to <the listed ones>`. The team's Team rules name the listed remotes to an agent that holds `git_remote`, and Settings → Rules → "Where agents may push" edits the list. The agent still needs `git_remote` and pushes no other branch; Catervas's own integration above is unchanged, always one pull request (ADR 0061). A task is awaiting integration on the board from its move into `accepted` until `task.integrated` records where its branch landed; an epic, whose children carry the branches, never is. Today lists every merge waited on, under any team file (changed in 0.115): `waiting.list` gives an `integration` row for each accepted task awaiting integration, "Accepted: its pull request waits for you to merge it" once a `pull_request.opened` follows its acceptance and "Accepted: waiting for you to merge <branch>" otherwise. An epic's plan task has no row (below). The integration branch is the repository's default branch unless the team configures another; the repository's default branch is what `origin/HEAD` points at, and a repository with no remote records one nowhere, so there it is the branch that is checked out (added in 0.5).

**When Catervas merges (added in 0.128; ADR 0073).** When `merging_allowed` is true (5.12) and the tick is Catervas's own (the human's `catervas integrate` never merges), the routine works through these cases in order for each open pull request of an accepted task or a folder change, in the project and in each member repository, each through its own `gh` (`IntegrationTarget.forge`). A conflict (`mergeable: CONFLICTING` or `mergeStateStatus: DIRTY`) goes as above. A failed check is an integration escalation, "A check failed on GitHub: {names}. Catervas did not merge {url}; fix it or merge it yourself.", after which ticks leave the work to the human. Pending checks wait for the next tick. With checks passed, or with none configured, a branch `BEHIND` its base is refreshed as above (a folder change escalates), `BLOCKED` is an escalation, "GitHub will not merge {url} yet: it needs a review or another of the branch's rules. Merge it yourself once it can.", `CLEAN`, `HAS_HOOKS` and `UNSTABLE` are merged, and `UNKNOWN` and `DRAFT` wait. A check passes when it is a check run that completed `SUCCESS`, `NEUTRAL` or `SKIPPED` or a status that is `SUCCESS`; it is pending when a check run has not completed or a status is `PENDING` or `EXPECTED`; any other ending fails it. A repository with no checks at all merges as if its checks had passed, at once: the task is accepted, so Catervas's own verification passed (the founder, 2026-10-19), and there is no wait for GitHub to register checks. The merge reads the methods the repository allows with `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}` (`allow_merge_commit`, `allow_squash_merge`, `allow_rebase_merge`, a missing field allowed), takes the first of merge commit, squash and rebase (none allowed is an escalation, "{owner}/{repo} allows no merge method."), and runs `gh pr merge <url> --merge|--squash|--rebase --match-head-commit <headRefOid>`: never `--admin` or `--auto`, and no branch is deleted; the pinned commit means a push made after the checks were read is never merged unchecked. When `gh` refuses, that is an integration escalation in its words. A successful merge records `pull_request.merged { url, method }` (about no task), reads the pull request again and, once it is merged, records `task.integrated` (or `folder_change.integrated`) and brings the local integration branch up to `origin`; a merge queue that has not merged it yet is found merged by the next tick. On the forge `Merged` path `integrated_by` is `governor` when the log holds a `pull_request.merged` for the pull request's address and `human` otherwise. Today's rows read "Accepted: Catervas merges its pull request when GitHub's checks pass" for an accepted task whose pull request is open, and "Catervas merges its pull request when GitHub's checks pass" for an opened folder change, while merging is allowed. One agent alone may use it, and an epic's plan task and a task in a private folder have no pull request, so nothing changes for them. With no `origin` nothing merges.

A task in a private folder, a Finance Specialist's or a Procurement Specialist's (0.70), has no branch (6.6; added in 0.21; as built in 0.62). For it, `accepted` is the end: its move into `accepted` carries the effect `nothing_to_integrate`, so the board never shows it awaiting integration, no `task.integrated` is recorded, the integration policy does not apply, and the human's `catervas integrate` of it is refused `nothing_to_integrate`; a task that depends on it counts it integrated, so its dependants may be assigned (5.2). It is not assigned while another task holds the folder (5.2, 6.6), the two roles' folders being apart, so a finance task and a procurement task may run at once.

An epic's plan task opens its own pull request (added in 0.115; ADR 0061; changed in 0.134; ADR 0079). A task whose `allowed_paths` are exactly its `plan` (5.16 item 3) is integrated like any task that writes documents: a tick records `task.integrated` for it at once, without a pull request, when its plan file is already on the integration branch (`has_file` finds it there; `integrated_by` `governor`, `sha` the integration branch's head; by the file and not by ancestry, so a squash merge counts), and otherwise it goes through the forge as every accepted task does, with a pull request that the owner merges, or Catervas does when it may (0.128). Until then the epic's tasks still start from the plan task's branch (above). The refusal `carried_by_its_tasks` is gone: the human's `catervas integrate` of it takes the same path as any task's. Before 0.134 the plan task opened no pull request and waited for the epic's tasks' pull requests to carry its file, so a plan whose only started task was cancelled never reached the integration branch.

One task integrates at a time (added in 0.5). A merge moves the repository's own checkout — the integration branch is checked out, merged into, and what was there is put back — so two integrations at once on one repository can interleave and land a merge commit on the wrong branch. Tasks work in their own worktrees and are unaffected; it is integration alone that is serialised. Sessions of different agents run at once (8.2); integration runs in a tick, which holds the process's turn as well as this lock (added in 0.118; ADR 0064) (and, since 0.115, Catervas makes no merge into the integration branch itself, except the pull request it merges when the owner allows it (0.128): the lock serialises pushes, pull requests, those merges and the recording of merges made by hand). Every push, pull request opening, and recording of an integration holds an exclusive lock on `.catervas/local/integration.lock`, a file lock because `catervas integrate` runs in a process of its own beside `catervas run`, and reads the log again under it, so that two callers racing for one task record one integration (added in 0.8). A folder change's write and the owner's decision on one hold the same lock, from their checks to their event (added in 0.94).

When integration cannot land (added in 0.8). A push or a forge that fails raises an escalation with reason `integration` whose detail is git's words (a conflict or git refusing a merge only in an older log, since Catervas no longer merges, 0.115); nothing leaves `accepted` (5.2), so the task stays `accepted` and awaiting integration, and the escalation is a message rather than a move; it is also said in the channel (added in 0.134; ADR 0079), as a folder change's already was, by a system line tagged with the task, "<id> could not be added to <into>: <detail>", which names "the integration branch" when the target itself cannot be resolved. A failed push leaves the merge in place, because dependents start from the local integration branch, and its detail says to run `git push origin <branch>` once it can be pushed. Catervas does not try again after an integration escalation: the human's `catervas integrate` is the way on, and it integrates whatever the escalations, each failed attempt raising its own. A branch the human already merged by hand is recorded by `catervas integrate` (above). No git Catervas runs may prompt: each runs with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and an empty `GIT_ASKPASS`, so a push or fetch that wants a credential no helper gives fails with git's words. A push or fetch also runs ssh in batch mode (`GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -o BatchMode=yes"`), so that ssh fails rather than asking on the terminal for a host key or a passphrase while the integration lock is held, unless the user chose how git runs ssh (`GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, `GIT_SSH`, or `core.sshCommand`), which Catervas leaves as it is. The team's `integration_branch` is checked by git as a branch name before it is used, so a name such as `main:other` or `-f` is refused rather than read as a refspec or an option, and so is a name git reads as another branch (`@`, `@{-1}`).

**A pull request that stops merging (added in 0.122; ADR 0069).** Rule 2 reads each open pull request with `gh pr view --json state,mergeCommit,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,headRefOid,statusCheckRollup` (the last three added in 0.128). On `CONFLICTING`, for a task, under the integration lock: Catervas fast-forwards the integration branch from `origin` (a failure is an integration escalation), and does nothing more when the branch already holds all of it (the forge's answer is stale for a while after a push, so a refresh never repeats on every tick); otherwise it adds the task's worktree again on its kept branch and merges the integration branch into it on the host with the message `chore: bring up to date with <branch>`. A clean merge is pushed (the same pull request updates), the worktree is removed and `pull_request.refreshed { url, sha }` is recorded. A conflicted merge is left in the worktree with its markers, `pull_request.conflicted { url, into, paths }` is recorded, and the governor moves the task `accepted → assigned` (gate `pull_request_conflicted`, no effect), clearing its "awaiting integration" flag; rule 7 finds the worktree there and starts the assignee, whose implement message names the conflicted files in an untrusted block `conflicts` and says to resolve each, run the checks, commit with `catervas_git_commit`, which finishes the merge, ask for `verifying`, and block the task with `catervas_declare_blocked` when a conflicted file is outside its allowed paths. `catervas_git_commit` refuses a file that still holds a line beginning `<<<<<<< ` or `>>>>>>> ` (`conflict_markers`). The task is reviewed and accepted again, and rule 2 pushes the branch, which `open_pull_request` finds open and reuses. `UNKNOWN` waits for the next tick. A failed push after a clean merge, or a refusal of the move, is an integration escalation. A delivery counts a task once, however often it is accepted (ADR 0062): a task with a move into `accepted` at or before the delivery's `since_seq` is left out.

**Moving the documents, and landing a task's (added in 0.129; ADR 0074).** `documents.set_local` makes one folder change each way, in a scratch worktree `.catervas/local/worktrees/documents-<n>` and never in the owner's checkout: turning on removes `docs/catervas/` from the integration branch (`git rm -r`, commit `docs: keep the team's documents on this computer`, branch `docs/keep-documents-on-this-computer`), turning off adds what is on disk (`git add -f -A`, commit `docs: put the team's documents back in the repository`, branch `docs/put-documents-back-in-the-repository`); each is recorded as `document_storage.changed { local, change, branch, sha }`, opened as a pull request titled `Docs: Keep the team's documents on this computer` or `Docs: Put the team's documents back in the repository` whose body is "## What changed" with one sentence and "## How it was verified" with "Chosen by the owner in Settings.", and listed on Today as "Keep documents on this computer" or "Put documents back in your repository"; with no `origin` it waits for a merge by hand. When a take-out is integrated, git has deleted the files from the root checkout, and Catervas writes back every file the change removed that is missing, from the change's parent commit; when a put-back is, it removes the exclude lines; neither files a re-derive. A switch whose pull request was closed without merging (that escalation alone) puts the policy back, removes the exclude lines it added, and says "Your documents stay as they were: the pull request that moved them was closed." in the channel. A task's documents land when it is accepted, before its worktree is removed: a file whose root copy still equals the start copy is written, one whose root copy already equals the task's is left, and any other is set aside under `.catervas/local/documents/set-aside/<task>/<path>` with a channel line, never written over (5.17).

Who commits (changed in 0.36). A task's commits, made through `catervas_git_commit`, and integration's merge commits are the user's: Catervas commits as the identity git has for the repository. When git has none there, `user.name` or `user.email` empty or unset at the repository's effective scope, as on a fresh computer or a CI runner, Catervas commits as `catervas <catervas@localhost>`, the identity the project setup's first commit is made with, rather than leave git to refuse. A commit that still fails is answered to the agent with git's words, and Catervas also posts a line in the channel about the task saying it could not be committed and why, since a task whose work is not committed never reaches `verifying`. `catervas_git_commit` refuses a message that names a task id, `commit_message_names_a_task: <id> is a task id, which stays inside Catervas; describe the change instead`, before it checks any path (added in 0.119; ADR 0066); its description asks for Conventional Commits (`feat: ...`, `fix: ...`, `docs: ...`), which is asked and not enforced.

A task is assigned only when every dependency it lists is accepted (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: it was accepted and integrated), a Finance Specialist's or a Procurement Specialist's task counting once accepted as before, since it has no branch (6.6; added in 0.21), and its branch starts from where its work stands (changed in 0.115). Catervas lists the branches the worktree is made from: each dependency that is accepted, still awaiting integration, has a branch and is in the same repository (the same `repo`), in the order the contract lists them; then, for a task under an epic that has a `plan`, and is not itself the plan task, the branch of the last accepted plan task under that parent whose `plan` is the same, while the plan is not on the integration branch yet; then, outside a private folder (changed in 0.134; ADR 0079), the branch of every task in the same repository that is accepted and not yet integrated and whose `allowed_paths` all start with `docs/catervas/`, in the order the tasks were created (the team's accepted documents, such as the architecture and conventions an earlier task wrote, which a task would otherwise not see until the owner merges them); a branch that does not exist is dropped. The worktree is made from the first of them, or from the integration branch when there is none, and each other branch is merged inside the worktree with a merge commit `chore: start from <branch>` (changed in 0.119); Catervas makes that merge in the task's own fresh worktree, which is not a merge into the integration branch. A conflict with a dependency's branch or the plan's removes the worktree and its branch and the task waits, and the next tick tries again, so that once the conflicting dependency is merged by the human it drops out of the list. A documents branch that conflicts is left out instead and the others are kept (changed in 0.134), and it is not retried for that worktree. When a task starts from other branches, Catervas writes the ref `refs/catervas/start/<id>` at the worktree's head, and a task's diff, changed paths, new-tests base, reviewer's diff, design review diff, `catervas_git_diff`, commit count and the diff on its page are all taken from that ref, not from the integration branch, so a task shows its own changes only; its pull request is still from its branch into the integration branch. Worktrees and containers are removed when a task is accepted or cancelled; branches are kept. A container that cannot be removed, docker being down, leaves the task's worktrees in place to be removed on a later tick, and holds up no other work.

Folder changes (added in 0.94; ADR 0051; phase 8 step 03). A document of a role's folder that Catervas commits (5.17) is a folder change: one commit on a branch of its own (changed in 0.119; ADR 0066), `docs/<slug>`, the slug made from the documents' plain names joined by " and " (an agent version beside its document adds no name) as a task's is from its title, free by the same rule, and recorded as `branch` in the event that made the change; a change of an older log has none and is `docs/folder-<n>`. Its number `n`, which names the change inside Catervas alone (`catervas integrate folder-<n>`), is the first above the highest `change` the log holds for which git has neither `docs/folder-<n>` nor `origin/docs/folder-<n>`, so a fresh clone never reuses one. Catervas makes it in the root's checkout under the integration lock, as a merge is made: the branch is made from the integration branch's head, each file is written, staged and committed with `git commit --only` over those paths alone, so nothing else the owner staged is committed, and the branch that was checked out is checked out again. The author is `<display name> (Catervas) <catervas@localhost>`, the name without `<`, `>` and control characters, or the agent's id when nothing is left; the committer is the identity git has (above); the message is `docs(<the folder's last segment>): <each path within the folder, joined by ", "> by <display name>`, with `, approved by the owner` after an approval. Nothing is made, and the owner's own work is never carried off or written over, when a file or a directory on the way to it is a symbolic link (`folder_doc_link`), when the owner has a change to a file that is not committed, staged, changed or untracked (`folder_doc_busy`: commit it or put it aside first), or when an earlier change holds the file and is neither integrated nor escalated (`folder_doc_waiting`: "<path> has a change waiting to be added to the project (folder-<n>)"); a head that is detached is refused before anything is written. When every file already says its text on the integration branch nothing is made, which the tool answers `folder_doc_unchanged` and an approval records with no change. A failure after the branch was made takes everything back: each file restored or removed and unstaged, the earlier branch checked out, the new branch deleted.

A folder change is integrated as an accepted task's branch is, by the same routine, by pull request (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061): Catervas pushes the branch and opens a pull request titled `Docs: Update <the documents' plain names>` (changed in 0.119), or `Docs: Report for delivery <n>` when every document is a delivery's report (changed in 0.122; ADR 0069), whose body (changed in 0.122) is "## What changed" with one line for each document's plain name and "## How it was verified" with one line: "Written by <name> at the delivery's review; the team's documents are not reviewed (ADR 0061).", "Approved by the owner on Today." for an approval, or "Saved by the owner on the Files page." for the owner's own save, under the same 1500-character cap, then reads its state on each tick; with no `origin` the branch waits for a merge by hand, recorded once it is in the integration branch. A second tick rule, after the accepted tasks' and in a tick scoped to no task, attempts each change not yet integrated, a change after an escalation waiting for the human's word, and one that waits for a merge by hand passed over with no report; it reports `folder-<n>: integrated at <sha>`, `opened the pull request <url>` or `escalated its integration to the human: <detail>`. The events are `folder_change.opened`, `folder_change.integrated` (`integrated_by` `governor`, or `human` for the human's integrate or a pull request the human merged) and `folder_change.escalated`, in place of `pull_request.opened`, `task.integrated` and the integration escalation, none of them about a task. An escalation is also posted in the channel with its detail, since Today lists the escalations of tasks, and the project scan is not refreshed, a folder change touching no language, toolchain, test or criterion. `catervas integrate folder-<n>` (the command `folder_change_integrate { change }`) integrates a change whatever its escalations, as it does a task, answers the commit of one already integrated, and is refused `no_such_folder_change` for a number that is none. A change holds its files only until it is integrated or escalated: a later change to an escalated change's files is made from the integration branch as usual, and integrating the older one afterwards is the human's call, a conflict then escalating like any other. Today lists a change waiting to be integrated as it lists a task awaiting integration, under every team file (added in 0.95; phase 8 step 03b; changed in 0.115): `waiting.list` gives, for each change neither integrated nor escalated, an `integration` row with `folder_change` and no `task_id`, titled with the documents' plain names ("Roadmap", "Product description", else the path within `docs/catervas/`) joined by " and " and then " from review <n>" for an approval of an older log or " by <name>" for a write, with the line "Its pull request waits for you to merge it" once a `folder_change.opened` names the change, and otherwise "You approved it; it waits for you to merge it" or "<name> wrote it; it waits for you to merge it"; Today's row reads "Add <title> to your project" and its "Add" is a button that sends `folder_change_integrate { change }`, which records the merge once the branch is in the integration branch and is refused `not_merged` before. The command line does not list these rows. An escalated folder change whose pull request no longer merges is escalated once with "the pull request <url> no longer merges into <branch>" (changed in 0.122).

The owner's save (added in 0.96; ADR 0051; phase 8 step 04). `files.save` (5.17) commits the owner's edit of a document as a folder change, on its own branch (above) from the integration branch's head, with the message `docs(<the folder's last segment>): edit <path within the folder>` (`docs(product): edit roadmap.md`) and as the person git knows, not as an agent; it holds the integration lock from its checks to its event and records `folder_doc.edited { path, change, sha }`, about no contract and with no agent or session, after which the daemon wakes the orchestrator so that the next tick opens its pull request. It is then integrated as any folder change is, by pull request. Text the integration branch already holds makes no change and records nothing. A folder change the owner made is not an agent's: it is not listed among the integrations that wait on the owner (the page shows it), and no agent is named for it in the Files page's last change.

**Under autopilot (added in 0.138; ADR 0082).** Catervas merges its pull requests as it does with `merge_when_checks_pass` and the merge permission (ADR 0073), without either being set. A check that failed is never merged over: the failure is the task's integration escalation, decided by the Product Manager (`reopen_integration`, at most three per task, after which the escalation waits for the owner), and the tick leaves the pull request alone until the team has decided; a check that is pending is waited for; and a repository with no checks at all merges once Catervas's own Definition of Done has passed (5.4). A folder change (5.17) whose integration failed is escalated as before and is retried by the Product Manager (`catervas_decide { folder_change, choice: retry_folder_change, reason }`, at most three times) or flagged for the owner; a folder change that cost three `decide` sessions is flagged by Catervas. A decision about a folder change names the change and no task. Turned off, the first pull request waits for the owner's merge again.

### 5.15 Recovery (added in 0.2)

Catervas can stop at any moment: the laptop closes, the process is killed. On startup it reconciles the event log with itself and with the files (8.4): every session that has a `session.started` event without a `session.ended` one is ended with reason `aborted` and the detail "interrupted: catervas stopped before the session ended" (the wire has no `interrupted` reason, and nothing would read one differently; changed in 0.8), and one with no `cost.recorded` is recorded as costing nothing on the model its start names, so that it counts against its task's sessions as any session does; every task that was `in_progress` stays `in_progress` and its next session starts from the last commit on its branch and the last note, in a sandbox made afresh, a container left by the killed run being replaced; a `verifying` task gets its reviewer's session again without its recorded criteria being run again; worktrees and containers that belong to accepted or cancelled tasks are removed, the containers by name since no handle to them survived, and the task's own worktree last, so that a recovery stopped part way does the rest next time. A finished task in a member (added in 0.113; ADR 0057; phase 9 step 02c) has its worktrees, `CTV-<n>` and `CTV-<n>-base`, removed by the member's own git, which then runs `git worktree prune` there so that no stale registration keeps the task's kept branch from being checked out in the member; when the member's git refuses a worktree (a member that moved and was located before its worktrees were repaired), or the member is missing or no longer listed, the folders are removed as plain folders, and a member that was missing keeps a stale registration of each until a later finished task in it prunes them, until then the kept branch cannot be checked out there (`'feature/CTV-1' is already used by worktree at …`). Nothing is lost that was committed or logged, and nothing is repeated that was recorded as done.

### 5.16 Epics: from a request to sub-contracts (added in 0.3)

Every prompt from the user that asks for work is translated into a contract before anything else happens, and so is every request an agent files from the channel, and every request the user sends from a one-to-one chat (changed in 0.34: the agent proposes it there, and the user files it, 4.3). The first thing that happens to a request is triage: the Scrum Master, or the Product Manager when the team has no active Scrum Master, decides whether the request is large or small and records the decision with a reason (`request.triaged`). A large request becomes an epic (`kind: epic`). A small request becomes a single standalone task (`kind: task`, no `parent`), written by the Product Manager like any task, with its questions to the user asked first and no approval of its contract (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: it was required by the team's policy `human_accepts_contracts` or for a `high` risk task); it then goes through the ordinary lifecycle without a breakdown. The governor refuses `draft → refining` until the triage is recorded, and the user may overrule it (`catervas triage <id> large|small`, or the board) before the Product Manager starts. Triage is a session of the triager's, the Scrum Master's when the team has an active one (changed in 0.10), and runs on the cheaper model, `claude-sonnet-5-5` at low effort whatever the triager's own model (changed in 0.33 from `claude-sonnet-5`), with `catervas_triage_request` as its one tool and no built-in tool, and produces one event, so a small request costs one short session on top of its own. Once a request is triaged, Catervas moves it to `refining` on the Product Manager's behalf with no session; the user's window to overrule the triage is the draft (added in 0.8). A request an approved data pipeline files (6.10) is triaged as any other (added in 0.76).

An epic goes through the same lifecycle as a task with four differences (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: its contract is no longer approved by the user, its plan task needs no review, and Catervas accepts it itself).

1. The Product Manager writes it, and must ask the user every question it needs first. In an epic's `refining` sessions the Product Manager asks through the question mechanism (5.7) before it writes the contract, and it writes the epic's requirements into the product's spec (`docs/catervas/product/spec` and its agent version, 5.17) once the epic is ready, which it is when its contract has passed the Definition of Ready (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: the user's approval is no longer waited for, so an "approved" epic in the Product Manager's skills means a ready one), and writes no product document for a `cancelled` epic, whose documents would describe a decision the team abandoned (added in 0.3; changed in 0.91: the Product Manager's prompt and its `writing-requirements` skill say so, and `catervas_write_product_doc`, which the governor refused until the approval, and its check are gone). When the Product Manager believes it has no questions, it says so in the contract's intent (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: no approval of the user checks that it was right).
2. Its contract is not approved by the user (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061; from 0.3 to 0.114 every epic required the user's acceptance of the contract before it left `refining`, whatever its risk). Once the contract passes the Definition of Ready, the governor moves the epic to `ready` like any contract; the row to `escalated` with reason `approval`, and the user's approving or sending it back, stay in the table for older logs only (5.2). A contract written in `refining`, or one filed whole (a breakdown's task, or a contract the user holds), is judged by the governor before the Product Manager refines it again; one that fails goes back to the Product Manager with its failures (added in 0.8); a contract the human sent back to `refining` is not filed whole, it is refined first (5.2; changed in 0.134); one that fails three times is escalated (5.2). The Product Manager asks the user its questions first (item 1), which is where the user shapes an epic. A contract's `summary` for the human is optional (5.4).
3. It is planned, its tasks are written, and they are assigned (changed in 0.98; ADR 0051; changed in 0.115; ADR 0061). A ready epic is assigned to the Scrum Master, or to the Product Manager when the team has no active Scrum Master; that assignee holds the epic, assigns its tasks (5.2), and closes it out (item 4). Its breakdown is the Product Manager's, in this order. With an active Architect, the Product Manager first files the task that writes the plan: `parent` the epic, assignee role `architect`, `plan` and `allowed_paths` exactly `docs/catervas/architecture/plans/<epic-id>` followed by the team's extension (`.html` or `.md`), no `lane`, and an `artifact` criterion that the plan exists, and no other, since no agent reviews it; a plan task is one whose `allowed_paths` are exactly its `plan`. The Architect writes the plan in that task's `implement` session, in lanes no wider than the team's active builders, and Catervas accepts the task once the plan exists (5.4); the plan task opens no pull request (5.14). Once the plan task is accepted, whether or not it is merged, a `plan` session of the Product Manager is asked for the epic's tasks, with the plan's text read from the integration branch or, while it is not merged, from the plan task's branch, and writes one task per planned task (`kind: task`, `parent` set), each with its `plan`, its `lane`, the planned tasks it needs as dependencies, and the Architect's paths and constraints. Catervas reads the plan from the integration branch, else from the accepted plan task's branch, and when it is in neither the Product Manager is asked to plan the epic again. A task that names the plan starts from the plan task's branch while the plan is unmerged (5.14), so it needs no merge to read it, and every pull request carries the plan with it to the integration branch. With no active Architect the Product Manager plans the lanes itself, filing each task with its `lane` and no `plan`, and no plan document is written, since a document needs a docs task and a reviewer the team may lack. Nothing is asked of the epic while a task under it is worked, and it is closed out once every task not cancelled is accepted and they are not all plan tasks. The Scrum Master no longer breaks an epic down. A task's `allowed_paths` fall within its epic's, its own plan's path aside (a task whose `plan` is its epic's plan path may name that path in any epic), its budget within the epic's remaining budget, and its parent must be `in_progress`; the Definition of Ready checks all three, and that the lanes keep apart and fit the builders (5.3). A task under an epic may be created only by its epic's assignee, by the Product Manager or by the human; a standalone task comes only from triage. Catervas assigns a ready epic on its assignee's behalf, with no session, once that assignee holds fewer open tasks than the WIP limit, and starts it (added in 0.8): to the Scrum Master when the team has an active one, with the Product Manager as its reviewer (added in 0.10), and otherwise to the Product Manager, whose epic the human reviews; since 0.115 the reviewer field is kept as it was but nobody reviews the epic, which Catervas verifies alone (item 4; ADR 0061). The Product Manager's `plan` session then breaks it down (changed in 0.98), and a `plan` session of the epic's assignee assigns each of its tasks once ready, a lane's tasks to its builder (5.2; added in 0.8). When nothing can be assigned and a Software Developer or UI/UX Designer holds no task while two or more `ready` tasks of its role wait unheld in the lanes of an epic in progress, the active Product Manager gets one `plan` session about the epic (added in 0.133; ADR 0078): it is told who is idle and each waiting task with its lane and dependencies, moves each task that needs no unfinished task's result back to `refining` (5.2), rewrites its `lane`, `dependencies` and `allowed_paths` so that it is a lane of its own for an idle builder, and readiness runs again (`lane_beyond_builders`, `lanes_overlap`). When the tasks truly wait on one another it changes nothing. It runs once per change (changed in 0.137; ADR 0081): only when no `plan` session of the epic has started since the epic's children last changed (a `contract.written` or `task.transitioned` of one of them) or the team last changed (`agent.updated` or `team.updated`), read from the log; nothing is kept in memory, so a restart does not repeat it and the idle builders, which change whenever a session starts or ends, no longer matter.
4. It is done when its tasks are. An epic moves to `verifying` when every task under it is `accepted` or `cancelled` and at least one is accepted; its own exit criteria are then run by Catervas on the integration branch, and the governor accepts or rejects the epic on them, with no reviewer, no Product Manager acceptance session and no user (5.4; changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: an epic of 0.3 to 0.114 was reviewed by the Product Manager or the human and accepted by the user, and an older epic with a `review` or `human` criterion still takes that path). The epic's assignee closes it out in a `plan` session once its tasks are done, writing its completion note and asking for `verifying`, or filing more tasks when the user's message asks for them; Catervas runs its mechanical criteria first (5.4; added in 0.8). A rejected epic goes back to `in_progress` by the governor's row, as a task does, and its assignee's close-out `plan` session, once every task under it is done, is given the last rejection, the failed criteria's ids and the review note, and asked to file the tasks that fix it rather than close it out again; once a task has been created under the epic since that rejection, the close-out is the plain one. A new rejection raises the iteration, which the iteration limit bounds (added in 0.10).

A request Catervas triages itself (added in 0.72; ADR 0042). The request for a plan's new version with a raised marketing budget (6.5) is filed by Catervas for the owner's decision, not from a person's words: `task.created` carries `raises: <plan>` (8.5) and Catervas records `request.triaged { size: small, reason: "a raised marketing budget for <plan>", triaged_by: "catervas" }` in the same call, so no triage session runs and no window to overrule remains; it is refined and approved as any request is.

The product plan task (added in 0.99; ADR 0051; phase 8 step 06; changed in 0.115; ADR 0061). The owner's word `product_plan_draft` (4.3) files the Product Manager's task for a new project's product plan: its `task.created` has `created_by: human` and `product_plan: true`, and Catervas records `request.triaged { size: small, reason: "a new project's product plan", triaged_by: "catervas" }` in the same call. Its contract is fixed: the title "Draft the product plan"; the Product Manager as assignee and the Architect, else the Scrum Master, as reviewer field; `low` risk; `budget` the placeholder budget (the team's cap on a task when it has one); `allowed_paths` `docs/catervas/product/spec.<x>`, `spec.agent.<x>`, `roadmap.<x>` and `roadmap.agent.<x>`, `<x>` the team's extension (`html` or `md`; changed in 0.108); and four `artifact` criteria (changed in 0.115: it had two `review` ones), one for each file: the spec satisfies R1, the roadmap R2 and each agent version R3. The task is judged as filed, as a re-derive is, so no refine session rewrites Catervas's contract, and a refused one goes to the Product Manager as any contract does. Its `implement` session is shown the owner's interview, as the interview's own session is, cut to leave room for what the owner said about the task, which is never cut. Nobody approves the plan: the task is accepted by Catervas on its criteria (5.4), the new project's other work then plans and its Catervafication starts (below), and the documents reach the owner as a pull request (5.14), to read and merge in their own time, or in Files (4.5). A team whose rules require a `test` or `command` criterion refuses it at readiness, as it refuses every docs task.

A goal's request (added in 0.130; ADR 0075). A request filed by `catervas_file_goal_work` (5.18) carries `goal` on its `task.created` and is triaged at its filing: `request.triaged { size, reason: "planned towards <goal>", triaged_by: catervas }` is recorded in the same filing with the size its planner gave, so no triage session runs and, as for a raise, the owner has no draft window to overrule the size. The Product Manager then writes its contract as for any request, and a large one becomes an epic and is broken down as usual. In one agent alone it is a small task given to that agent, who writes its contract (4.3).

A user who wants to write the epic themselves does so in the editor or as a file, locks it (5.11), and approves it; the breakdown still happens by the Product Manager. When the triage sized a request as small and the Product Manager finds while refining that it is not, it re-triages the request itself as large (`catervas_triage_request` accepts this one change from the Product Manager of a `refining` standalone task); the standalone task becomes the epic and its refining starts over. The user may overrule any triage until refining starts.

The product's spec and roadmap, `docs/catervas/product/spec` and `roadmap`, each with its agent version, are the Product Manager's own, and sit in its folder (5.17); changed in 0.91: `catervas_write_product_doc`, which wrote them under `.catervas/product/` and recorded a `product_doc.written` event for each, and the `.catervas/product/` directory itself are gone. The event kind stays in the protocol so that older logs read (8.5). The Product Manager writes its folder in docs tasks of its own (changed in 0.92; 5.17).

The Catervafication's epic (added in 0.101; ADR 0051; phase 8 step 07; changed in 0.115; ADR 0061). `catervas_store::requests::file_catervafication_epic` files it whole, as `file_request` files an epic (its `kind` is Catervas's to set), and records `request.triaged { size: large, reason: "the Catervafication of an existing repository" | "the Catervafication of a new project", triaged_by: "catervas" }` and `catervafication.started { project }` in the same filing, so that no triage session runs. It is judged as filed whole, as a breakdown's task is: no refine session rewrites it, and nothing asks the owner to approve it. Its contract is fixed: the title "Catervafy the repository" or "Catervafy the new project"; the Product Manager as assignee and the human as reviewer field; `low` risk; a budget of the placeholder budget for each task it is filed with (seven for an existing repository of one repository, five plus two for each member present at the Start in a project folder, else three; changed in 0.117; ADR 0063); `allowed_paths` `docs/catervas/**`; and one `artifact` criterion, the product spec: `docs/catervas/product/spec` in the team's extension, `must_contain` the format's first heading (`<h1` in an HTML team, `# ` in a Markdown one), in a single repository and in a project folder alike, since Catervas runs an epic's criteria on the integration branch of the project folder's own repository, where `docs/catervas/` lives (it had one `review` criterion asking whether every task under it is accepted or cancelled); its `summary` is the Offer card's sentence for the owner, not the intent. For an existing repository (changed in 0.117; ADR 0063) its second requirement, R2, is that the Software Developer and the UI/UX Designer, when the team has them, hunt for bugs and file every bug found as a request, and the criterion satisfies R1 and R2; an epic filed without R2 (before 0.117) gets no hunt, so its budget is never overrun; its intent and summary say the team also hunts and starts the marketing. The owner starts it by Start, or, for a new project, it starts by itself when the product plan's task is accepted (below). Catervas accepts the epic itself once its tasks are integrated and the spec criterion passes; a team that changed its format afterwards fails the criterion and sends the epic back, which the owner's choice of format accepts.

Its tasks (added in 0.101). At the epic's breakdown point, when it is `in_progress`, Catervas files, as itself and with no session, the task of each role `catervafication_roles` lists that has none under the epic in any status (a task the owner cancelled is not filed again), each under the epic. For an existing repository the roles are, in this order, the Product Manager, the Architect, the Software Developer, the UI/UX Designer and the Marketing Specialist; for a new project the Architect, the Software Developer and the Marketing Specialist, the product plan being step 06's own task. A role is listed when it has an active agent and the team has a reviewer for its task (the default reviewer of 5.1, since `ReviewerAvailable` would refuse it otherwise); and the UI/UX Designer only when its browser is ready (6.8) (changed in 0.117; ADR 0063: the Marketing Specialist no longer waits for the Product Manager's row). The Scrum Master gets no task. Each task is a fixed template: a title, an intent ending "Follow your skill catervafying-the-repository.", one `artifact` criterion for each document (the path, `must_contain` a heading (`<h1` in an HTML team, `# ` in a Markdown one), the Architect's `overview` also `<svg` or a Mermaid block (changed in 0.108)), `allowed_paths` the role's folder, and `low` risk, and, for the two roles that change code, a `review` criterion asking whether each document says only what the project, its history or its owner's words show and names where it read it and whether any contradicts another or the code (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: the Product Manager's, the Architect's and the Marketing Specialist's tasks lose that `review` criterion, since only code is reviewed): each in the team's format (`.html` or `.md`): the Product Manager's `spec`, `spec.agent`, `roadmap` and `roadmap.agent`; the Architect's `overview`, `features`, `jobs` and `structure` (a new project's `overview` and `structure`); the Developer's `conventions` and `workflow`; the Designer's `ui-inventory`; the Marketing Specialist's none, its plan being proposed with `catervas_propose_marketing_plan` (6.5), the task's first criterion being a `command`, `ls docs/catervas/marketing/plans/MP-* >/dev/null 2>&1` with exit code 0 (changed in 0.115), and its second (added in 0.117; ADR 0063) an `artifact` on `docs/catervas/marketing/kickoff` in the team's format holding a heading and `MP-`. The Marketing Specialist's task, "Write the marketing plan and start on it", is filed with the others in both kinds of project, with no dependency (changed in 0.117; ADR 0063; it depended on the Product Manager's task from 0.115): it reads the whole project (6.5), proposes the plan, schedules the first posts and writes `kickoff` naming the plan, what it scheduled and what it asked for. Two agents of a role share one task: a folder is the role's.

Bug hunts (added in 0.117; ADR 0063; standalone plan `catervafication-work`). Beside the documentation tasks, after them, an existing repository's epic (with R2) files a hunt for the Software Developer, "Hunt for bugs in the code", when one is active, and for the UI/UX Designer, "Hunt for bugs in the app's screens", when one is active and its browser is ready (6.8); a new project gets none, having no code. A hunt changes no code: its `allowed_paths` are exactly its role's report, `docs/catervas/engineering/bug-hunt` or `docs/catervas/design/ui-bug-hunt` in the team's format, its one criterion is an `artifact` on that report holding a heading and "Bugs filed", and its `reviewer_role` is the Product Manager. A task whose `allowed_paths` are exactly its role's hunt report is a hunt (`is_hunt`, as a plan task's paths are exactly its plan), and a hunt is the one task of a code-changing role that no agent reviews: `reviewed_by_an_agent` is false for it, so the governor accepts it on its criterion (5.4). A hunt is filed once, with the Catervafication; the owner gives a later one in the agent's chat (4.3). A Designer's hunt skips the explore and design-plan stage, since it changes no screen, and its implement session is given the preview and the browser. In a project folder the hunts are filed for each member present at the Start, in `repos.yaml` order, the Developer's and then the Designer's, each naming that member in `repo` and writing its report inside that member, so each runs in that member's worktree and sandbox; a member has a UI when its project scan finds a way to start its app (`app_start`, ADR 0054), and one without a UI gets no UI hunt, Catervas writing once on the epic the note "No UI bug hunt for <name>: Catervas found no way to start its app.". Phase 9 step 06 may move the reports to `docs/catervas/repos/<name>/`.

A hunter files each bug as a request with `catervas_file_bug`, offered in the implement session of a hunt alone and refused (`bug_refused`) to anyone but the hunt's assignee. Its input is a `title` (3 to 120 characters), `where` (1 to 300), `steps` (1 to 10, each 1 to 300), `expected` and `actual` (1 to 1,000 each), a `severity` (`low`, `medium` or `high`) and `evidence` (1 to 5 items, each 1 to 1,000; text, such as a URL, a console line, or a command and its output), counted in code points of the trimmed text; a field out of its limit is refused `bug_out_of_bounds`. It files a `draft` request created by the hunter, whose intent is the parts in fixed words, `task.created { found_by: <hunt> }`, and, in the same filing, `request.triaged { small, reason: "a bug <hunt> found", triaged_by: catervas }`, so no triage session runs; the Product Manager then writes its contract like any request's and the team fixes it under the usual flow. A hunt files at most 10 bugs (`hunt_bug_limit`), and a bug whose title, trimmed, lower-cased and with its spaces collapsed, matches an open task that any hunt filed is refused `bug_already_filed`, naming it. The answer is `{ task_id, status, filed, left }`. A hunt ends when its report is written and committed: what was checked, and under "Bugs filed" each bug's id and title. A wrong bug is caught when the Product Manager refines it, and the Product Manager can cancel what is not a bug.

A request given in a chat (added in 0.117; ADR 0063). A task given to an agent in its chat (4.3) is not refined by the Product Manager. Rule 10 moves it to `refining` with no session, and rule 9 gives the refine session to that agent, told "<Name>, the owner gave you this task in your one-to-one chat, and you write its contract yourself" and what to keep, who writes the contract with the Product Manager's standing on that one task while it is `draft` or `refining` (a paused agent's task waits). Readiness and the governor's own check are unchanged, since no agent judges a contract (ADR 0061). Whoever writes it, the Product Manager included, cannot change its `assignee_role` (`given_task_role_fixed`), its `reviewer_role` from the default reviewer of that role (`given_task_reviewer_fixed`) or its intent, the owner's words (`given_task_intent_fixed`); the human's `contract.save` is not held, and a change of the assignee role returns the task to the ordinary rules. Once `ready`, rule 8 assigns it (5.2).

A new project's Catervafication (added in 0.101; changed in 0.115; ADR 0061). In a tick that is about no one task, once a project whose log holds `project.started` has its product plan's task accepted (the task created with `product_plan: true`, accepted whether or not it is merged) and no `catervafication.started`, Catervas starts it as itself, with an active Product Manager and at least one role to give a task; with none, it files nothing and records nothing. Catervas records no approval of the owner's for the epic, which waits for none (5.16 item 2): `catervafication::start` no longer records `human.accepted { subject: contract }` for either caller.

**Under autopilot (added in 0.138; ADR 0082).** An epic, or a contract of risk `high`, that escalates with the reason `approval` or `risk_gate` is approved by the Product Manager (`catervas_decide { choice: approve_plan, reason }`): the contract is accepted and the task goes to `ready`, recorded as `human.accepted` with `accepted_by` the Product Manager's id and the reason as its message. `back_to_plan` and `cancel` stay its other choices.

### 5.17 Role folders (added in 0.91; ADR 0051)

Every role but the Finance and Procurement Specialists owns a folder under `docs/catervas/`, committed in the repository, where it keeps what it knows of the project as documents. Only the owner writes its folder; every agent reads every folder (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: the Marketing Specialist's reading, held to the Product Manager's folder and its own from 0.93, is open, 5.6). The table, in the order the Team rules list it (`catervas-core`'s `folders::ROLE_FOLDERS`):

| Role | Folder |
|---|---|
| Product Manager | `docs/catervas/product/` |
| Architect | `docs/catervas/architecture/` |
| Software Developer | `docs/catervas/engineering/` |
| UI/UX Designer | `docs/catervas/design/` |
| Scrum Master | `docs/catervas/delivery/` |
| Marketing Specialist | `docs/catervas/marketing/` |

The folder belongs to the role: two Developers both own `engineering/`. The Finance and Procurement Specialists own none; their private folders under `.catervas/local/` (6.6) are a different thing. The DevOps Engineer's `operations/` comes with its role (6.9).

Ownership is held at readiness. While a role has an active agent, no other role's task may name an `allowed_paths` entry that could reach its folder (`folder_owned`, 5.3); a folder whose owner has no active agent is anyone's. The Definition of Done does not hold it a second time: the diff is held to `allowed_paths` (5.4).

A human document and its twin. Three kinds of document are written for people and kept beside a twin written for agents, `<name>.agent.md` or `<name>.agent.html` in the document's own format: `docs/catervas/product/spec`, `docs/catervas/product/roadmap`, and each marketing plan `docs/catervas/marketing/plans/MP-<n>`, each `.md` or `.html`, `n` decimal digits not starting with `0`, directly in `plans/`. The list is fixed, not a pattern. A path is normalised as the permission check normalises it (5.6) and compared with letter case, as git records it; the twin is the path with `.agent` before its extension. The two are one document written twice: the Definition of Done refuses a diff that changes one without the other (`pair_changed_alone`, 5.4). The marketing plan's twin is written by the tool that proposes the plan, from its `agent_text` (6.5), so that a plan's task can be accepted.

The Product Manager's documents. Its folder is `docs/catervas/product/`; `.catervas/product/` and `catervas_write_product_doc` are gone. Its prompt names the folder and what goes there, and its `writing-requirements` and `scoping-a-release` skills tell it to write the spec and the notes in a docs task of its own, `spec` and its agent version changed and committed together (changed in 0.92). It writes the contract of such a task and is its assignee, on the branch `docs/CTV-<n>`, held to the document paths and kept off other owners' folders; the Scrum Master assigns it, or the Product Manager itself when the team has no active Scrum Master. Its tiers are `read`, `network`, `write_workspace` and `git_local` (5.6), because a docs task reaches `verifying` only with a commit, and its refine, plan and triage sessions, which are not about a task's implement session, change nothing (5.6; `no_task_no_write`). No agent reviews it: Catervas accepts it on its criteria (5.1, 5.4; changed in 0.115; ADR 0061), and the spec and the roadmap it writes at a delivery's review land like any document (below).

What every session is told. The Team rules (8.2) end with the folders line, built by `folders_line`, the documents line (5.12) and the stale twins line. The folders line is built from the roles with an active agent: `- folders: <folder>/ (<role>), ...` for each role of the table that is active or is the reader's own, in table order; then `Yours is <folder>/: write no other folder named here.` or, for a role with none, `You have none: write none of them.`; then `Read any of them, and where a document has an .agent.html or .agent.md twin beside it, read the twin, which is written for agents.` Every role is told the same last sentence since 0.115 (ADR 0061; the Marketing Specialist's `Read only docs/catervas/product/ and docs/catervas/marketing/…` of 0.93 is gone). With nothing to list it is `- folders: none`. Each owner's prompt also names its own folder and what goes there (6.1 to 6.5, 6.8).

Writing a folder document (added in 0.94; ADR 0051; phase 8 step 03). `catervas_write_folder_doc { path, text, agent_text?, summary? }` is a `read`-tier tool (5.6). It is offered in a `ceremony` session whose thread is `review` or `retro` and whose agent's role owns a folder (5.9), and refused `folder_doc_refused` in any other session, since the hook checks only the session's list. The path is repository-relative, normalised as the permission check normalises it and compared with letter case, a `.md` or `.html` file at least one segment below the caller's folder, not an agent version, at most 512 characters and not a path the team protects, itself or its twin (`folder_doc_path`); a marketing plan is `folder_doc_marketing_plan`, proposed with `catervas_propose_marketing_plan` in a task (6.5). `text` is the document, or for a pair the version for people, not blank (`folder_doc_empty`) and at most 262,144 bytes (`folder_doc_too_large`), the Files page's cap. For `docs/catervas/product/spec` and `roadmap`, in either format, the human documents the owner approves (`OWNER_ACCEPTED`), `agent_text` (the agent version, the same bounds) is required (`folder_doc_agent_text`) and refused for any other path; `summary` is no longer required for them, and one given is not recorded (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: nobody decides on the change), while for any other path a `summary` is still refused. A document for agents is written as a folder change (5.14): the tool answers `{ path, change, branch, next }` and records `folder_doc.written { path, written_by, change, sha }` with the session on its envelope and no task, posting nothing in the channel; `next` says "Catervas opens a pull request for <branch> on its next tick; the document is in <into> once it merges." when the project has an `origin`, and "<branch> waits for you to merge it into <into>." when it has none (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061) Text the integration branch already holds is `folder_doc_unchanged`, and the refusals of a folder change are `folder_doc_busy`, `folder_doc_link` and `folder_doc_waiting` (5.14). A human document is written at a delivery's review alone (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: it was proposed and waited for the owner, 5.7), `folder_doc_at_review` in another ceremony or when no delivery has closed ("<path> is written at the review, not at another ceremony"): the spec and the roadmap land as one folder change of both files, the version for people and its agent version (`agent_text`), authored for the writing agent, and the tool records `folder_doc.written` and answers as for any document, so the change reaches a pull request (5.14). Proposals already in a log are still decided (`folder_doc_decide`, 5.7). Both refuse the same text as the integration branch's, a text and its twin both, as `folder_doc_unchanged`. The tool holds the integration lock from its checks to its event.

Staleness (added in 0.96; ADR 0051; phase 8 step 04). A twin is stale when the last commit that changed its human document is neither the last commit that changed the twin nor an ancestor of it, both read on the integration branch with git's history simplification, not along the first parents: a re-derive that began before a second edit and merged after it must stay stale, and its merge commit would hide that. It is not stale when one integration brought both, the last commit of each path along the first parents being the same one, and a pair with a file missing is no pair. Nothing is stored: `catervas-core`'s `twin_is_stale` is the rule and `catervas-store`'s `git::stale_twins` the reads, beside `integration_branch`. The owner's change not yet integrated makes nothing stale. A twin made stale by the owner's own git commit, outside the Files page, gets no re-derive; the page then says only "The team’s version is older than yours", naming no agent (04b).

Every session is told which twins are stale (added in 0.96). After the folders line and the documents line the Team rules say `- stale twins: <paths joined ", ">. Each is behind the document for people beside it, which the owner changed: read that document as well until the twin is brought up to date.`, and nothing when none is. A git error reading them leaves the line out rather than failing the session. The Definition of Done lets a diff that changes only a stale twin pass `pair_changed_alone` (5.4).

The Files page's server (added in 0.96; ADR 0051; phase 8 step 04; the page is 4.5). `files.tree {}` answers the team's `integration` policy and one folder for each role of the table with an active agent, in table order, with its name (its last segment as words, `Product`), its role, the role's first active agent in team-file order, and its documents: the regular `.md` and `.html` files under the folder at any depth read from the integration branch's head, never from the root checkout, except the twin of a human document that is present, which rides on its document as `twin`. A document that only the branch of a task accepted and still waiting to merge holds (its board row's `awaiting_integration`, the first such task in board order) is listed too, with that task as `task` (else `null`), so a pull request not yet merged hides nothing; `files.read` and `/documents/raw` read it from that branch, and it is neither editable nor askable until it merges (added in 0.109). A document is named by `catervas-core`'s `DOCUMENT_STEMS`, keyed by stem without an extension (`product/spec` "Product description", `roadmap` "Roadmap", `architecture/overview` "Overview", `features` "Features", `jobs` "Scheduled jobs", `structure` "Structure", `engineering/conventions` "Conventions", `workflow` "Workflow", `engineering/bug-hunt` "Bug hunt" (added in 0.117; ADR 0063), `design/ui-inventory` "UI inventory", `design/ui-bug-hunt` "UI bug hunt" (added in 0.117), `delivery/cadence` "Delivery rhythm" (changed in 0.116), `marketing/brand/brand-kit` "Brand kit", `persona` "Brand persona", `marketing/kickoff` "Marketing kickoff" (added in 0.117), `marketing/research/product` "The product", `audience` "The people it is for", `competitors` "Competitors", `outreach` "How competitors reach people", `positioning` "Where to start" (added in 0.127)), a file directly in a folder's `plans/` whose stem is a task on the board or a marketing plan is "Plan: <its title>", and any other is its file stem with `-` and `_` as spaces and the first letter upper case; documents come in that order, then by path. `files.read { path }` answers the document and its twin, each with its text, its blob and its last change; whether the twin is stale and whether a task that brings it up to date is neither accepted nor cancelled (`rederiving`); whether the owner may edit it (`editable`, false for a marketing plan); and the owner's own waiting change. A path `files.tree` would not list is `NOT_FOUND`. The last change is the last commit along the integration branch's first parents that changed the path, read by what its subject names, the first task id or folder change in subject order (`named_in_subject`) and, when it names neither, a pull request number (added in 0.119; ADR 0066): a subject that starts `Merge pull request #<n>` or ends `(#<n>)`, read through the newest `pull_request.opened` of a task that names no `repo`, or `folder_change.opened`, with that number: a task on the board gives `task_id` and its assignee as `agent_id`; a folder change gives `by_you` when the owner made it, else the agent that wrote it or whose proposals the owner approved in it; anything else gives only the commit's author name. While a folder change the owner made holds the path and is neither integrated nor escalated, `waiting` is `{ change, branch }` and the document, its blob and its last change are read from that branch's head with `by_you`; another's waiting change is not shown.

Saving (added in 0.96). `files.save { path, text, base }` refuses with -32005 and `data.errors` of `{ path, message, code }`, `path` a JSON pointer, in this order: `outside_folders` (`/path`: not under `docs/catervas/`, climbing out, or under no folder `files.tree` lists), `not_a_document` (`/path`: not a `.md` or `.html` file), `agent_twin` (`/path`: the team writes its twins), `marketing_plan` (`/path`: "A marketing plan changes through a new version on its page.", which keeps its own flow, ADR 0042), `too_large` (`/text`: over 262,144 bytes); then, holding the integration lock, `file_changed` (`/base`: the integration branch has no file there, or its blob is not `base`), `file_busy` (`/path`: the root checkout has an uncommitted change to the file), `is_a_link` (`/path`) and `change_waiting` (`/path`: an earlier change of the path is neither integrated nor escalated); git's own failure is an internal error. The save is a folder change (5.14) and answers `{ change, branch }`, or both null when the text is the file's.

Documents in either format (added in 0.108; ADR 0058). A document under `docs/catervas/` is `<name>.md` or `<name>.html`; its format is its extension, and a human document's agent version has the same one (`<name>.agent.md`, `<name>.agent.html`). Only those two extensions are documents. The fixed documents (the spec, the roadmap, the Catervafication documents, the marketing plans, `DOCUMENT_STEMS`) are known by name without the extension and whichever format is there counts; the product plan's task is accepted when its spec and roadmap, in either format, are written (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: it was approved when both were on the integration branch). When a document is held in both formats the format other than the team's is the one read. Every role's prompt and skills name documents by stem (`docs/catervas/product/spec`), and the prompts Catervas writes itself name the file that is there, or the team's format for a new one; the Architect's plans are `architecture/plans/<epic>` plus the team's extension, and readiness accepts a contract's `plan` in either format. In a contract an agent writes, an owner document in `allowed_paths` is named by a glob such as `docs/catervas/product/spec.*`, which matches either format and the agent version; the product plan's own task names the four files in the team's format.

The format rule (added in 0.108). `catervas_write_folder_doc` writes a path in the team's format. When the same name exists in the other format (`cadence.md` for `cadence.html`), the same folder change removes that file, which is how an agent-only document is rewritten in place; the spec and the roadmap are not, and writing `spec.html` while `spec.md` is there is refused `other_format_exists`, since their rewrite reaches the owner through a task. A path in the other format is written only when that file is already on the integration branch; otherwise it is refused `wrong_format`, its message naming the path in the team's format. In a Markdown team `other_format_exists` says `<existing> is this document: change it there.`. A marketing plan proposed in an HTML team is `MP-<n>.html` and `MP-<n>.agent.html`: `catervas_propose_marketing_plan` wraps `text` and `agent_text` each in a whole page with the viewport line, a `<title>` and `<h1>MP-<n>: <title></h1>`, as it puts `# MP-<n>: <title>` above a Markdown plan; plans already proposed keep their format, and `marketing_plan.proposed` records `format: "html"` (absent for Markdown), and `marketing_plan.get` answers `format`, `markdown` or `html`. No Definition of Done rule holds the format: a task that adds a Markdown document in an HTML team still lands. (One can be added if teams drift.) Catervafication in an HTML team files its documents as `.html`; each artifact criterion asks for `<h1` (`# ` in Markdown) and the architecture overview also `<svg` (a Mermaid block in Markdown).

The server's additions (added in 0.108). `files.tree` lists `.md` and `.html` documents; `files.read` answers `askable`, true when the document is `editable` and not under `docs/catervas/delivery/`; `files.save` accepts `.html`, and its `not_markdown` is `not_a_document`. `GET /documents/raw?path=<path>[&task=<id>][&theme=dark]` answers an `.html` document as `files.read` reads it (the owner's waiting change included), or as the task's branch holds it when `task` names one, else from the task's worktree (a regular file, no link on the way), which is how a marketing plan not yet committed is shown. It needs the session cookie: `403` from another host, `401` without a session, `404` for a path that is not an `.html` file under `docs/catervas/` the branch holds; Markdown is never served here. The answer is `text/html; charset=utf-8` with `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox; default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data:; font-src data:; frame-ancestors 'self'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `X-DNS-Prefetch-Control: off` and `Cache-Control: no-store`, so the document runs no script, reaches no network and cannot read the app's session. Before the document's own styles the route inserts a fit block (after the opening `<head>` tag, else `<html>`, else a doctype, else at the start): the viewport line, `body { margin: 0 auto; padding: 16px; max-width: 72rem; overflow-wrap: anywhere }`, `img, svg, video, canvas { max-width: 100%; height: auto }` and `table, pre { display: block; max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto }`, then the app's page and ink, `html, body { background: #F3E7D3 !important; color: #161616 !important }`, or with `theme=dark` (which the page adds while the app is dark) `#161616` and `#F3E7D3`, so a document that paints its own page still matches the app (changed in 0.126).

Asking for a change and rewriting (added in 0.108). `files.ask_change { path, words }` files, for the role that owns the path's folder, a small whole task "Change <document name>" with `created_by: human`, the owner's trimmed words (1 to 2000 characters) quoted as the owner's, `allowed_paths` the document and its agent version, triaged at once with no triage session as a re-derive is; a change to the spec or the roadmap is a task like any other, accepted by Catervas on its criteria and reaching the owner in a pull request (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061). It refuses, in this order, with `data.errors` as `files.save`: `not_editable` (`/path`), `no_words` (`/words`, "Say what should change."), `no_task_taker` (`/path`: the Scrum Master takes no task and keeps `delivery/` up to date at its retro), `no_owner` (`/path`: the folder's role has no active agent), then `not_editable` for a path `files.tree` does not list. `files.rewrite {}` files, as the owner's word and each triaged at once, one docs task for each role with an active agent whose folder holds a `.md` document found on the integration branch and that can take a task with a reviewer the team can staff, and records `document_rewrite.started { tasks }`. A task is "Rewrite the <role name>'s documents as HTML" (for example "Rewrite the Product Manager's documents as HTML") with `allowed_paths` `<folder>/**`, one `artifact` criterion for each document (`<name>.html` exists and holds `<h1`, the overview also `<svg`) and a `review` rubric: every `.md` named is gone with its agent version, and each `.html` says everything its `.md` said, nothing more. The task commits with `catervas_git_commit` and names each file it replaces in its `removed` list. Marketing plans (`marketing/plans/MP-<n>.*`) are not rewritten, each being the version the owner approved; the spec and the roadmap come back to the owner once. The Scrum Master takes no task: while the team writes HTML, a rewrite has started and `delivery/` still holds a `.md` document, its retro is told "Rewrite the documents in docs/catervas/delivery/ as HTML with catervas_write_folder_doc; writing <name>.html removes <name>.md.". When only the Scrum Master's documents are `.md` the rewrite files no task and still records `document_rewrite.started { tasks: [] }`. It refuses, in this order, `not_html` (the format is Markdown), `rewrite_open` (a task of the last rewrite is neither accepted nor cancelled) and `nothing_to_rewrite` (no task can be filed, and no active Scrum Master's `delivery/` holds a `.md` document). Settings → Work → Documents shows "Rewrite documents as HTML" while the format is HTML and the Files page lists a `.md` document other than a marketing plan, with the refusal's words under it.

The re-derive (added in 0.96). When a folder change the owner made (`folder_doc.edited`) of a human document is integrated, by any of the three policies and after `folder_change.integrated` is recorded, Catervas files the twin's re-derive, unless a task whose `task.created` names `rederives: <twin>` is still `draft`, `refining`, `ready` or `assigned` (one not yet in its worktree, which will hold the owner's change); a change of another document, and an agent's change, file none. It is a whole contract with `created_by: catervas` and `request.triaged { small }` by `catervas` at once: the title `Bring <twin file name> up to date with the owner's change`; the intent `The owner changed <human> on the Files page. Rewrite <twin>, the version written for agents, so that it says what <human> now says.`; the twin in scope and the document out of scope; the requirement R1 and a `review` criterion C1 with the rubric `Every fact, decision and limit in <human> is in <twin>.` and `Nothing in <twin> contradicts <human>.`; the folder's owner as assignee; the reviewer the team's default for that role, else the first of its preferred reviewers (readiness then names a reviewer that is missing, 5.3); risk `low`, the placeholder budget, and `allowed_paths` the twin alone. It is judged as filed whole, as a breakdown's task is, so that no refine session rewrites it (5.16). A filing refused is posted in the channel with its reason; the integration stands.

Attached documents (added in 0.131; ADR 0076; standalone plan `attached-documents`). The owner gives the team a document about the product or the architecture, and it becomes a team document, a pair (above), under `attached/` in the folder of the role that keeps it: `docs/catervas/product/attached/<slug>.md` and its twin `<slug>.agent.md` for `product`, the Product Manager's, and the same under `docs/catervas/architecture/` for `architecture`, the Architect's. `is_human_document` is true of a path directly in either `attached/` folder, `<slug>.md` with a slug of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, and false of its `.agent.md` twin, of a file in a folder below `attached/`, and of any other folder's `attached/`; the twin is the path with `.agent` before its extension, as for every pair. The slug is the file's name without its extension, lowercased, each run of characters outside `a-z0-9` made one `-`, trimmed of `-`, cut to 60 characters and trimmed again, and `document` when nothing is left; a slug whose file or twin the integration branch holds, or a folder change not yet integrated holds, takes `-2`, `-3` and so on. Since it is a pair, the owner's edit of it (`files.save`, above) and its re-derive work as for the spec.

`document.attach { name, kind, data_base64 }` (added in 0.131; ADR 0076; standalone plan `attached-documents`). `name` is the file's name, 1 to 200 characters; `kind` is `product` or `architecture`; `data_base64` is the file in standard base64 with padding, at most 14,000,000 characters. It refuses with -32005 and `data.errors` of `{ path, message, code }`, `path` a JSON pointer, in this order: `no_folder_owner` (`/kind`: no active agent has the folder's role), then, at `/data_base64`, `unreadable` (the base64 does not decode), and the codes of the conversion below. Then, under the integration lock, it commits the text as the owner's own change as `files.save` does, by `tools::folders::land`, with the message `docs(<product|architecture>): attach <slug>.md`, and records `folder_doc.edited` and then `document.attached` (8.5); a change that lands as `files.save`'s do refuses with `file_busy`, `is_a_link` or `change_waiting` at `/name`. It answers `{ path, change }`, and nothing is committed or recorded for a refusal. When the change is integrated (`folder_change.integrated`), the re-derive above files the task that writes the twin, so the folder's agent writes the team's version. Under the lock it first refuses with `documents_switching` at `/name` while the documents are being moved, as `files.save` does (ADR 0074). With the documents kept on this computer (ADR 0074) nothing is committed: the text is written at once at a free path of the folder on disk, a slug whose file or twin is on disk taking `-2`, `-3` and so on, recorded as `local_documents.written` by the owner and then `document.attached`; the task that writes the twin is filed at once, and it answers `{ path, change: null }`. A link in that folder refuses with `is_a_link` at `/name`.

The conversion (added in 0.131; ADR 0076; standalone plan `attached-documents`), in the daemon, of at most 10 MiB of bytes (`too_large` above that, checked after the base64 is decoded). A file starting `%PDF-` is a PDF: its text, page by page, a blank line between pages; a PDF with no text, a scan, is `no_text`, and one that cannot be read, an encrypted one among them, or whose reading fails, is `unreadable`.
