A zip with `word/document.xml` is a Word file: each paragraph a line, a paragraph styled `Title` a `#` heading and `Heading1` to `Heading6` a heading of that level, a numbered or bulleted paragraph a `- ` item, a table one line for each row with its cells joined by ` | `, the text of a paragraph's runs joined, pictures dropped; a zip without that part is `unsupported_type`. Anything else must be UTF-8 and named `.md`, `.markdown` or `.txt`, and is kept as it is; otherwise it is `unsupported_type`. A converted text over the owner's edit limit, 256 KiB, is `too_large`. The media type `document.attached` records is `text/markdown`, `text/plain`, `application/pdf` or `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document`. The refusals are said in the web app in its own words: `attach_unsupported_type` "Catervas reads Markdown, text, PDF and Word files.", `attach_no_text` "This PDF has no text Catervas can read. It may be a scan.", `attach_unreadable` "Catervas could not open this file.", `attach_too_large` "This file is too large. Catervas takes up to 10 MB, and up to 256 KB of text.", `attach_no_folder_owner` "No one on the team keeps these documents. Add a Product Manager or an Architect.", and `attach_too_many` for a sixth document.

Naming attached documents (added in 0.131; ADR 0076; standalone plan `attached-documents`). `request.file`, `chat_message_post` and `message_post` take `attachments`, 1 to 5 paths, and the events they record carry them (8.5). They are held to the same check before anything is recorded: more than five is refused `too_many_attachments` at `/attachments`, and a path that `is_attached_path` does not accept or that no `document.attached` recorded is refused `not_attached` at `/attachments/<i>`, `i` the first path at fault. A command refuses with the reason "<code>: <sentence>" ("A message holds up to five documents.", "Only a document you attached can go with a message."). `chat.messages` and `channel.messages` answer each message's `attachments` as `[{ path, name }]`, left out when there is none. A solo team's request (ADR 0071) carries them on the chat message it files for its agent. `files.read` answers `attached: { name } | null` (4.5).

What the answering session reads (added in 0.131; ADR 0076; standalone plan `attached-documents`). The session that answers the owner's words gets a section "Documents the owner attached", placed after "From the human" and before "This session": for each document in the order the message names, a line with its path in backquotes and, under it, its text in an `untrusted` block named `attached_document` (the untrusted-content rule of the prompt applies to it, since the owner may have pasted a stranger's words). The texts share 64 KiB (`ATTACHED_BYTES`) in that order; a document that does not fit in what is left, or whose text cannot be read, is given as the line "<path>: read it from the folder.". The text is read from the integration branch, else from the branch of the newest folder change not yet integrated whose paths hold it, else not read. The sessions that get the section are the triage, refine and implement sessions of a task whose `task.created` has `attachments`, the `chat` session answering a chat message with `attachments` (the newest message of the owner's), and the `conversation` session a channel post with `attachments` starts (the newest pending post that has any); every other session gets no section.

Starting a Catervafication (added in 0.101; ADR 0051; phase 8 step 07). `catervafication_start` (an empty body) is the owner's order for an existing repository: it files the epic as `human`, asks `draft -> refining` as the first active Product Manager, and the tick then readies it with no session; it records no approval of the click's (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061). It is refused, in this order and with nothing recorded, `catervafication_started` ("your team is already documenting this project, as <epic>"), `catervafication_new_project` ("a new project's Catervafication starts by itself once its product plan's task is accepted"), `catervafication_no_product_manager` ("the team has no active Product Manager to move the epic into its plan; resume one first") and `catervafication_no_writers` ("no one on your team can both write and have their notes checked; add an Architect or a Scrum Master", when the roles have no Product Manager's row; it cannot occur since 0.103, a Product Manager always having its row); two orders at once record one epic. Its answer says "Your team starts documenting the project: <epic>." (changed in 0.116; ADR 0062). The query `catervafication.get` is 4.2's.

The delivery report and the notes' refresh (added in 0.102; ADR 0051; phase 8 step 07b). At each delivery's review the Product Manager writes the delivery's report, for agents, to `docs/catervas/product/reports/D<n>` in the team's format with `catervas_write_folder_doc`, and writes changes to its two human documents (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: it proposed them for the owner's approval); the Architect brings `features`, `jobs` and `structure` up to date in its own session. Both are asked in the review's refreshes (5.9): one session each per delivery, not one per integration. A delivery's report is named "Report for delivery <n>" on Today, in its branch (`docs/report-for-delivery-<n>`) and in its pull request, "Docs: Report for delivery <n>" (changed in 0.122; ADR 0069); `Dx` or a report of no number keeps the plain name.

### 5.18 Goals (added in 0.130; ADR 0075)

The owner gives the team one goal and the team keeps working towards it, round after round, within the daily budget, until the owner marks it reached or ends it. The design is `docs/design/team-goals.md`; the decision is ADR 0075.

**What a goal is.** The owner's words (1 to 300 characters), a target (a number above 0) and its unit (1 to 40 characters), both or neither, and, for a goal with a target, `server`, the connector an active agent has connected and reads the number from, or none, when the owner tells the team. A goal with no target has no readings and is reached only by the owner's word, as every goal is. Its id is `goal-<n>`, counted from 1 in the project's log. One goal stands at a time, active or paused; a second is refused `goal_active`. A goal is events alone (8.5): the standing goal, its readings, its rounds and its status are folded from the log on every read, as deliveries are, with no projection table.

**The owner's commands (4.2).** `goal_set { words, target?, unit?, server? }` is refused, in this order, `goal_active`, `goal_needs_daily_budget` (the team has no daily budget), `goal_target_unit` (one of target and unit without the other), `goal_server_without_target` and `goal_server_not_connected` (no active agent has the server); `goal_edit { goal, words, target?, unit?, server? }` is refused `goal_unknown` for a goal that does not stand and then as `goal_set` but `goal_active`, and records `goal.set` again with the same id, keeping the readings and the rounds; `goal_pause { goal }` is refused `goal_unknown` and `goal_already_paused`; `goal_resume { goal }` is refused `goal_unknown` and, on a goal that is not paused, is Keep going; `goal_end { goal, outcome }` ends it `reached` or `dropped`, and only this marks a goal reached; `goal_report { goal, value }` records the owner's number and is refused `goal_unknown`, `goal_not_measured` (no target) and `goal_value` (below 0 or not finite). Each refusal is `<code>: <words>`. The query `goal.get` answers the standing goal with its status (`active`, `paused`, `met`, `stalled`, with `stall` `nothing_planned` or `no_progress`), its readings newest first (at most 10), `reader`, `planner`, `open`, `done`, `waiting_on_owner` and `planning`, and the last goal ended.

**Status and progress.** The status is the first that holds: `paused`; `met` (the latest reading is at or above the target; the owner decides whether the goal is reached); stalled because the last round filed nothing and nothing new has come in since; stalled because `GOAL_ROUNDS_BEFORE_CHECK_IN` (5) rounds that filed work have passed with no progress; else `active`. Progress is the owner's word (a `goal.set`, a `goal.resumed` or a `goal.measured` from the owner) or a reading above every earlier one, the first reading counting. A round is one `goal.planned`; a reading's day is its UTC date, as the daily budget's day is.

**The planning rule.** The last rule of a tick, after every rule that has work, and run only under every rule in a tick about no one task. The planner, the active Product Manager or, in one agent alone, that agent, gets one `goal` session when: a goal stands and is not paused; the team has a daily budget and today's is not spent; the planner is awake and has no session running; a new project's product plan is not awaited; the board is quiet, no task in any status but `accepted` and `cancelled` (accepted work waiting for the owner's merge does not hold a round); the goal is not met; and it is not stalled. The session is about no task, runs read-only on the read tier in the project's root with its agent's connectors, on the agent's own model and effort, and is offered the reading tools, `catervas_post_message`, `catervas_write_memory`, `catervas_file_goal_work` and `catervas_record_goal_progress`. Its first message holds the goal's words, number and unit, the last five readings with their source and age, who reads the number and from which service (and, when the planner is the reader, to read it first and record it), each earlier round's tasks with where they stand, the accepted tasks waiting for a merge, in one agent alone that each step it files is its own task and small, and the method: read the progress and what earlier rounds did; pick one to five steps that move the number or build what the goal names; prefer what the team can finish; never repeat what is done or under way; name a step that needs a service the team lacks as a request for that connection; and, when nothing sensible is left, file nothing and say why in one post. When the session ends Catervas records `goal.planned { goal, filed }` with each `task.created` that has the goal since the session started, unless it ended `aborted` (a stop, or another session's cost spending the day), `provider_limit` or `credential_refused`, which is no round, so the next tick with room plans again; a session that ended at a limit or with an error counts as a round.

**The measuring rule.** After the planning rule, once per UTC day, the first active agent in team order that has the goal's `server` connected (the reader) gets one `goal` session, offered `catervas_record_goal_progress` alone, when the goal stands, is not paused and has a server, no connector reading is recorded today, the reader has started no `goal` session today, the day is not spent and the reader is free. It does not wait for a quiet board. When the reader is also the planner its planning session reads first, so one session does both that day. Catervas calls no service itself.

**The tools.** Both are tier `read` and offered in a `goal` session alone. `catervas_file_goal_work { title, request, size }` (`size` `large` or `small`; title 3 to 120 and request 20 to 2,000 characters) is refused `goal_session_only`, `goal_none` (no goal stands, or it is paused), `goal_work_limit` (`GOAL_WORK_PER_SESSION`, 5, filed by the session) and `goal_large_in_solo`; in a team it files a draft request from the title and request with `goal` on its `task.created` and triaged at its filing (5.16), and in one agent alone a small task given to the caller; it answers `{ task_id, status: draft, left }`. `catervas_record_goal_progress { value, note? }` is refused `goal_session_only`, `goal_none`, `goal_not_measured` (no target or no server), `goal_not_your_service` (the caller has not connected the goal's server) and `goal_value`, and records `goal.measured { source: connector, server }` by the caller in its session; it answers `{ goal, value }`.

**Outward acts and money are unchanged.** A post outside the marketing plan, a paid connector call and a purchase still ask the owner, Catervas opens pull requests and merges only where the owner allowed it (ADR 0073), and the marketing budget's hard stop holds (5.5, 5.6, 6.5). The goal adds no budget (5.5). Ending or reaching a goal cancels nothing: the work already filed carries on, and the owner cancels any they no longer want on the board.
Documents kept on this computer (added in 0.129; ADR 0074; `docs/design/local-documents.md`). `policy.documents_local` (5.12) with the log's newest `document_storage.changed` gives four modes, `team.get`'s `documents_mode`: `committed`, `taking_out` (on, its pull request not merged), `local` (on, out of the repository) and `putting_back` (off, its pull request not merged). In `local` and `putting_back` every reader reads the root checkout's `docs/catervas/` from disk, with a blob that is git's object id of the file's bytes, so `files.save`'s `base` keeps its meaning; in `taking_out` and `putting_back` nothing is written: `files.save` and `catervas_write_folder_doc` are refused `documents_switching` and `folder_doc_switching`, and rule 7 passes over a task whose `allowed_paths` reach `docs/catervas/`. `documents.set_local { local }` answers `{ mode, change }` and is refused at `/local`, in this order, `project_folder`, `documents_switching`, `documents_in_flight` (naming the tasks), `change_waiting`, `documents_busy` and `is_a_link`; the same value as now changes nothing. In `local` mode a save, `catervas_write_folder_doc` and a task's landing write the file whole or not at all, refuse a link on the way, and record `local_documents.written { paths, removed, by, written_by, task_id, set_aside }`; the owner's save of a human document files its twin's re-derive at once. A task's worktree gets a copy of the folder (links not followed) and a start copy under `.catervas/local/documents/start/<task-id>/`, once; the Product Manager's docs task "reaches `verifying` only with a commit" except in a mode that reads the disk. The last change of a document is the newest `local_documents.written` naming it, and a twin is stale when the newest write naming its human document is newer than the newest naming it; an edit made outside Catervas is seen by neither. The Team rules gain one line after the documents line in `local` and `putting_back`: "- documents kept on this computer: docs/catervas/ is not in git. Grep and Glob skip it: find its files with LS and read them with Read. Never commit them; catervas_git_commit refuses them. Your changes to them reach the team when your task is accepted."

**Under autopilot (added in 0.138; ADR 0082).** A stalled goal is flagged for the owner on Today, in "Flagged by the team" with the planning round's words, not asked: the goal card still shows its words and its "Keep going", and the owner may use them. Nothing else about goals changes, and the team never files work for an idle agent.

## 6. Launch roles

Each role ships as a directory under `roles/<role>/` with `role.yaml` (mandate, what the role produces, what it may not do, its default model and effort, and the skills it ships with), `system.md` (the prompt), and a `skills/` folder holding one `<skill-name>/SKILL.md` per skill in the Agent Skills format. A role's permission tiers and session limits are not in `role.yaml`: they are the governor's defaults (5.6, 5.5), which the team file overrides per agent (`grants`, `revokes`, `budgets.session`), and an agent's own `model` in the team file overrides the role's default model and effort. A copy in the role file that the governor did not read would be one a user edited expecting an effect (added in 0.8). The user can edit all of it. A role's skills are written into the prompt of every session of the role (ADR 0011). The user can also give one agent, or the whole team, a skill of their own (added in 0.40; 6.7, ADR 0034): the team's lives in `.catervas/skills/<name>/` and one agent's in `.catervas/agents/<agent_id>/skills/<name>/`, and a name resolves agent, then team, then role, a team or agent skill replacing a shipped skill of its name only when the person said so.

### 6.1 Product Manager

Mandate: own the backlog, translate every request from the user into a contract, an epic or a standalone task as the triage sized it, after asking the user its questions (5.16), accept a code task's work against its contract (a task that changes no code is accepted by Catervas on its criteria, 5.4; changed in 0.115; ADR 0061), keep the product pointed at a user need. The PM is the source of exit criteria and, for code, the last non-human gate. The PM writes the tasks of every ready epic, from the Architect's plan when the team has an Architect (5.16 item 3; changed in 0.98). When the team has no Scrum Master, the PM also triages requests and assigns tasks.

Produces: epic contracts and standalone task contracts, the task contracts under an approved epic, from the Architect's plan (added in 0.98), the questions it asks the user, product decisions, release scope, and its folder `docs/catervas/product/`: the product's `spec` and `roadmap`, each with its agent version, and its delivery reports (changed in 0.91; 5.17), and `CHANGELOG.md` (added in 0.93, on the founder's decision of 2026-10-10, "PM owns CHANGELOG"): each time a delivery closes, Catervas files a docs task of its whose `allowed_paths` name `CHANGELOG.md`, and it adds in it what the delivery's accepted tasks changed, in the user's words, since a review writes nothing itself (`no_task_no_write`, 5.6; changed in 0.116; ADR 0062). The task is a whole contract filed in the tick that records `delivery.closed` (5.9), as `owner_change` is, with `filed_as: changelog` and no refine session: titled `Add delivery <n> to the changelog`, for the Product Manager, reviewed by the role `reviewer_for` names (the field is filled and never runs, since only code is reviewed, 5.1), risk `low`, the placeholder budget, `allowed_paths` `CHANGELOG.md` alone, its intent listing each task of the delivery as `CTV-<n>: <title>`, and two criteria Catervas runs itself, so that Catervas accepts it alone (5.4): an `artifact` check that `CHANGELOG.md` exists and a `command` check that `grep -qi 'delivery <n>' CHANGELOG.md` finds the delivery. It is not filed when the team has no active Product Manager, and the delivery closes all the same; a changelog task never counts towards a delivery (3).

New project (added in 0.99; ADR 0051; phase 8 step 06). For a project started in Catervas the Product Manager interviews the owner in its one-to-one chat before anything else is planned (4.3), and then writes the product plan, `spec` and `roadmap` with their agent versions, in the docs task the owner's word files for it (5.16), which Catervas accepts on its criteria; nobody approves the plan (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061).

Cannot: write application code, which only the Software Developer and the UI/UX Designer do (changed in 0.31), and the DevOps Engineer in an incident's fix (6.9; changed in 0.32); work a task outside the team's `document_paths` (5.3; added in 0.11); write product documents for an epic that is not ready; run the test suite as a reviewer of its own contracts; accept a task without a reviewer's verification event.

Default tools: read, network (for competitor and docs research), write_workspace and git_local (added in 0.92, for the docs tasks of its folder: it writes only documents, within the contract's `allowed_paths`, on `docs/CTV-<n>`, and no agent reviews it: Catervas accepts it on its criteria, 5.4; changed in 0.115; ADR 0061, which also removed the owner's acceptance of a docs task whose `allowed_paths` may change `spec` or `roadmap`, added in 0.95), the task and decision tools. The decision tools are `catervas_write_decision`, which the Product Manager and the Architect alone may call, and `catervas_read_decisions`, which every agent may (5.8; added in 0.16). Default model: the strongest available, since contract quality is leverage on everything downstream.

Kit (added in 0.46; 6.7): five skills, `asking-the-right-questions`, `writing-requirements`, `prioritising-the-backlog`, `scoping-a-release` and `using-product-sources`, and four services: Amplitude, Linear and Notion, which it only reads, and GitHub, which it reads for issues and an organisation's project boards and writes to, an issue or a comment, only after the human allows that call (changed in 0.65; ADR 0044).

Data pipelines (added in 0.76; phase 7 step 10e; changed in 0.115; ADR 0061). The Product Manager no longer decides the Procurement Specialist's requests for a data source (6.10): Catervas files a free one that sends no data out at once, and passes one that costs money, whose cost is not known or that sends the project's data out to the owner at once. The decision session, `catervas_decide_data_pipeline` and the skill `deciding-data-pipelines` are gone.

Kit (added in 0.101; ADR 0051; phase 8 step 07): the kit's seventh skill, `catervafying-the-repository`, written for the Product Manager's Catervafication task: write the product plan from the project (`spec` and `roadmap`, each with its agent version in the same commit), each fact with where it was read, and, at a delivery's review, write the plan's changes with `catervas_write_folder_doc` (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: it proposed them for the owner's approval). Documents are named by stem, without an extension, and written in the team's format (changed in 0.108).

The goal (added in 0.130; ADR 0075). The Product Manager, or the one agent in one agent alone, is the planner of the owner's goal (5.18): it gets a `goal` session whenever the board is quiet and files the next one to five steps with `catervas_file_goal_work`. The kit gains the skill `working-towards-the-goal`, listed before `catervafying-the-repository`, which teaches it to read the progress, pick and size the steps, never file again what is done, ask for a connection the work needs and file nothing when nothing sensible is left; the kit has seven skills in all. A task the planner's agent files in one agent alone is refined by that agent, told "<Name>, you filed this task working towards the owner's goal “<words>”, and you write its contract yourself".

### 6.2 Scrum Master

Mandate: keep work flowing and keep the human informed. Triages every request from the user as large or small (5.16), in a session of its own on the cheaper model whatever its own, given the triage tool alone (added in 0.10). Does not break an epic down (changed in 0.98): the Architect plans it in lanes and the Product Manager writes its tasks. Assigns each ready task to the appropriate agent, every task of a lane to that lane's builder (5.2). Runs each delivery's review and retro, one session each, and the Product Manager runs them when the team has no active Scrum Master (5.9; changed in 0.15; changed in 0.116). Posts the escalation digest in each delivery's review (5.7; changed in 0.116; ADR 0062). Appends what the retro learned to `team/retro.md` (5.8; added in 0.15). Enforces WIP limits (default: one unfinished task per agent, counted as 5.2 says: a task the agent holds that is under way and not stuck; changed in 0.116). Judges no contract: the judgment of 0.10 is gone (5.3; changed in 0.115; ADR 0061). Is assigned the ready epics, which Catervas verifies itself (5.16; added in 0.10; changed in 0.115). Owns escalation hygiene.

Produces: triage decisions, assignments, the tasks an epic's close-out asks for (changed in 0.98), review summaries, retro notes, escalation digests; its folder `docs/catervas/delivery/` (the team's cadence and ceremony notes; added in 0.91, 5.17), which it has no tool to write until step 03 of phase 8.

Cannot: change an epic's requirements or contract; change a frozen contract; write application code, which only the Software Developer and the UI/UX Designer do (changed in 0.31), and the DevOps Engineer in an incident's fix (6.9; changed in 0.32); work a task outside the team's `document_paths` (5.3); accept work (changed in 0.11).

Default tools: read, the board tools, the triage tool, the retro tool (added in 0.15), and the contract tools for the tasks an epic's close-out asks for. Runs on a mid-tier model; its work is coordination, not deep reasoning.

Kit (added in 0.46; 6.7): two skills, `running-ceremonies` and `writing-escalation-digests`, and no service (changed in 0.116; ADR 0062: the planning skill is gone). The chat bridge is planned in the last phase.

Kit (added in 0.101; ADR 0051; phase 8 step 07): the kit's fourth skill, `catervafying-the-repository`, listed last. It is for the retro of the delivery that documented the project: the Scrum Master writes the team's cadence to `docs/catervas/delivery/cadence` with `catervas_write_folder_doc` and keeps it true at each retro. It has no task of its own. Documents are named by stem, without an extension, and written in the team's format (changed in 0.108).

### 6.3 Architect

Mandate: hold the shape of the system. Writes architecture decision records, sets constraints that go into contracts (allowed paths, patterns to follow), and reviews the developer's diffs for design, writing the review note. An Architect's task is a document: it runs no spikes, and it does not write application code, which only the Developer and the UI/UX Designer do (changed in 0.10, and in 0.31 for the Designer, from the founder's decision of 2026-09-24). Its tasks are held to the team's `document_paths` and work on `docs/CTV-<n>` (5.3, 5.14; added in 0.11). It also helps build (added in 0.132; ADR 0077): when a Software Developer's task is `ready` and no active Software Developer has room for it (its lane's builder included, 5.16 item 3), rule 8 offers it to the active Architects with room, and the assigner may assign it to one. The task stays the Developer's: its branch, its criteria, its review and its lane follow the contract's `assignee_role`. The Architect's `implement` session on it is given the Software Developer's instructions and kit skills, and `git_remote` when the team's `push` is on, as a Developer's would be; every other session of the Architect's is its own. It cannot review its own work, so its reviewer is another Architect or a Software Developer, which the assignment gate accepts for that task alone (`may_build`, `may_review`). A hand-over (5.2) stays within the contract's role.

Produces: ADRs, design notes attached to contracts, review notes, an approved epic's implementation plan in lanes, written in the docs task the Product Manager files for it (added in 0.98; 5.16 item 3); its folder `docs/catervas/architecture/` (added in 0.91, 5.17): `overview` with diagrams, `features`, `jobs` (the cron and scheduled work found in code, CI and config), `structure` and `plans/<epic-id>`, each in the team's format (5.17).

Cannot: write application code in its own tasks, merge or push a shared branch, accept work (changed in 0.10, and in 0.132 for the Developer's tasks it builds).

Default tools: read, write_workspace, execute, network, git_local, so that it commits the documents that are its work (changed in 0.10). It records its decisions under `.catervas/decisions/` with `catervas_write_decision`, which the Product Manager and the Architect alone may call, and reads them with `catervas_read_decisions` (5.8; added in 0.16).

Kit (added in 0.47; 6.7): six skills (changed in 0.98), `designing-apis-and-data`, `reviewing-dependencies`, `security-review`, `setting-performance-budgets`, `using-architecture-sources` and `planning-in-lanes`, and four services it only reads: Context7 (library documentation), Grep (public code search), OSV (known flaws in packages) and GitHub (the code and pull requests of the user's own repositories, private ones included, reached with a key the user pastes until Catervas Cloud runs (phase 11) and by a sign-in through Catervas Cloud with Catervas's GitHub App from then; changed in 0.65, ADR 0044).

Kit (added in 0.101; ADR 0051; phase 8 step 07): the kit's seventh skill, `catervafying-the-repository`, listed last: the Architect documents how the project is put together (`overview` with a diagram, `features`, `jobs`, `structure`) from the code and its configuration, each fact with where it was read, and brings the last three up to date at each delivery's review. Documents are named by stem, without an extension, and written in the team's format (changed in 0.108).

### 6.4 Software Developer

Mandate: implement contracts. With the UI/UX Designer, the only role that writes application code, beside the DevOps Engineer's incident fixes (6.9) (added in 0.11; changed in 0.31 and 0.32). Works on a task branch, `feature/CTV-<n>` or `fix/CTV-<n>` by the contract's `change` (5.14; changed in 0.11), runs the exit criteria before declaring done, writes a completion note.

Produces: diffs, commits on task branches, completion notes; its folder `docs/catervas/engineering/` (added in 0.91, 5.17): `conventions` and `workflow`, each rule with the evidence it was read from.

Cannot: modify contracts, accept work, push to shared branches without the `git_remote` grant, touch files outside allowed paths.

Default tools: read, write_workspace, execute, git_local. The developer runs the project's own tooling; Catervas does not reimplement a coding agent. See section 8.

Kit (added in 0.48; 6.7): six skills, `test-driven-development`, `debugging`, `safe-migrations`, `testing-per-stack`, `answering-a-review` and `using-docs-and-the-browser`, and one service it only reads, Context7 (library documentation), the Architect's entry with its own `why`, signed in to by route 1. Its browser is the built-in Playwright of the UI/UX Designer's kit (6.7), off unless the user turns it on for the Developer on its page; it opens the task's preview and nothing else, in the Developer's `explore` and `implement` sessions, and a Developer's `verify` session is not given it. The Developer holds `network` since 0.115 (ADR 0061: every role does) and so searches and fetches the web in its sessions; Context7 is still its documentation lookup, its `query` and `libraryName` are words the agent writes, sent to Context7 (Upstash), each call recorded as `tool.called`, and they are not tagged `external_effect` or `paid`, so no documentation lookup waits for approval. A development database and deploy status are not in this kit: the database a task uses runs in the sandbox or the preview, which a host server cannot reach, and deploy status is the DevOps Engineer's (6.9).

Kit (added in 0.101; ADR 0051; phase 8 step 07): the kit's seventh and eighth skills, `catervafying-the-repository` and `catervas-recommended-workflow`. The first has the Developer write `conventions` and `workflow` from the evidence (the lint and format configuration, the test layout, the last fifty commits' messages and branch names, the continuous integration files and a contributing guide), each rule with where it was read, and say at the top of `workflow` whether it records the project's own process or adopts Catervas's recommended workflow, which it must do when the project has no documented process, no CI that runs tests and no consistent commit style. The second is that workflow: brainstorm, plan, test first, verify, review and Conventional Commits. Documents are named by stem, without an extension, and written in the team's format (changed in 0.108).

Bug hunt (added in 0.117; ADR 0063). In an existing repository's Catervafication the Developer hunts once for bugs in the code (5.16): it reads the code, runs the project's tests and checks in the sandbox, changes no code, files each bug it finds with `catervas_file_bug` (its input, limits, refusals `bug_refused`, `bug_out_of_bounds`, `hunt_bug_limit` and `bug_already_filed`, and answer are 5.16's) and writes its report, `docs/catervas/engineering/bug-hunt`. The `catervafying-the-repository` skill says how. No agent reviews a hunt. It also takes work its role does from its chat with `catervas_take_task` (4.3).

### 6.5 Marketing Specialist

Mandate: own the business's marketing (changed in 0.52 on the founder's decision of 2026-10-05, ADR 0042; `docs/design/marketing-specialist.md`; built in phase 7 steps 08b to 08f). It owns four things: the brand kit, the brand persona, the marketing plan, and the social presence on the business's channels. It researches the market, the audience, competitors, the words customers search for and what each channel costs, to decide the best plan; writes the plan with its budget, which the owner approves when it spends money (a plan that spends nothing is approved by Catervas at once; changed in 0.115; ADR 0061); posts on the business's social channels and runs its search ads as the plan says; and still writes release notes, landing and README copy and positioning, and synthesizes user feedback the user pastes in (the research and the plan added in 0.10).

It reads no member repository (added in 0.114; ADR 0057; phase 9 step 03). In a project folder its read roots (5.6) are none: it reads the Product Manager's and its own folders of the project folder, as before, and no other member's files.

Produces: files under the team's `document_paths` (default `docs/**`, `**/*.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md`; changed in 0.11), among them the brand kit (`docs/catervas/marketing/brand/brand-kit` and its files under `docs/catervas/marketing/brand/assets/`), the brand persona (`docs/catervas/marketing/brand/persona`), each marketing plan (`docs/catervas/marketing/plans/MP-<n>.md` or `.html` for people and `MP-<n>.agent.md` or `.agent.html` for agents, in the team's format when proposed; added in 0.91) and its research (`docs/catervas/marketing/research/`); positioning decisions; the posts Catervas sends for it; the Google Ads campaigns it runs for an approved plan; customer-facing release notes and announcements, and README copy, are documents in its folder, written from the Product Manager's roadmap and delivery reports (added in 0.93), and `CHANGELOG.md` is the Product Manager's, because Claude Code's `Edit`, and its `Write` over a file that exists, need a `Read` of that file first and the Marketing Specialist's reading is held to two folders (5.6). The folder is the Marketing Specialist's (5.17; moved from `docs/marketing/` in 0.91): while it has an active agent, another role's task may not reach it in its allowed paths (5.3; added in 0.52); every agent may read them, and the UI/UX Designer takes the project's colours and voice from the brand kit.

Cannot: change application code, which only the Software Developer and the UI/UX Designer do (changed in 0.31), and the DevOps Engineer in an incident's fix (6.9; changed in 0.32); work a task outside the team's `document_paths` (5.3); spend money but through an approved plan, within its budget, or a call the owner allows (a `paid` one); delete a post, an email or a campaign; change billing, account access or conversion tracking at any service (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: it may publish or send what is free, a post outside the plan going out with a Stop, and it reads the whole project, where it was held to `docs/catervas/product/` and its own folder from 0.93).

Its marketing plan (added in 0.52; ADR 0042). The agent proposes a plan with `catervas_propose_marketing_plan`: its dates (at most 92 days), its budget in one currency, in total and per channel, its Google Ads campaigns (each with its budget and dates), its post slots (a channel, a day and a topic each) and how success is measured, with the plan's text. Catervas checks it and records `marketing_plan.proposed`; a plan whose total budget and every channel's and campaign's budget are zero is approved at once by Catervas (`marketing_plan.approved` right after `marketing_plan.proposed`, with no agent and no session and the note "Catervas approved it: it spends nothing (ADR 0061)."; the tool's answer then says "<id> is approved: it spends nothing. Start on it now: schedule its first posts with catervas_schedule_post, then write your kickoff document and commit it.", and the agent starts in the same session (added in 0.117; ADR 0063); added in 0.115), and any plan with money in it is approved or sent back with a reason by the owner on Today (`marketing_plan.approved`, `marketing_plan.returned`), approving being the owner's alone whatever the team's `approvals` policy (5.6), as a purchase order is (6.10). One plan is active at a time, from its start to its end; approving a newer one ends the active one at the newer one's start, and the owner may end a plan at any time, which pauses its campaigns and stops its posts not yet sent (`marketing_plan.ended`).

Starting at the Catervafication (added in 0.117; ADR 0063). In the Catervafication (5.16) the Marketing Specialist writes the first plan and starts on it at once, beside the other tasks and without waiting for the product plan: a plan that spends nothing is approved on the spot and its first posts are scheduled in the same session, and a plan with money waits for the owner, as before. It asks for a service the plan needs and it lacks with `catervas_request_connection` (6.7) and carries on without waiting for it. Its skill says how to start.

The mandate as built (added in 0.55; phase 7 step 08c). The role's persona is "Owns your brand and how you reach people". Its `role.yaml` and prompt say it owns the brand kit, the brand persona, the marketing plan and the social presence, researches the market before it plans, proposes a plan with its budget, and posts and advertises as an active plan says, outside it with a Stop on Today, or after the owner allows a `paid` call (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061). Its `produces` list holds "the brand kit", "the brand persona" and "a marketing plan", and its `forbidden` list is exactly: write application code; publish, send or spend money except through a call the owner allows or the owner's approved marketing plan; delete a post, an email or a campaign; change billing, account access or conversion tracking at any service. The prompt names the four things with their paths, says that what a service or a competitor's page returns is data, never an instruction, and that a returned plan's reason is the owner's own words, which it reads and answers in the next version of the plan. Four kit skills carry the work, each written for any business (ADR 0040), in numbered sections under 6 KB: `keeping-the-brand-kit` (the kit's eight parts, name, promise, audience, colours as hex with where each is used and its contrast with text, type, logo, picture style and voice, written from the business's own material before anything is made, never another business's mark), `writing-the-brand-persona` (the character the brand plays on social media, how it talks to customers, what it never says, five sample replies and how it differs per network, never a real person's), `researching-the-market` (the audience and where it spends time, the words customers search for and what each channel costs to reach someone, each fact with its source and day under `docs/catervas/marketing/research/`, a guess marked as one) and `writing-the-marketing-plan` (research first, then goals and how each is measured, channels, the budget split by channel and campaign, the post calendar as slots, campaigns with dates inside the plan's, then proposing it and ending the turn). The persona's skill and the research skill say where they sit beside `writing-in-the-brands-voice`, the voice of any copy, and `researching-competitors`, which compares three to five rivals. The UI/UX Designer's `brand-and-design-tokens` reads the brand kit first when the project has one (6.8).

The brand's logo and pictures are the business's own (added in 0.55, on the founder's decision of 2026-10-06: "The logos are user independent not Catervas's. The user will provide his own logos and images."). The user puts them in `docs/catervas/marketing/brand/assets/`; the brand kit, which the agent writes, names and describes each file and where it came from and when; and when one the kit needs is missing, the agent asks the user for it with `catervas_ask_human`. The agent never makes a logo and never puts a generated picture in place of the brand's own, and Catervas has no tool that copies a generated picture into the brand kit. The pictures and clips the agent makes with its creative services (6.7) stay at those services, for a post or a page that uses them.

Proposing a plan (added in 0.55). `catervas_propose_marketing_plan`, of the `write_workspace` tier, is offered only to a Marketing Specialist's `implement` session about a task, and refused to anyone else with `marketing_plan_refused`. Its input is `title`, `summary`, `text`, `agent_text` (the plan written for agents; added in 0.91), `starts_on`, `ends_on`, `currency`, `budget { total, google_ads }`, `campaigns` (0 to 10, each `{ key, channel, name, goal, advertises, budget, starts_on, ends_on }`; `advertises` added in 0.72), `posts` (0 to 200, each `{ key, channel, on, topic }`), `measures`, and two fields the first design left open: `google_ads_account` (`NNN-NNN-NNNN`, which a plan with campaigns needs and one without them refuses) and `replaces`, the id of an approved plan still in force that the new one supersedes. Every amount is a decimal string of at most eight digits and at most two decimals, compared in hundredths and never as a float. Catervas checks the plan and answers every fault at once, each with its code and field: `marketing_plan_text` (a title of 3 to 100 characters, a summary of 20 to 600 and a text of 200 to 16,000, trimmed, and, field `agent_text`, an agent text of 200 to 16,000, trimmed; added in 0.91, checked in the tool beside the plan's checks); `marketing_plan_dates` (`starts_on` no earlier than yesterday's UTC date, so an owner west of UTC is not refused their own today, and `ends_on` not before it and at most 92 days later, both days counted); `marketing_plan_currency` (three capital letters, and, for a plan that replaces another, the other's currency: the campaigns Catervas made for the old plan hold its amounts in it, so a plan in another currency replaces nothing and is proposed once the old one has ended; amended in 0.68, from step 08f's landing review); `marketing_plan_budget` (Google Ads at most the total, and the campaigns' budgets adding up to at most Google Ads'); `marketing_plan_campaign` (each of channel `google_ads`, a name of 1 to 100 characters, a goal of 1 to 300, what it advertises, the product, service or offer, of 3 to 200 characters trimmed (`advertises`; added in 0.72), a budget above 0 and dates inside the plan's); `marketing_plan_post` (each of one of eleven channels, `instagram`, `x`, `facebook`, `linkedin`, `threads`, `bluesky`, `tiktok`, `pinterest`, `youtube`, `google_business` and `mastodon`, on a day inside the plan's, with a topic of 1 to 200 characters); `marketing_plan_key` (every campaign's and post's key is lower-case words joined by `-`, at most 40 characters, and unique across the plan); `marketing_plan_measures` (1 to 10, of 3 to 200 characters each); `google_ads_account_needed`; and `marketing_plan_unknown` for a `replaces` that names no approved plan in force. A plan whose dates, amounts or channels cannot be read is answered with those faults alone, since the checks after them would be guesses, and a task with a plan waiting already is refused `marketing_plan_waiting` before anything else is checked. The plan's number is `MP-<n>`, one more than the highest of the log's plans and of the `MP-<n>` files, `.md` or `.html`, in `docs/catervas/marketing/plans/` of the project's root and of the task's worktree, taken under one lock, so a fresh clone never reuses a committed number. Catervas writes the text, under the heading `# MP-<n>: <title>` (in an HTML team as a whole page, 5.17), to `docs/catervas/marketing/plans/MP-<n>.md` (`.html` in an HTML team) in the task's worktree (`marketing_plan_file_exists` when it is there) and the agent text, under the same heading, to `docs/catervas/marketing/plans/MP-<n>.agent.md` (`.agent.html`) beside it (added in 0.91; `marketing_plan_file_exists` when that is there, and then the plan's own file is removed before the refusal returns, as both are when the event is refused), after the permission check of both paths, which is why the daemon's hook judges a Catervas tool of the `write_workspace` tier by the path its input names and the contract must allow it (`path_outside_allowed` otherwise). It records `marketing_plan.proposed`, whose `text` is the plan for people alone, since the owner reads that version, and answers the plan's id and that the agent is to end its turn: the owner's decision starts the next session, as a question's answer does (5.7).

The owner's decision (added in 0.55). Only the owner decides, under `ask` and `auto` alike (ADR 0041), with the commands `marketing_plan_decide { plan, decision, note? }`, `decision` `approve` or `return`, and `marketing_plan_end { plan, note? }`, which arrive only on `POST /command` behind the daemon's token or the browser's `command` behind its cookie, as `tool_approve` does (ADR 0031, 8.6), and never from an agent's session. `note` is at most 600 characters; it is the reason, and required, for `return` (`marketing_plan_reason_needed`), and optional for the rest. The refusals are `unknown_marketing_plan`, `marketing_plan_decided` (decided before), `marketing_plan_expired` (approving a plan whose `ends_on` is past), `marketing_plan_not_approved` (ending one that was never approved) and `marketing_plan_ended`. A plan whose task was cancelled may still be approved, since the plan does not depend on its task. The check and the write are one step under one lock, `PLANS`, which the owner's decision, the owner's end and the dated ends all hold, and every end goes through one function that reads the plans again under it and records nothing for a plan already ended, so two ends at once record one. `marketing_plan.approved { plan, note }` and `marketing_plan.returned { plan, reason }` (8.5) carry the proposing task on their envelope and no agent or session; the store reads one that names either as deciding nothing, as it reads a connector call's decision, and an end that names either likewise. The decision lowers the task's `open_plans` (5.7), and the next session is told it as the owner's own words (5.7). One plan is active at a time: among the approved plans not ended, the one approved last whose first and last day hold today, in UTC. Approving a plan ends, in the same step and with `marketing_plan.ended { why: replaced, replaced_by }`, every approved plan not ended that starts on or after the new one's first day; one that started earlier ends on the new one's first day, by the rule below, and a plan that is ended before its first day replaces nothing. A plan whose last day has passed ends `expired`. Those two dated ends are made by a rule with no model, `end_marketing_plans`, which every tick whose scope names no task runs first, before its pause check, so that it also runs while the team is paused, starts no session and does not use up the tick. The owner ends an approved plan at any time (`why: by_owner`). Ending a plan records its event and, in the same step, stops its posts as Posts below says (added in 0.57); pausing its campaigns comes with Google Ads (08f), which extends the one function that records an end.

Where the owner sees a plan (added in 0.55). The queries `marketing_plan.list {}`, every plan newest first with its `plan`, `title`, `state` (`proposed`, `returned`, `approved`, `active` or `ended`), dates, `currency`, `total`, `agent_id`, `task_id` and `proposed_at`, and `marketing_plan.get { plan }`, the proposal whole with its state, the owner's decision with their words and time, and the end with its `why`, the owner's note when they ended it with one, and the plan that replaced it when a newer plan did, and `not_found` for a plan nobody proposed, both read the log; `waiting.list` gives the row of 5.7 (a plan whose task is not on the board has no row). On Today the row "Marketing plan to approve: <title>" shows the agent's picture and name, the summary, the total budget with its currency, the dates, and "Review", which opens the plan's page at `/marketing/plans/MP-<n>`; a row of a kind the page does not know is skipped, never an error. The page shows the summary first, the budget as a table by channel and campaign, the post calendar by week, the measures, and the plan's text as text, never rendered as markup; while the plan waits, "Approve" and "Send back", whose reason is required and at most 600 characters; while it is approved or active, "End the plan", with an optional note and a confirmation that says what ending does; and once it is decided, who decided it, when, and their words; an ended plan says how it ended, quoting the owner's note when they ended it with one and linking the plan that replaced it when a newer plan did. It shows each campaign's `advertises` and price and, once Catervas's watch has read the spend, the spend against the budget and the pauses (below; changed in 0.72). What its posts have done is shown slot by slot under the calendar (added in 0.57; Posts, below). The command line is `catervas marketing plan show [<plan>] [--json]`, which reads the log and lists the plans or shows one whole, `catervas marketing plan approve <plan> [--note <text>]`, `catervas marketing plan return <plan> --reason <text>` and `catervas marketing plan end <plan> [--note <text>]`, which send the decision to the daemon when one drives the project and make it in the process otherwise (section 3, ADR 0014).

Posts (added in 0.52; as built in 0.57, phase 7 step 08d, ADR 0042). The agent writes a post with `catervas_schedule_post` and never calls a posting service's write tool itself: Buffer's `create_post` and `edit_post` are `denied` to it (6.7), and Catervas makes the call itself, one hour before the post's time, with the connection of the agent that wrote it. The tool, of the `read` tier since what governs it is the plan and the owner, is offered only to a Marketing Specialist's `implement` session about a task, and is `post_refused` from any other. Its input is `channel` (one of the plan's eleven), `buffer_channel` (Buffer's id for the channel, which the agent reads with Buffer's `list_channels`; `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$`), `text`, `media` (at most four `{ url, kind }`, `kind` `image` or `video`), `at`, `details?` and `slot?`. Catervas checks it in this order and answers the first fault with its code: `post_channel_unknown`, `post_buffer_channel_invalid`, `post_too_long` (1 character to the network's limit, counted in Unicode scalar values, with no NUL: x 280, bluesky 300, threads 500, mastodon 500, pinterest 500, google_business 1,500, instagram 2,200, tiktok 2,200, linkedin 3,000, youtube 5,000, facebook 63,206), `post_media_invalid` (more than four, or another kind), `media_url_refused`, `post_needs_media` (Instagram and Pinterest need a picture or a clip, TikTok and YouTube a clip), `post_details` and `post_board_unknown` (YouTube needs `{ title, category_id }`, a title of 1 to 100 characters and one of Buffer's fifteen categories, as strings: 1, 2, 10, 15, 17, 19, 20 and 22 to 29; Pinterest needs `{ board }`, one of the channel's boards in Buffer's `get_channel`; no other network takes details), `post_time_invalid` (`at` is RFC 3339 with an offset), `post_in_the_past` and `post_too_far` (at most 92 days ahead). With a `slot`: `no_active_marketing_plan`, `not_a_plan_slot` (a slot of the active plan, of the same channel), `slot_used` (no other post of that plan and slot is scheduled or sent; a stopped, missed or failed one frees it), `post_off_its_day` (the date of `at` in its own offset is the slot's day, so Catervas needs no time-zone table) and `post_too_soon` (at least three hours from now). Last, Catervas's own `get_channel` through the agent's connection says whether the channel is the network's: `post_wrong_channel` (a channel that is another network's names that network in Catervas's own words, never in Buffer's, and says "another network" for a word it does not know; when Buffer refuses the channel, its words come in an `untrusted` block), `buffer_not_connected` or `buffer_unreachable`. A picture's address is checked at scheduling and again at hand-over (`media_url_refused`): `https` only, port 443, no user or password, at most 2,000 characters, a public IP address or a name of two labels or more that is not `.local`, `.localhost`, `.internal`, `.lan` or `.home.arpa`; Catervas's request for it follows no redirect and no proxy, connects only to a public address (a name that resolves to a private one is refused at the connection), and must be answered with a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP picture (never an SVG) of at most 20 MiB, or with a video of at most a gigabyte, whose size it says when it says one. The agent's pictures are the business's own, ones the owner gave it, or ones it made with its creative services (6.7), never another's; the address must stay public until the post goes out, since Buffer reads it then.

A post that fills an unused slot of the active plan is recorded `social_post.scheduled { approved_by: plan, plan, slot }`, whose sequence number is the post's number, and the tool answers `{ post, hands_over_at }`. Today shows it under "Going out" with its text, pictures, channel and time in the browser's time zone, why it may go out, and Stop; one hour before its time Catervas calls Buffer's `create_post { channelId, text, schedulingType: automatic, mode: customScheduled, dueAt, assets, metadata? }` itself (`metadata` for YouTube's title and category and Pinterest's board alone) and records `social_post.sent { post, buffer_post }`. A post outside the plan (no `slot`, or no active plan) is recorded `social_post.scheduled { approved_by: catervas }` at once (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: it was `social_post.requested` and waited for the owner on Today with "Post it" and "Don't post"), and goes out as a planned post does: shown under "Going out" with Stop, handed over an hour before its time. It must be at least three hours ahead, `post_too_soon` ("a post is written at least three hours before it goes out") otherwise, as a planned post must; a post that names a `slot` is checked against the plan as before, and with no active plan `no_active_marketing_plan` says "no marketing plan is active, so a post cannot fill a slot; leave slot out to post it outside the plan". `social_post.requested` is never written again and `social_post_decide`, `unknown_post`, `post_decided` and `post_in_the_past` stay for requests an older log holds; such a request whose time comes within five minutes undecided is recorded `social_post.missed { why: undecided }`. The task does not wait for a post.

Stop (`social_post_stop { post }`, the owner's alone) takes a scheduled post not yet with Buffer back at once (`social_post.stopped { by: owner }`); for a post Buffer has, whose time is still ahead, Catervas first calls Buffer's own `delete_post` and records `stopped { by: owner, taken_back: true }` only on its success, else refuses `post_not_taken_back` with nothing recorded; once its time has passed it is `post_already_out`; `post_being_handed_over` while Catervas is giving it to Buffer, `post_not_going_out` for a post requested, stopped, missed or failed, and `unknown_post`. Ending a plan stops, as `stopped { by: plan_ended }`, the plan's posts not yet with Buffer when the owner ended it, or when a newer plan replaced it and the post's slot day is on or after the newer plan's first day; never when the plan only ran out, since each post was checked to fall on a slot day inside the plan, and never a post Catervas is handing over at that moment, which stays with its Stop. A post already with Buffer stays, with its Stop. Every check and record of a post holds the plans' lock `PLANS`, never across a wait for Buffer: the hand-over claims a post under it (`HANDING`, by the project and the post) before it calls Buffer and records the outcome under it after, so that a Stop is either before the claim and the post is not handed over, or after it and is refused.

The hand-over (`hand_over_posts`) is a rule with no model that every tick whose scope names no task runs after `end_marketing_plans`, before the pause check, so that it runs while the team is paused by Catervas's own refusal of the key, since Buffer needs no model. Only a pause by the owner holds it: it hands nothing over, and records `social_post.missed { why: paused }` for each scheduled post whose time is within five minutes. Otherwise, oldest hand-over first, a scheduled post whose time has come to be handed over (an hour before its time, or the owner's decision when that is later) is claimed and its picture addresses are asked again; a post whose time is within five minutes (or past) is recorded `missed { why: not_running }` instead, and one Catervas was not running to hand over in time is sent when its time is still more than five minutes ahead. A failure is recorded `social_post.failed { post, reason }` and never retried, since Buffer may already have the post: a tool error, or Buffer turning the call away over its rate limit with an HTTP 429 (the body is its words), "Buffer did not take it: “<Buffer's words, cut at 300 characters>”"; a timeout, "Buffer did not answer in time and may have the post: look in Buffer's queue before <time>."; an answer with no post id, "Buffer answered without the post's id: look in Buffer's queue before <time>."; a connection that is not there or has lapsed, "<the agent's display name>'s Buffer connection is not there; connect Buffer again." (its name as the owner reads it, the id only when the team file has no such agent); any other failure, "Catervas could not reach Buffer."; a picture that no longer opens, "Its picture or clip no longer opens." The hand-over runs between sessions, and a session runs to its end before the next tick, so a post can be handed over late by one running session, and a session limit over 55 minutes (`max_wall_clock_seconds`) can make one missed.

What the owner and the agent see (added in 0.57). The queries `social_posts.list {}` (every post scheduled or sent whose time is still ahead, soonest first, each with `hands_over_at`, then every post missed or failed in the last 24 hours, the latest first, with `missed_why` or `reason`) and `marketing_plan.get`, which gains `written_posts` beside the plan's slots (each post written for them, oldest first, with its state and when it reached it), read the log; the method `social_post.media { post, index }` has the daemon fetch a post's picture and answers its content type and base64, or `not_found` for a clip, an unknown post or picture, and an address the check above refuses, since the browser's `img-src` is `'self' data:` and a clip or a picture the daemon will not fetch is opened by its address in a new tab (`noopener noreferrer`). Today's "Going out (<n>)" section says "Posts in your plan go out without asking you. Stop any of them before its time." and each row says its network, its day and time in the browser's time zone, how soon, its words as text, its pictures, "Approved in your plan MP-<n>" or "You allowed this", and when Catervas hands it to Buffer or that Buffer has it; "Stop" asks first and, once sent, says Catervas takes it back from Buffer, and when Buffer would not, "Delete it in Buffer before <time>, or it goes out." with a link to Buffer. A post that did not go out in the last 24 hours is listed, muted, with why and that the agent hears of it: a miss says "Catervas could not hand it to Buffer before its time." (true whether Catervas was off, paused or busy with a long session, and no more than Catervas knows), "The team was paused, so it was not sent." or "You had not decided by its time, so it was not sent.", and a failure its `reason` as text. The plan's page counts its slots' posts ("<n> sent, <n> going out, <n> stopped by you, <n> missed, and <n> not written yet", a count of none left out), shows each slot's newest post with its state and an earlier failure, and the end confirmation says how many posts not yet sent will not go out and how many are already with Buffer. The agent's activity line says "Waiting on you: may <agent> post on <Network>?" for a request, `waiting.list` gives it a row of kind `social_post`, and `moved.since` words each post event ("Kai wrote the Instagram post for 13:00.", "You stopped the X post for Sat 31 Oct at 09:00.", and the like). The agent's next `implement` message tells it, after the rest, of each of its posts that was missed or failed ("Catervas could not post <post> (<Network>, <time>):" and the reason in an `untrusted` block), that the owner did not allow it ("The owner did not allow your post <post> on <Network>." and, with a note, "The owner adds: <note>", in the owner's own words, unwrapped) or stopped it ("The owner stopped your post <post>."). The command line is `catervas marketing post list [--json]`, `catervas marketing post stop <n>`, `catervas marketing post send <n>` and `catervas marketing post decline <n> [--note <text>]`; a command handled in the terminal runs on deps whose daemon holds the connections kept on this computer, so that a Stop reaches Buffer, and a run's end lists a request as "<task> waits: <agent name> wants to post on <Network>: catervas marketing post send <n>, or catervas marketing post decline <n>" (section 3, ADR 0014). Paid Instagram and Facebook ads wait until Meta admits Catervas's client to its Ads server.

Google Ads (added in 0.52). Catervas's own connection (6.7, ADR 0038), signed in with Google through Catervas's own Google app, which Catervas Cloud holds from phase 11 (ADR 0048), no build being able to sign in to Google before it (changed in 0.61, ADR 0044), for the one scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords` (ADR 0035, pulled forward by ADR 0042). Its reads (the accounts, fixed reports with clicks, impressions, cost and conversions, and keyword ideas) are `network`. Its writes (a Search campaign for a plan campaign, its ad groups, keywords and ads, a budget, pause or enable) are `external_effect` marked as approved by the marketing plan, a mark only Catervas's own servers may carry: the hook lets such a call run while a plan is active, and Catervas's server refuses every write the active plan does not cover (`not_in_marketing_plan`), never asks. A campaign is created paused, ending with its plan campaign, with a budget Google itself keeps within what the plan campaign has left: a total budget where Google offers one, else a daily budget no larger than what is left divided by the days left. The budget is a hard stop: while Catervas runs it reads the spend every 15 minutes with no model, and when a campaign or the plan reaches its budget it pauses the plan's campaigns itself, records `marketing_budget.reached`, and Today asks the owner to raise the budget (a new version of the plan) or end the plan. Google may spend up to one read's worth past a cap while Catervas runs, and its own budgets bound the spend while Catervas does not.

Google Ads, as built (added in 0.68; ADR 0042, ADR 0044; phase 7 step 08f; the connector is described in 6.7). The kit's skill `running-search-ads` teaches looking before making (`list_accounts`, `keyword_ideas`), one campaign for each plan campaign, ad groups by theme with keywords and their match types, negative keywords, two or more ads for each ad group, `maximize_conversions` only on an ad account that already tracks conversions (Catervas never sets tracking up), enabling a campaign last, `report`'s `search_terms` read to pause what costs without results, and never a competitor's brand name, a claim without a source or sensitive targeting. Until Catervas Cloud signs customers in to Google in phase 11 (ADR 0044, ADR 0048) the connector is built and tested against a fake Google Ads server, the kit row for Google Ads says it comes with Catervas’s web launch and offers no Connect, and the founder's live check is phase 11's. The spend read and the budget's hard stop are as built in 0.72 (below); with no process driving the project, the budget Google keeps (a total budget or a daily one, 6.7) is what bounds the spend.

The budget's hard stop, as built (added in 0.72; ADR 0042; phase 7 step 08g). **The watch.** `Orchestrator::watch_marketing_spend` runs in a task of its own that `catervas serve` and `catervas run` spawn once recovery is done and that ends with the orchestrator, since a tick waits for a running session, which may run 30 minutes (5.5). It starts no session and runs while the team is paused, because stopping spend is never paused. Until a `marketing_campaign.created` is in the log it waits for the first campaign made, and from then on it wakes every minute (`RECHECK`, through the sleeper). A store error ends it and stops the orchestrator, so `catervas serve` ends saying so, and so does a panic in it (added in 0.72 after review); a Google, sign-in or team-file failure is that read's failure, and the watch goes on. **The read.** An active plan with a campaign made under its lineage is read when its last attempt, kept in memory by plan id, is 15 minutes old or absent, so a restart reads at once; a failed read is an attempt too, since a retry every minute would spend Catervas Cloud's shared quota (ADR 0044) on failures that rarely clear within one. A read is one `Search` for each ad account the lineage's campaigns are in, `spend_query` over that account's campaigns, from the day before the first campaign was made, in UTC, to tomorrow, so the account's time zone cannot drop a day; costs are summed for each plan campaign's key and in all, in hundredths rounded up from micros. The plan's cost is that of every campaign of the lineage, as enabling counts it (6.7), so enabling and the cap count one spend: 96 operations a day for each active plan and ad account. Whose connection reads (changed in 0.72 after review): the plan's proposer's `google-ads` entry, then each other Marketing Specialist's, the active ones first, then the paused, then the retired, each in the team file's order, through the entry that `matches_kit` and its stored sign-in (no session ticket); an agent's status does not keep it from being tried, since stopping spend is never paused: a paused agent keeps its sign-in; a retired agent is tried last and finds a sign-in only when it was retired outside Catervas (a hand edit of the team file, or a pulled one), since retiring it in Catervas pauses its ads first and deletes its keys (ADR 0030, below), and is passed over otherwise (changed in 0.72 after review). The next is tried when this one's grant cannot be had (no entry, not the kit's, a sign-in that has lapsed, is unconfirmed or failed) or Google answers that this sign-in does not reach the account; any other answer of Google's ends the read, since another sign-in meets the same and spends more of the quota; with none left the read fails with the last reason, and the last spend that worked stays beside the failure, with its time. **The caps.** `catervas_core::marketing::caps_reached` decides, and only for the active plan: a plan campaign's key whose cost is at least its budget reaches a `campaign` cap; the plan's cost at least its Google Ads budget (when that is above nothing) reaches the `plan` cap, which takes every campaign the active plan carries. A campaign is carried only when its plan is in the active plan's lineage, the active plan has its key, and it is in the active plan's `google_ads_account`. A cap recorded for the active plan, by its scope and key, is not reached again, and a raised version's own budgets decide from its approval. **A pause** reads status first, one `Search` for each ad account with `status_query` (the campaigns' resource names and statuses, no metrics, so a campaign with no cost still has its row), then sends one `googleAds:mutate` of `PAUSED` for each campaign reported `ENABLED` or missing from the rows, each on its own since one mutate is atomic; a campaign reported `PAUSED` or `REMOVED` counts as paused with no call. It is Catervas's own fixed act, not a session's call and with no hook, on the list of operations of 6.7. At a cap Catervas pauses its campaigns, then records `marketing_budget.reached { plan, scope, key?, spent, budget, currency, paused, failed? }`, `paused` being the campaigns Google accepted or reported paused and `failed` the first refusal's words cut at 300 characters. While the cap's plan is the active plan, each later read reads the status of the cap's campaigns again and pauses any that is `ENABLED` (a refused pause, or a campaign enabled by hand), recording `marketing_campaign.paused { plan, key, campaign, why: budget_reached }` once for a campaign not in the cap's `paused` and not recorded paused for a budget since the plan's first cap (changed in 0.72 after review, so that a raised version's pause of a campaign its predecessor had paused is recorded too). The writes' lock (6.7) is held from the read through the pauses, so no write is in flight. **A plan that ends** by the owner, `replaced` or `expired` has the campaigns the active plan does not carry paused at the watch's first wake after `marketing_plan.ended`, not at the next 15-minute read: the campaigns `to_pause_for_end` lists (every campaign Catervas made that the active plan does not carry, whether it was made under a plan outside its lineage, for a key it lacks or in another ad account, and that is not yet recorded paused for the end; with no active plan, every such campaign; changed in 0.72 after review), each recorded `marketing_campaign.paused { why: plan_ended }` when Google accepts the pause or reports the campaign `PAUSED` or `REMOVED`. A campaign the active plan carries keeps running under it within its budget, and its own end stops it at Google in any case. A refusal is kept as the plan's `unstopped` and tried again every 15 minutes, until a later pause of the plan succeeds; once every campaign is recorded paused for the end the plan is not looked at again. A campaign recorded paused because Google Ads was removed (`connection_removed`) counts as paused for the end (changed in 0.72 after review) while no `google-ads` connection has been recorded since, so that a plan ending after a removal asks Google for nothing, keeps no `unstopped` and shows no "Ads still running" for ads that are paused; once Google Ads is connected again it counts no more, since an agent could have enabled the campaign. It counts no more either while an agent that is not retired has a `google-ads` entry in the team file (changed in 0.72 after review, with the same note): another Marketing Specialist's sign-in could have enabled the campaign with no connection recorded, so the end's pause reads status with that grant and pauses what is `ENABLED`, as for any other campaign. A retired agent has no sign-in to enable with (retiring it deletes its keys and it runs no session), so retiring the only Marketing Specialist that has Google Ads leaves nothing to pause when the plan ends. The watch, `catervas disconnect` and the command that ends a plan, handled with no process driving, read the same rule. **Removing Google Ads.** `connector.disconnect` for `google-ads`, once the command's own checks pass (the agent has the entry; a refused removal pauses nothing, changed in 0.72 after review), first pauses, under the writes' lock and with that agent's grant, every campaign Catervas made that is not recorded paused for its plan's end, whichever Marketing Specialist runs it, recording `marketing_campaign.paused` with `why: plan_ended` for a campaign `to_pause_for_end` lists and `connection_removed` for the others; then the connection is removed whatever Google answered, since Catervas could not stop the ads without it. The writes' lock is held from the pause until the removal is done (the entry out of the team file and its keys deleted), so that no agent's enable runs in between and turns on what Catervas stopped (added in 0.72 after review); every removal path holds it the same way, from its pause through its write of the team, and the order of the locks is the writes' lock first and the team's second, never the other way. A refusal, or a grant that cannot be had, is kept as `unstopped` for Today (5.7). The Remove confirmation says so beforehand: "Catervas pauses your marketing plan's running ads first, since without this connection it could not stop them at their budget. If Google refuses, Google Ads is removed anyway, and the ads keep running at Google until their end date or their budget there; pause them in Google Ads." Every other path that takes a Marketing Specialist's `google-ads` sign-in away does the same before it writes (added in 0.72 after review): `team.save` and `team.start` when the team they write drops the entry or the agent that holds it, `template.apply` when the template removes an agent that has it or retires one, and retiring an agent (the page's retire, which is `agent_update`; `agent.replace`; and the template's retirement), which keeps the entry in the team file but deletes the agent's keys (ADR 0030). Each pauses for the first agent that loses the sign-in whose pause leaves nothing running, with that agent's grant, holding the writes' lock until it has written, then goes on whatever Google answered, keeping a refusal as `unstopped`; a team, a template, a replacement or a retirement that would be refused pauses nothing. A save cannot retire an agent (a status changes only on the agent's card), and the command line has no command that retires one, so none needs `catervas disconnect`'s refusal (added in 0.72 after review). `catervas disconnect <agent> google-ads` refuses `disconnect_in_the_browser: remove Google Ads on <agent>'s page in the browser, where Catervas pauses its running ads first` whenever a campaign Catervas made is not recorded paused for its plan's end, whether or not a process drives the project, since the pause and the removal go together on the agent's page in the browser (changed in 0.72 after review, from "when nothing drives the project").

What each campaign advertises, and its price (added in 0.72; the founder's decisions of 2026-10-07: "Catervas must have a plan of what exactly to advertise and get a final price before beginning. If the price is dynamic, then just dont say so before committing to a plan", then "Disclose dynamic ones"). Each campaign of a plan says what it advertises (`advertises`, required, 3 to 200 characters; a plan proposed before has none, read back empty and shown "Not stated"). `price_kind(campaign, currency, day)`, pure, is `campaign_budget`'s kind (6.7) for a campaign made on `day`: `Fixed` for a total budget, which Google never bills past, and `NotFixed` for a daily one, which may spend past its cap for about an hour because Google reports cost up to about an hour late (Google Ads Help 2544985). `marketing_plan.get` gives each campaign `advertises` and `price` (`fixed` or `not_fixed`), as of today while the plan is proposed or sent back and as of the day it was approved (the UTC date of the approval event) once approved; a campaign already made for the key under the plan's lineage, in its ad account, is priced by the budget it has, `fixed` for a total and `not_fixed` for a daily one, whatever dates a new version gives it (changed in 0.72 after review, since a raised version of a long daily campaign would otherwise show a price it cannot have). The plan's page shows, under each campaign's goal, "Advertises: <advertises>" and "Price: fixed at <budget> <currency>" or "Price: up to <budget> <currency>, may run over by about an hour's spend"; "What approving lets <agent> do" adds, for each campaign not at a fixed price, "<name> is not at a fixed price, so it may run over by about an hour's spend.", the decision bar "1 campaign may run over by about an hour's spend." ("<n> campaigns …"), and a note under the table says "A fixed price is a total that Google itself never charges past. Google keeps one only for a campaign of 3 to 90 days; any other has a daily budget, and since Google reports cost up to about an hour late, Catervas may pause it after about an hour's more spend." Once approved, the budget's caption adds "Prices as on the day you approved the plan." A fixed price stays fixed: `AdsPlanView` carries `approved_on`, and creating a campaign for a key that was `Fixed` on that day is refused when `campaign_budget` would now give a daily budget ("<key> was approved at a fixed price, which Google keeps only for a run of 3 days or more; propose a new version"). The kit's skills `writing-the-marketing-plan` and `running-search-ads` say: "Prefer campaigns at a fixed price: 3 to 90 days, made at least two days before they start. Say in the plan's text what each campaign advertises, and which campaigns are not at a fixed price and why."

The plan's page shows the spend (added in 0.72). `marketing_plan.get` gains `spend { read_at?, total?, by_key?, failed?, failed_at? }` from the watch's memory (left out until it has tried; `by_key` is by plan campaign key), `reached` (the plan's `marketing_budget.reached`, each `{ scope, key?, spent, budget, failed?, at }`) and `paused` (its `marketing_campaign.paused` and the campaigns paused at a cap, each `{ key, name, why, at }`, oldest first). The page's "Spent so far" ("Spent" once the plan ended) section gives the total against the plan's Google Ads budget with a meter, "Google Ads' own figures, read <when>. Catervas reads them every 15 minutes while it runs." (once ended: "… last read <when>, before the plan ended. Google Ads itself has the final figures."), and, after a failed read of a plan still running, "Catervas can't read the spend now: <reason> Last tried <when>; Catervas tries again every 15 minutes. Until a read works, Catervas cannot pause the ads at their budget."; the budget table gains each campaign's spend, marked "Paused at its budget", "Paused: the plan ended" or "Paused: Google Ads was removed" by its newest pause; and "Ads Catervas paused" lists each pause, newest first, with its time and why ("<name>: it reached its budget, <spent> of <budget> <currency>.", "<name>: the plan ended.", "<name>: Google Ads was removed."). The End confirmation of a plan with ads begins "Catervas pauses its running ads within a minute." and, once a read worked, "<spent> is spent so far, by Google's figures at <time>.", and the hint beside End reads "Ending pauses the ads within a minute and stops the posts not yet sent." (changed from 08c's, since the browser always has `catervas serve` driving); `catervas marketing plan end`, handled with no process driving, adds "Catervas pauses <plan>'s ads when it next runs." when a campaign Catervas made is still to pause. `moved.since` tells each pause: "Catervas paused <plan>'s ads at their budget." ("… campaign <name> at its budget." at a campaign's; "Catervas could not pause …" when Google refused) and "Catervas paused <plan>'s campaign <name>: the plan ended." ("… Google Ads was removed.", "… it reached its budget.").

The raise (added in 0.72; ADR 0042).
