"Raise the budget" on Today's row opens a dialog for the new Google Ads budget and the new budget of each campaign that reached its own, refusing in the dialog, with no call, an amount at or below its spend ("Make it more than the <spent> <currency> already spent."), a Google Ads budget below what the plan has now ("Make it at least the <budget> <currency> it is now.") and campaigns adding up to more than the Google Ads budget ("The campaigns' budgets add up to <sum> <currency>: make this at least that."); the plan's total rises by what the Google Ads budget does, `check_proposal` refusing a Google Ads budget above the total. It calls `marketing_budget.raise { plan, google_ads, campaigns: [{ key, budget }] } -> { task_id }`, one of the gates' write methods, which checks the same (`raise_refused`), that `plan` is the active plan with a `marketing_budget.reached`, and that no raise of it is open (`raise_open`: a raise whose task is neither accepted nor cancelled). What was spent is the last good read, else the recorded caps', so the owner can raise right after a restart. It files a request through the same path as `request.file`, titled "New version of <plan> with a raised budget", whose text says: "Propose a new version of <plan> that replaces it (replaces: <plan>), starting today, with its Google Ads budget <amount> <currency> and its total <amount>, and <key>'s budget <amount>; keep its campaigns and post slots that are not over, each with its key and what it advertises, their dates from today on. Once the owner approves it, raise each paused campaign's budget at Google with set_campaign_budget, then enable it.", with `raises` on `task.created` and the triage of 5.16. The agent proposes the new version as any plan; the owner approves it as any plan, and approving it replaces the old plan as a newer plan does (above). Rejected: the owner approving a raised budget directly, which would leave Catervas to enable ads itself.

What Google may spend past a cap (added in 0.72). Google reports cost up to about an hour late (Google Ads Help 2544985), so a campaign at a daily budget may spend about an hour past its cap, and up to a minute more, while a process drives the project (`catervas serve`; `catervas run` exits when idle); a campaign at a total budget is never passed. With no process driving the project, Google's own budgets (6.7) bound the spend.

The research foundation (added in 0.127; ADR 0072; `docs/design/marketing-agent.md`). Before its first marketing plan, and again before each plan after, the Marketing Specialist runs five stages in order, each one task and one document under `docs/catervas/marketing/research/` in the team's format, each reading those before it: `product` (what it does, for whom, its proof, its price, how it describes itself; from the Product Manager's folder, else the project's own files and site, then the owner's corrections), `audience` (one main group and at most two more, each from at least five separate pieces of evidence: their job, trigger, doubts and words, quoted short with links, each theme labelled High, Medium or Low, and the sample's bias), `competitors` (direct, almost the same product; indirect, a different product for the same job; substitutes and doing nothing; each fact as seen with its source and day, inferred with a confidence, or what it implies), `outreach` (each competitor's channels, posts, ads and offers, who it targets, its search words, and the gaps) and `positioning` (the positioning, the message per group, and three cheap channel tests, each with a measure and a point to stop). A document under 92 days old is refreshed, not redone. The plan opens with the first 30 days from `positioning`. Reddit is read through Exa (`web_search_exa`, `web_fetch_exa`), threads the owner pastes and Reddit's Trends summaries the owner copies in, since the agent's own web tools refuse reddit.com; X and LinkedIn through search results of their public pages and the owner's exports; ad libraries the owner opens and pastes or screenshots. The agent signs in nowhere as anyone and keeps no person's name or handle beyond a quote's link. A poster is an SVG under `docs/catervas/marketing/assets/posters/` laid out from the brand kit, its words exact; a video starts as a storyboard. A reply, or a comment on Reddit, is a draft for the owner to send. In its chat (12 tool calls, 3 minutes) it answers from the foundation and takes a question that needs research as its own task with `catervas_take_task`, saying so.

Default tools: read, network, write_workspace scoped to its paths, git_local, so that it commits what it wrote (changed in 0.10).

Kit (added in 0.51; 6.7): fifteen skills written for any business, software or not, `positioning-and-messaging`, `planning-a-launch`, `writing-for-search`, `writing-in-the-brands-voice`, `keeping-a-content-calendar`, `researching-competitors`, `measuring-campaigns`, `making-images-and-video`, `posting-and-email` (added in 0.53), `keeping-the-brand-kit`, `writing-the-brand-persona`, `researching-the-market` and `writing-the-marketing-plan` (the four added in 0.55) `running-social-channels` (added in 0.57) and `running-search-ads` (added in 0.68), and five services, each signed in to. Two spend the user's credits, Higgsfield (images, video and voice-overs) and Recraft (graphics and vector art), each making one image, clip or edit inside an allowance the user sets and asking for everything else. Two reach the business's audience (added in 0.53; ADR 0042): Buffer reads the business's channels and how earlier posts did for the agent and, through Catervas's own calls, schedules the posts of the plan, and the posts outside it, to Instagram, X and nine other networks; Kit drafts email broadcasts, email series and landing pages and reads their numbers, and a broadcast is only a draft the human schedules and sends from Kit. Its pictures and clips are files and addresses the human or a post uses. One runs the plan's search ads (added in 0.68; ADR 0042): Google Ads, Catervas's own connector, tagged `paid`, whose writes run only inside the plan the owner approved (5.6, 6.7). Design files (Figma, Canva) are in no kit while those services admit only clients on their own lists.

Kit (added in 0.101; ADR 0051; phase 8 step 07): the kit's sixteenth skill, `catervafying-the-repository`, listed last: propose the first marketing plan with `catervas_propose_marketing_plan` from `docs/catervas/product/` alone, which its sessions read already (5.17), and say what the product plan lacks rather than guess. Documents are named by stem, without an extension, and written in the team's format (changed in 0.108).

Kit (added in 0.127; ADR 0072): seven more skills, listed before `catervafying-the-repository`, which stays last: `running-the-research-foundation`, `understanding-the-product`, `researching-the-audience`, `studying-competitor-outreach`, `finding-where-to-start`, `optimising-for-search` and `making-posters`, each rewritten for Catervas from public skill sets and naming them in its "Drawn from" section (Corey Haines's `marketingskills`, MIT; Anthropic's `knowledge-work-plugins` and `canvas-design`, Apache-2.0; `claude-seo` and `geo-seo-claude`, MIT); `researching-competitors` is rewritten for the three groups, `writing-the-marketing-plan` opens with the first 30 days, and `running-social-channels` drafts replies and Reddit comments for the owner. Exa joins the services, keyless, with `web_search_exa` and `web_fetch_exa` both `network` (the Procurement Specialist's reader stays `denied`). A kit lists at most 30 skills (was 20).

**Under autopilot (added in 0.138; ADR 0082).** A marketing plan that spends, and one that raises the marketing budget, is approved when proposed, by Catervas, recorded `marketing_plan.approved` with `by: autopilot` and a note that the marketing budget stays its hard stop; a plan that spends nothing is approved as before. The budget's hard stop holds (6.5, 8.6). A post outside the approved plan already goes out without asking (ADR 0061).

### 6.6 Finance Specialist (added in 0.21)

Mandate (changed in 0.103; ADR 0055): keep track of the business's money: what it owns, spends, earns and has at stake. For a software product, start with the team's own AI spending, then its other costs and its revenue; for any business, keep its books, forecast them, and do the analysis a task asks for, a portfolio's holdings, a risk or an opportunity among them. Record the numbers, forecast them, and recommend budgets in plain words. For a product the costs are the team's AI spending, read from Catervas's own records; when the product uses Stripe, its revenue, fees, payouts and refunds; and everything the user's receipts and bank statements show, such as cloud, infrastructure, storage, hosting, domains, software subscriptions, and payment and billing fees. It records the AI spending and forecasts it first; then it takes each receipt from the receipts mailbox, categorises it and records it, reconciles the books against the bank or card statement, closes each month, forecasts expenses over 12 to 36 months, analyses pricing and unit economics, and recommends budgets in plain words. What it produces is management accounting, not a tax filing, statutory accounts, or financial advice, and it says so. It is optional: the team builder offers it and does not suggest it (ADR 0019; `docs/design/finance-specialist.md`).

Produces: `.xlsx` workbooks in `.catervas/local/finance/`, the books (`books.xlsx`, each row naming its receipt file, statement line or Stripe object), the forecast (`forecast.xlsx`), and any other a task asks for; the receipts it filed, under `receipts/<yyyy-mm>/`; the completion note that explains them.

Cannot: write application code or anything in the repository; pay, refund, move money, change Catervas's budgets, or change anything in Stripe or the mailbox; send, delete, move, or mark any email; publish anywhere; write outside its finance folder.

Default tools: read and network (to research prices), and Catervas tools that only it may call, but for the two sheet tools, which the Procurement Specialist has for its own folder (6.10; changed in 0.70), each of the `read` tier: `catervas_read_costs`, the team's AI spending by task, agent, day or purpose; `catervas_read_sheet`, which every role may call, reading either private folder's workbooks (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061); `catervas_write_sheet`, which writes a whole workbook in the finance folder and keeps the previous version in `.history/` (as built, below; changed in 0.56); and, once receipts intake ships, `catervas_read_receipts`, the messages of the receipts mailbox not yet filed, and `catervas_file_receipt`, which saves a message's receipt and marks it `recorded`, or marks it `not_a_receipt`. Its reviewer field names the Product Manager, who reviews nothing: Catervas accepts its tasks on their criteria (5.4; changed in 0.115; ADR 0061).

As built so far (added in 0.54; phase 7 step 09). The role is `finance_specialist`, "Finance Specialist", tag "FIN", with the persona "Keeps your numbers straight", the model `claude-sonnet-5-5` at `medium` effort and the default session limits. Its tiers are exactly `read` and `network`, its reviewer field names the Product Manager (and nobody reviews its tasks, 5.4), and it does not change code (5.12). Its prompt and its one skill, `keeping-the-books`, say that its numbers are management accounting, not a tax filing, statutory accounts or financial advice; that every number names its source; and that it never pays, refunds or moves money, changes a budget, or writes to a service. Its kit, since phase 7 step 10, holds six skills and the services Stripe, Digits and Kick, each only read (6.7; changed in 0.67). Its picture is the brand's `extra-4` character, copied under the key `finance-specialist` while `extra-4` stays among the extras, and its tag colour is a pale olive, `#C2C79B` in both themes, held to the same contrast against the role ink as the other role colours. The Team page's "Add someone" offers it after the Marketing Specialist, and an agent added as one takes that picture and a spare name; setup does not suggest it, and offers it, unticked, under "More roles" (added in 0.70; F1). The user can talk to it in a one-to-one chat. Its spreadsheet tools are described below (added in 0.56), and its tasks, which run in its private folder, below them (added in 0.62).

The spreadsheet tools, as built (added in 0.56; phase 7 step 09b). Three tools of the `read` tier, each writing only to Catervas's own private folder, as `catervas_write_memory` writes only the agent's notebook (5.6).

The folder line. The Finance Specialist's folder is `.catervas/local/finance/`, found from the role by `private_folder(role)` in `catervas-core`, which is `None` for every role but this one and the Procurement Specialist, whose folder is `.catervas/local/procurement/` (6.10; 0.70); it is made readable by its owner alone when it is first written, and it is never committed, since `.catervas/local/` is kept out of git. A tool's `path` is relative to the caller's folder: 1 to 200 characters in at most 3 parts joined by `/`, each part 1 to 100 characters of letters, digits, spaces, `.`, `_` and `-` that starts with a letter or a digit (so no part starts with a dot, and `.history/` cannot be named), the last ending in `.xlsx` in lower case; the procurement folder also holds notes, so `private_file_fault(folder, path)` in `catervas-core` lets a path there end in `.md` in lower case too, which the sheet tools never open, since they check the path as a workbook's first (0.70). A path of any other shape, a path with a part that is a link, a folder that is a link or lies below one (every part from the project's root down is checked, so `.catervas/local` and `.catervas/local/finance` themselves may not be links), and a path that resolves outside the folder once links are resolved are each refused as `private_path_refused: <path> <why>`, and nothing is written. The tools report no path to the permission check (5.6) and hold the folder line themselves, so `.catervas/local/**` stays a protected path for every other call. They read `.xlsx` alone: CSV, with `imports/`, comes with receipts intake in phase 18.

`catervas_read_costs { by, from?, to? }`. `by` is `task`, `agent`, `day` or `purpose`, the key the costs of 5.5 are summed by; `from` and `to` are UTC days, `YYYY-MM-DD`, given together or not at all, `from` not after `to` and at most 366 days apart, and the sum then counts the costs recorded on those days, both included (`cost_range_invalid` otherwise). It answers `{ by, rows: [{ key, usd, input_tokens, output_tokens, sessions }] }` and records nothing. A Finance Specialist may call it in any session; any other role is refused `sheet_refused`, the Procurement Specialist among them (0.70).

`catervas_write_sheet { path, sheets }` writes one whole workbook in the caller's own folder, and only in the implement session of a task whose assignee is the caller, so that a chat or a conversation never writes the books or the register (any other call is refused `sheet_refused`; the Procurement Specialist has it too, 0.70, and takes no `folder`). `sheets` is 1 to 20 of `{ name, columns, rows }`. A name is 1 to 31 characters with none of `[`, `]`, `:`, `*`, `?`, `/`, `\` and `|`, no apostrophe at either end, not History in any case, and different from the other names without regard to case. `columns` is 0 to 100 headings, written as the sheet's bold first row when there are any, and `rows` 0 to 10,000 rows of 0 to 100 cells, so that row numbers are the spreadsheet's own and the headings are row 1. A cell is a number, a string of up to 32,767 characters, a boolean, `null` for an empty cell, `{ "date": "YYYY-MM-DD" }` (from 1900, written as a date and shown as `yyyy-mm-dd`), or `{ "formula": "=..." }`. A bound that is broken, or a date that is not one, is refused `sheet_refused`, naming the sheet or the cell, before anything is written. A string is always written as text, never as a formula, whatever it starts with, so that a value from Stripe, a receipt or an email that starts with `=`, `+`, `-` or an at sign stays inert in the user's spreadsheet program (8.6). A formula is refused `formula_refused`, naming its sheet, its cell and its row and column, and nothing is written, when it does not start with `=`, when it holds `[` (an external reference) or `|` (a DDE call such as `=cmd|' /C calc'!A0`), or when it uses `HYPERLINK`, `WEBSERVICE`, `FILTERXML`, `IMPORTDATA`, `IMPORTXML`, `IMPORTHTML`, `IMPORTRANGE`, `IMPORTFEED`, `IMAGE`, `RTD`, `DDE`, `CALL`, `REGISTER.ID`, `EXEC`, `INFO`, `CELL`, `COPILOT`, `TRANSLATE`, `DETECTLANGUAGE`, `PY`, `STOCKHISTORY`, `GOOGLETRANSLATE`, `GOOGLEFINANCE` or `AI`. To use a function is to name it, in any letter case, after the start of the formula, a character outside letters, digits, `_` and `.`, or one of the prefixes `_xlfn.`, `_xlws.`, `_xleta.` and `_xludf.`, and before white space and either `(`, which calls it, or `)`, `,` or the end of the formula, which hands it to another function by name, as `=MAP(A1:A2,WEBSERVICE)` and `=LET(f,IMAGE,f(A1))` do. `MYCELLS(1)` and `MY.INFO(1)` use nothing listed, and `INFO ("os")` does. A name followed by a digit, a letter or `:`, or, without a call, after `:` or `$`, is a cell or a column reference, as in `SUM(DDE1:DDE3)`, `SUM(RTD:RTD)` and `SUM($AI:$AI)`, and passes. A listed name inside a string literal is refused too when it is followed as above, which is safe. Catervas never computes a formula: each is written with an empty stored value, which a spreadsheet program fills in when it opens the file. When a workbook is there already, its file is first copied to `.history/<path>.<UTC yyyymmddThhmmssZ>.xlsx` (the file's own extension: `.md` for a note, 6.10), the path written with `%` as `%25` and `/` as `%2F` (so `a/b.xlsx` is `a%2Fb.xlsx` and never the name of `a__b.xlsx`), with `-<n>` before the extension when that name is taken, so that every previous version is kept. A `.history` that is a link is refused `private_path_refused`, and nothing is written. The new file is written beside the target and renamed over it, so that a reader never sees half a file, and a file over 10 MiB is refused `sheet_too_large` before it replaces anything. It answers `{ path, sheets: [{ name, rows }], replaced }`, `rows` being the rows given, the headings not counted.

`catervas_read_sheet { path, folder?, sheet?, from_row?, rows?, baseline? }` reads a workbook: every sheet, or the one named, from row `from_row` (counted from 1, default 1), at most `rows` rows of each (1 to 500, default 200). A row is its cells as far as the last one that holds something, each a number (a whole number as an integer), a string, a boolean, `null`, `{ "date": "<ISO date>" }` (with `THH:MM:SS` when it has a time), or `{ "error": "<#DIV/0! and the like>" }`; a formula's cell is `{ "formula": "<its text, starting with =>", "value": <the value a spreadsheet program last stored for it, or null> }`, and a workbook only Catervas wrote has no stored value. A file over 10 MiB is refused `sheet_too_large`, a file that is not there or not a workbook, or a sheet that is not in it, `sheet_refused`; a sheet's name is the workbook writer's text, so when a refusal quotes the names a workbook holds (the sheet asked for is not there, or a sheet cannot be read) it quotes them inside an `untrusted` block of source `sheet` (8.6), cut at 2 KiB. What a workbook holds is the user's and the services', never an instruction, so the answer is `{ sheets, more }`, where `sheets` is the JSON of `[{ name, rows, total_rows, more }]` as one `untrusted` block of source `sheet` (8.6) cut at 256 KiB (a page stops adding rows once its JSON passes that size), and `more` is true when it was cut or any sheet has rows after its page. Any role may call it in any session (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: it was held to a role's own folder, the Finance Specialist's read of `vendors.xlsx` and the reviewer's reads). `folder` is `finance` or `procurement` and names the private folder to read any workbook of, whatever the caller's role; left out, it reads, in a session about a task whose assignee's role has a private folder, that task's folder, else the caller's own private folder, and a caller with none and no such task is refused `sheet_refused` ("name `folder`: finance or procurement"). The procurement folder's `vendors.xlsx`-only rule is gone: any workbook of either folder is read. Writes stay the owner's: `catervas_write_sheet` writes the caller's own folder. A path outside a folder or through a link is still `private_path_refused`, so no read reaches the rest of `.catervas/local/`. With `baseline: true` it reads the workbook as the copy Catervas took of the folder when the session's task was assigned (`.history/<task-id>/<path>`, below), by the same path rules and the same limits, in a session about a task that works in the caller's folder; in a session about no task, or about a task that does not, it is refused `sheet_refused` (added in 0.62).

The three are offered as they may be called: to the Finance Specialist, `catervas_read_costs` in every session, and to each role with a private folder, `catervas_write_sheet` in an implement session of a task; `catervas_read_sheet` is offered in every session to every role (changed in 0.115); `catervas_read_costs` is the Finance Specialist's alone, so the Procurement Specialist is not offered it and is refused it `sheet_refused`.

Finance tasks, as built (added in 0.62; phase 7 step 09c). A task of the Finance Specialist's is a task in its private folder, found from the role by `private_folder(role)`, and runs there; every rule below keys on that one function, so another role's folder is one more arm of it (6.10). Its readiness is 5.3's `private_folder_task`, and its reviewer is held to the Product Manager alone by `private_folder_reviewer` (the founder's decision of 2026-10-07); its assignment waits while another task holds the folder (5.2), and then Catervas copies the folder's files but `.history/` to `.history/<task-id>/`, once, and starts the task there, with no worktree, branch or sandbox made. Its implement session, and, for a task filed before 0.115 (ADR 0061), its reviewer's session and the Product Manager's acceptance session, run with the folder as their working directory (made for its owner alone when it is not there) and with no executor, so the hook, which judges every path against the working directory (5.6, 8.2), lets them reach the folder and nothing outside it: not another task's worktree, not `.catervas/local/catervas.db`, not the files above the folder. The implement message names the role's folder, `.catervas/local/finance` for this role, and says that nothing there is committed (changed in 0.70, from "where your books are"). It asks for `verifying` with `catervas_request_transition`, whose `workbooks` names the workbooks it wrote, one to twenty paths in the folder (a list of none or of more is `InvalidInput`), and the governor's gate reads them from the folder (5.2); the files that changed since the copy are the task's diff, and the Definition of Done holds them to `allowed_paths` and excepts the folder from the protected paths (5.4). Catervas checks its `artifact` criteria on the host and shows its reviewer which files changed, each beside its copy (5.4). Once Catervas accepts it (5.4; changed in 0.115), it is finished with nothing to integrate and counts as integrated for the tasks that depend on it (5.14). Each task's copy, `.history/<task-id>/`, is kept, as every version of a workbook under `.history/` is (the tools' own copies, above), and is the restore point for a cancelled task, whose changes stay in the folder. Its prompt and its skill say all this: work in the private folder, nothing there is committed, record each `artifact` criterion with `catervas_record_criterion_result` before asking for `verifying`, and ask for it naming the `workbooks`. A session of its ends in one of three ways, as every role's does: it asks the human, declares itself blocked, or asks for `verifying`, and naming the `workbooks` is how the third goes.

Stripe, Digits and Kick (changed in 0.67; phase 7 step 10; ADR 0019's amendment of 2026-10-07). The role reads the services its kit offers (6.7), each connected by the user and each only read. Stripe, when the product uses it, gives the revenue, fees, payouts and refunds, through Stripe's official server: the user signs in to Stripe (route 1), choosing the account, live or a sandbox, and the permissions on Stripe's own page, and can end Catervas's access under ‘OAuth sessions’ in their Stripe user settings. Read-only is Catervas's own lock, which holds whatever the user ticks on Stripe's page: in the kit the tools that read the business's numbers are `network` and every tool that writes, whatever it writes, is `denied`, so the harness refuses a write before Stripe would. This replaces the restricted key with read permissions that 0.54 described, since a signed-in service refreshes its own access and a kit entry has one way in. Digits and Kick, which a business may already keep its books in, are signed in to and read the same way. The books carry totals and Stripe's own ids, never a customer's name, email or card: `stripe_api_read` takes any `GET`, so a charge comes back with its customer's details, Catervas cannot split one tool, and the role's prompt and the skill `using-finance-sources` hold the line. What that leaves open is a known risk (8.6).

Receipts intake (changed in 0.21 on the founder's decision of 2026-09-27, from a connector to the user's main mailbox; ships in the first release after the web release, phase 18 step 02). The user keeps a receipts mailbox of its own, an alias or a second address at their own provider, and forwards or routes receipts to it; vendors can bill it directly. Catervas reads that mailbox over IMAP, with an app password, or the provider's IMAP sign-in through Catervas Cloud where it suits (changed in 0.61, ADR 0044), kept in the OS keychain; it reads no other mailbox, so the boundary is the mailbox itself rather than a filter Catervas promises to apply, and no provider's restricted-scope verification applies. The connector asks for unread messages, has no call that changes the mailbox, never hands over a message already filed, accepts a sender only from the user's approved list, and gives the agent each message's text, and each attachment it files, under the untrusted-content notice (8.6). An attachment is filed only if it is a PDF or an image and at most 10 MB. The mailbox settings, the approved senders and the ledger of filed messages live in `.catervas/local/finance/mailbox.json` (8.4). The user drops no bill anywhere; a bank or card statement, the one file every bank exports as CSV, goes under `imports/` and is the source the books are reconciled against, because a receipt describes a purchase and a statement shows the money. `catervas finance connect`, `catervas finance disconnect` and the web app's finance setup manage the mailbox; `mailbox.connected` and `mailbox.disconnected` record it. A connector to the user's main mailbox through Google's or Microsoft's mail API, filtered by a label or folder, is not planned: it needs Google's restricted-scope verification with a paid yearly assessment, its filter is Catervas's promise rather than the provider's enforcement, and it is built only if users ask once receipts intake has shipped.

When it works. While a process drives the project, Catervas starts a receipts sweep once a day, as a tick rule that runs once a UTC day: the connector fetches the new messages first, and a sweep with nothing new starts no session and costs nothing; otherwise a short Finance Specialist session files each receipt and records it in the books, its cost under the `finance` purpose (F17). `sweep.started` and `sweep.ended` are recorded either way, so the day's tick has a last run to count from. The user can start one with "Check now" or `catervas finance sweep`. `receipt.filed` records each receipt. One piece of finance work touches the folder at a time, and a sweep is one: once receipts intake ships, a sweep does not start while a task holds the folder (5.2), and a finance task is not assigned while a sweep runs. A finance task is otherwise a task in the folder, as "Finance tasks, as built" above says: its `allowed_paths` are under `.catervas/local/finance/`, its criteria are `artifact` ones, its session runs in the folder, it names its `workbooks` to reach `verifying`, its reviewer is shown what changed beside the copy taken at its assignment, and once `accepted` it is finished (5.14).

The mailbox plumbing (added in 0.77; phase 7 step 10f). The reading and sending of a mailbox of the user's own is Catervas's, in `runtime/src/mailbox.rs`: providers and their servers, the login checked over TLS with the platform's certificates, `MailboxSecrets` (the password kept like a connector's keys, one per purpose), the alias rule that opens only the mail Catervas expects, and the ledger that numbers a folder. The Procurement Specialist is its first user (6.10); the Finance Specialist's receipts intake (phase 18 step 02) reuses it and does not rewrite it, with its own purpose and its own folder.

### 6.7 Role kits (added in 0.22)

The owner's Claude connectors are found, never used by a team's agents (added in 0.142; ADR 0059; phase 10 step 03b). The services `catervas discover` finds (section 3) are what the owner uses through Claude; a team's agents never use those connectors or their keys. A team connects Catervas's own connectors, which Today suggests where Catervas has one for the service (a later step of phase 10).

The services the owner declares (added in 0.146; ADR 0059; phase 10 step 06). The owner may say which services they use with Claude, chosen from the catalog or named (`finding.declare_services`, 4.4); the declared set is kept in `machine.db` (8.4) beside the services found, replaces the set before it, and is no more a connection than the services found are: no team's agent uses it, no key is asked for and nothing is sent to the service.
The computer's GitHub token (added in 0.148; ADR 0059, ADR 0044; phase 10 step 06d). The token the owner pastes for GitHub is kept by the connector key store (the OS keychain, else `connectors.json` in the state folder) under the account `machine:github`, with the login it belongs to, never in `machine.db`, a team's files, an event or a log. It is read by two things only: the hub's GitHub client, which sends it to `api.github.com`, and the clone of `github.copy`. It is never shown again, never given to an agent or put in a session's environment, and a refusal never quotes it. Phase 7's kits that take a GitHub key (step 07c) keep their own, per agent.

What the daily reminder reads of Claude Code and GitHub (added in 0.151; ADR 0059; phase 10 step 07). Of Claude Code's folder it opens one more file, `mcp-needs-auth-cache.json`, and only when it is a regular file of at most 1 MB: its top-level keys, the names of the connectors Claude Code says need signing in again, and nothing under them. The services reader above still never opens it (changed in 0.151). Of a session's transcript the `TodoWrite` call's count of items whose status is not `completed` is kept with the tool call, and no to-do text is. Through the computer's GitHub token (read only, 4.4) the client reads, for each of at most 50 repositories that have a scheduled workflow, `GET /repos/{full}/actions/workflows` for each workflow's `state`, `GET /repos/{full}/actions/workflows/{file}/runs?event=schedule&per_page=1` for the last scheduled run's `conclusion` and `run_started_at`, and `GET /repos/{full}/deployments?per_page=1` and that deployment's `statuses?per_page=1` for the environment and latest state (Vercel, Netlify and Render report theirs there), at the reminder's time and at the daily rescan; each answer is read for those fields alone.

Services found for a team made from the proposal (added in 0.150; ADR 0059; phase 10 step 06e). When a team is made from the proposal, the services its projects use through Claude are written to `.catervas/local/found-services.json` as `[{ service_id, name }]`, a file that stays on this computer. `team.get` answers `found_services: [{ agent, server, service_id, name }]`: for each service in the file, the first active agent whose role's kit offers a connector whose catalog id is that service's and who does not hold it. Today lists each after the connections agents asked for, as "You use Zoho Books with Claude. Connect it for Finn?" with Connect and Not now, which hides the pair as it hides any other. A kit that offers nothing for a service gives no suggestion for it.

Each role ships a kit, `roles/<role>/kit.yaml`, validated against `kit.schema.json` (ADR 0020; `docs/design/role-kits.md`): the skills it carries, in the Agent Skills format of section 6, and the connectors it may be given, each an MCP server (5.6) with its setup copy for the wizard, the credential keys it needs, every tool tagged by the kit, and its tool list pinned so that a test fails when the service's list drifts, each pin update re-reviewing the tags. Every connector is optional; a role works without any. The user connects one by signing in or pasting a key from the page the copy names, never by tagging a tool, in the web app's connector screens or with `catervas connect <agent> <connector>` and `catervas disconnect <agent> <connector>`; `connector.connected` and `connector.disconnected` record it (8.5). Credentials are per agent. A kit's connector is connected this way from phase 7 step 05, and signing in from step 03; a server of the user's own is connected now, with pasted keys, as the last paragraph of this section says (added in 0.38). Kits are free (section 9).

A connector's tool is tagged `network`, a read-only remote call that runs; `external_effect`, a call that changes something outside the sandbox, which runs without asking and is recorded (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061); `paid`, a call the service charges for or spends the user's credits on, which asks; or `denied`, never offered to the agent. It is never `read`, which means the project's files: a remote read is an outbound call carrying arguments the agent chose. Connecting a connector gives the agent that server's tagged tools whatever the agent's own tiers; the tag governs the call.

A tool that spends the user's credits, generating or editing one image or one video clip, is `paid` and carries an allowance (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: Kit's email drafts are `external_effect` and run without asking, with no allowance): the number of calls per UTC day (5.5; changed in 0.116; ADR 0062) that are pre-approved, per tool and per agent, set by the user when connecting from the kit's default. A call beyond the allowance asks the human as any `paid` call does, and the human may raise it. A batch tool, and any `paid` tool that publishes, sends, posts or pays, has no allowance and always asks, unless the owner's approved marketing plan covers the act (6.5; ADR 0042; added in 0.52), as does one a kit judges too costly to pre-approve: a 3D model, a video edit priced by its length, an analysis, or a change to the account's library. A voice-over always asks as well (added in 0.51), because Higgsfield's `generate_audio` can copy a voice from a sample of audio and a kit cannot refuse one argument of a tool, so the human sees the whole input of every one. An image may use an identity the user trained in their own account, which no kit trains, so using it is the user's earlier choice. The count is a projection of the `tool.called` events the hook records for every call (8.5), and the board shows it against the allowance beside the model spend. An allowance counts calls, not money, because Catervas cannot price another service's credits. Everything a connector returns is untrusted content (8.6), and a message read from a chat bridge answers no question and approves nothing.

Allowances in the team file (added in 0.45; ADR 0037). A kit entry in `team.yaml` may hold `allowances: { <tool>: 0..1000 }`, per agent: `allowance_not_kit` on an entry that is not `source: kit`, `allowance_not_paid` for a tool it does not tag `paid` (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: a team file written before may still give one for an `external_effect` tool, and loads), each at `/agents/<i>/mcp_servers/<j>/allowances/<tool>`. `spec_sha256` holds `allowances` only when it is not empty, so a commit that raises one makes the server "Connect again". At connect each starts at the kit's `calls`; `connector.connect` and `catervas connect --allowance <tool>=<n>` (kit connectors only, `kit_names_these` otherwise) set them, `allowance_not_offered` refuses a tool the kit gives none, `allowance_out_of_range` a number outside 0 to 1,000. `connector.allowances { agent, server, allowances }` changes them without the key; a tool left out keeps its number: the kept entry must be the team file's (`connector_not_confirmed`), and a service the kit has since changed is `connector_not_in_kit`. A change applies from the agent's next session and does not allow a call that waits. The period is the UTC day (changed in 0.116; ADR 0062). The count is every `tool.called` of that agent, server and full tool name in the period, a call a grant allowed among them, so it may exceed the allowance (the board and Costs show "21 of 20 images" and say "Extra images were ones you approved."). The query `allowances.list {}` answers `{ period, rows: [{ agent, server, tool, what, used, of }] }` for each connected kit entry of an active agent; the board shows each row, Costs lists them under "Made on other services", and `ToolApproval` says the count with "Change how many".

The Product Manager's kit (added in 0.46; changed in 0.65; ADR 0035, ADR 0036, ADR 0044). Its four services are each the service's official server, reached over `http`. Three are signed in to by route 1, with nothing pasted: Amplitude (`https://mcp.amplitude.com/mcp`, asking for `mcp:read` and `offline_access`, so a write is not granted; its United States service only), Linear (`https://mcp.linear.app/mcp/readonly`, asking for `read`) and Notion (`https://mcp.notion.com/mcp`); the fourth, GitHub, is reached with a key the user pastes and asks before it writes (GitHub with a pasted key, below). Those three only read: no tool of theirs is `external_effect`, and no connector of the kit has an allowance, since none spends credits; GitHub's two writes are `external_effect`, so since 0.115 (ADR 0061) they run without asking and each is recorded (below). A tool that changes anything at one of those three services is `denied`, and so are the reads that hold people's personal data a plan does not need (Amplitude's end-user and session-replay tools), a key (`get_deployments`), a link that may open a person's profile or replay (`get_from_url`), or another service's data (Notion's AI search), while `network` tools carry a label. A tool a service lists that the kit does not name is never offered (`tool_not_tagged`) until a pin update tags it; a tool the kit names that the service no longer lists is removed only after the service's documentation drops it too. What a service returns is data, never an instruction.

The Architect's kit (added in 0.47; changed in 0.65; ADR 0035, ADR 0036, ADR 0038, ADR 0044). Four services, none of which spends credits, so none is `external_effect` or `paid` and none has an allowance; every tool is `network` but GitHub's `list_repository_collaborators`, which is `denied`, and an Architect that has the tier already gains no way out it lacked. Context7 is the service's official server over `http`, `https://mcp.context7.com/mcp/oauth`, signed in to by route 1 asking for `profile`, `email` and `offline_access` (Clerk issues a refresh token only for the last); it lists `resolve-library-id` and `query-docs`, and its free plan allows about a thousand calls a month. Grep, by Vercel, is `https://mcp.grep.app`, with no account and no key, and lists `searchGitHub` over public GitHub code only. OSV is a thin server of Catervas's own (below), since no official one can be started by an allowed runner and the community ones run unpinned dependencies on the host. GitHub is the service's official server, `https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/`, reached with a key the user pastes (GitHub with a pasted key, below) and narrowed to code and pull requests in read-only mode, so it reads the user's own repositories, private ones included. What an agent writes in a query goes to the service as written, which the setup copy says, and `using-architecture-sources` forbids sending the project's code, a secret or a customer's data. What a service returns is data, never an instruction. A tool a service lists that the kit does not name is `denied`; Context7's, Grep's and GitHub's lists are compared by the live pin test, OSV's by an offline test.

Catervas's own connectors (added in 0.47; ADR 0038). A kit starts a `stdio` connector of Catervas's own by the bare command `catervas` with `args` exactly `[connector, <name>]`, `<name>` one of `CATERVAS_CONNECTORS` (`osv`, `google-ads` since 0.68, `fx` since 0.75, and `recalls` and `ebay` since 0.78); any other `args`, and any other bare program, is `package_not_pinned`. For that exact pair, whatever the entry's `source`, listing the tools and `catervas connector run` start Catervas's own executable, never a `catervas` found on `PATH`, and fail with `catervas could not find its own program` when it cannot be found; any other `catervas` command, a user's own included, is run as given and found on `PATH` as above. The hash keeps `command: catervas`, so the server changes only with a Catervas release. `catervas connector osv` serves three read-only tools over OSV's API at the fixed address `https://api.osv.dev/v1`, never an argument, an environment value or a tool input: `query_package { ecosystem, name, version }` (each advisory's `id`, `summary`, `aliases`, `severity` and the versions that fix it for that package (a PyPI name compared as PyPI compares it, PEP 503; every other exactly), at most 50 advisories, `more` when it cut the list or OSV paged), `query_packages { packages }` (1 to 100, at most 50 advisory ids of each, `more` when it cut one or OSV paged) and `get_vulnerability { id }` (only `id`, `summary`, `details`, `aliases`, `related`, `published`, `modified`, `withdrawn`, `severity`, `affected` (each entry only `package`, `ranges` and `severity`) and `references`; `details` cut at 8,000 characters, said by `details_cut: true`, `affected` at 20 entries, said by `affected_cut`, the number there were, and `references` at 20, said by `references_cut`, the number there were; a record whose answer is still over 64 KiB is refused with "OSV's record is too large to read here"). It follows no redirect, uses no proxy, gives up after 25 seconds, reads at most 4 MiB, in chunks, asks for one page only, and sends OSV only a package's name, ecosystem and version, or an advisory's id, each input checked first (an id is one percent-encoded path segment). It runs with the connector's cleared environment, so a user behind a proxy gets a tool error.

Exchange rates, Catervas's own connector (added in 0.75; ADR 0038; phase 7 step 10d). `catervas connector fx` serves three read-only tools over Frankfurter's API, which publishes the central banks' reference rates with no account, at the fixed address `https://api.frankfurter.dev/v2`, never an argument, an environment value or a tool input: `latest_rates { base, quotes }` (`{ base, rates: { <quote>: { rate, date } } }`, each quote with the day Frankfurter gave it, since the banks it reads publish on different days; a quote Frankfurter gives no rate for is a tool error), `rate_on { base, quote, date }` (`{ date, base, quote, rate }`, `date` the day Frankfurter answered for, which may be earlier than the day asked, so a rate is never claimed for a day that had none) and `list_currencies {}` (`[{ code, name }]`, at most 400). Each input is checked before a request leaves: a code is three capital letters; `quotes` are 1 to 30 distinct codes, none the base; `quote` is not the base; a `date` is written `YYYY-MM-DD` exactly and is from 1999-01-04, the earliest day Catervas allows (Frankfurter answers some earlier days, the dirham on 1997-06-02 among them, and Catervas does not ask for them; changed in 0.75 after review), to today in UTC. It follows no redirect, uses no proxy, gives up after 15 seconds, reads at most 1 MiB, in chunks, builds its query from pairs and never by formatting it into the address, and sends Frankfurter only currency codes and a day. Whatever Frankfurter answers that is not rates, a redirect and an unknown code (422) included, is the one sentence "Frankfurter could not answer that; check the codes and the date", without its body, and an answer over 1 MiB is "Frankfurter's answer is too large". It runs with the connector's cleared environment, so a user behind a proxy gets a tool error. Its three tools are `network` in the Procurement Specialist's kit, and its pin is the offline test `fx_server_lists_the_kits_tools`, as OSV's is.

Safety recalls, Catervas's own connector (added in 0.78; ADR 0038; phase 7 step 10g). `catervas connector recalls` serves five read-only tools over the United States' product-safety and vehicle-safety agencies' public data, with no account, at three fixed addresses, never an argument, an environment value or a tool input: the Consumer Product Safety Commission's `https://www.saferproducts.gov/RestWebServices`, NHTSA's `https://api.nhtsa.gov` and NHTSA's VIN decoder, vPIC, at `https://vpic.nhtsa.dot.gov/api`. `product_recalls { words, field, since? }` searches the CPSC's recalls for `words` (1 to 100 characters) in one field, `title`, `product_name` or `product_type`, which the CPSC takes as `RecallTitle`, `ProductName` and `ProductType` (never `Title`, which it ignores while answering all it has), from the day `since` (an ISO date) on, and answers the newest 50 by date as `{ recalls, more }`, each `{ number, date, title, url, description, products, hazards, remedies, manufacturers, retailers, countries }`, a description over 2,000 characters cut and said by `description_cut: true`; its search is a plain text match, so the skill searches a product's name, then its type, then its maker's. `vehicle_recalls`, `vehicle_complaints` and `vehicle_safety_ratings`, each `{ make, model, model_year }`, answer NHTSA's: `{ recalls }` (each `{ campaign, date, component, summary, consequence, remedy, park_it, park_outside }`), `{ count, by_component, newest }` (a component counted once for a complaint, the 20 newest by the day filed, read as MM/DD/YYYY, each summary cut at 600 characters and said by `summary_cut: true`) and `{ ratings, more }` (each `{ vehicle, overall, frontal, side, rollover }`, for at most 10 versions of the car, an id that is not a positive whole number skipped). `decode_vin { vin }` answers the twelve fields of vPIC's decoding that name the car (`Make`, `Model`, `ModelYear`, `Trim`, `BodyClass`, `EngineCylinders`, `DisplacementL`, `FuelTypePrimary`, `DriveType`, `PlantCountry`, `ErrorCode`, `ErrorText`). Each input is checked before a request leaves: a make or a model is 1 to 40 ASCII letters, digits, spaces and hyphens, so it is one path segment; `model_year` is a whole number from 1950 to next year; a VIN is 17 capital letters and digits, none of them I, O or Q; `since` is a real day written `YYYY-MM-DD`. It follows no redirect, uses no proxy, gives up after 20 seconds, reads at most 4 MiB, in chunks (a vehicle's complaints 8 MiB, since a popular car's are several megabytes), builds its queries from pairs and its paths from segments, never by formatting them into an address, never asks for an address an answer carries, and sends the agencies only the agent's words, a make, a model, a year or a VIN. Whatever an agency answers that is not rows, a redirect included, is "The CPSC could not answer that" or "NHTSA could not answer that" (vPIC is NHTSA's), without its body, and an answer over the cap is "The CPSC's answer is too large; ask a narrower question" or "NHTSA's answer is too large to read here". It runs with the connector's cleared environment, so a user behind a proxy gets a tool error. It covers products and vehicles sold in the United States only; the EU's and Canada's lists are candidates a data pipeline may bring. Its five tools are `network` in the Procurement Specialist's kit, its pin is the offline test `recalls_server_lists_the_kits_tools`, and `live_catervas_servers_answer` calls each tool once at the real hosts, by hand.

eBay listings, Catervas's own connector (added in 0.78; ADR 0038, ADR 0039's amendment of 2026-10-07, ADR 0043; phase 7 step 10g). `catervas connector ebay` serves two read-only tools over eBay's official Browse API at the fixed address `https://api.ebay.com`, never an argument, an environment value or a tool input, with the user's own free eBay developer keys (`credential_keys` `EBAY_CLIENT_ID` and `EBAY_CLIENT_SECRET`, from `https://developer.ebay.com/my/keys`), which reach it only through the launcher's cleared environment (ADR 0030) and are held as secrets, never in an answer, an error or a log. With either key missing or empty it still lists both tools, and every call is the tool error "eBay is not set up; connect it again with your App ID and Cert ID" with nothing sent. At its first call it asks `POST /identity/v1/oauth2/token` for an application grant (`Authorization: Basic` of the two keys, `grant_type=client_credentials` and the scope `https://api.ebay.com/oauth/api_scope`) and keeps the token in memory, asking again when less than a minute of it remains (eBay's lasts 7,200 seconds and is believed for a day at most; two calls at once make one grant); the Basic header goes with the grant alone, and a search or an item request carries `Authorization: Bearer` of the token and nothing else. A search or an item that eBay refuses with 401 drops the token, so the next call asks for a new grant (changed in 0.78 after review). A grant refused (400, 401 or 403) is "eBay refused the App ID and Cert ID; connect it again with your production keys"; a 429 from either request is "eBay's limit for these keys is used up for now; try again later"; a 404 for an item is "eBay has no listing with that id; it may have ended"; any other refusal, a redirect included, is "eBay could not answer that", never with eBay's body. `search_items { words, marketplace, condition?, min_price?, max_price?, limit? }` searches fixed-price (Buy It Now) listings, asking prices and never bids, in `EBAY_US`, `EBAY_GB`, `EBAY_DE`, `EBAY_AU`, `EBAY_CA`, `EBAY_FR`, `EBAY_IT` or `EBAY_ES` (sent as `X-EBAY-C-MARKETPLACE-ID`), for `words` of 1 to 100 characters, `new` or `used`, a price from and to as a decimal text of up to 7 digits and 2 after the point (`min_price` not above `max_price`, with the marketplace's currency in the filter `price:[10..50],priceCurrency:GBP`) and 1 to 50 listings, 20 when left out, answering `{ items, total, more }`, each item `{ item_id, title, price, currency, condition, seller_feedback_score, seller_feedback_percent, location: { country, postal_code }, shipping?, url }`. `get_item { item_id }`, an id from a search (`v1|` and 6 to 20 digits, `|`, 1 to 20 digits), answers the same fields and the description as plain text (cut at 4,000 characters and said by `description_cut: true`), `return_terms` and at most 30 `item_specifics`. No answer carries a seller's username, which eBay's API License Agreement forbids collecting: only the seller's feedback score and percentage and the listing's address, which Catervas never asks for. A listing's title and description are the seller's words, untrusted (8.6). It follows no redirect, uses no proxy, gives up after 20 seconds, reads at most 4 MiB, in chunks, builds its query from pairs and its path from segments, and sends eBay only the agent's words and filters. Its two tools are `network` in the Procurement Specialist's kit, its pin is the offline test `ebay_server_lists_the_kits_tools` (with two obviously fake keys, and another without either), and `live_catervas_servers_answer` calls each tool once at eBay with the founder's keys in `CATERVAS_KIT_EBAY_EBAY_CLIENT_ID` and `CATERVAS_KIT_EBAY_EBAY_CLIENT_SECRET`.

The built-in connector (added in 0.33; ADR 0026). Before any kit, Catervas ships one connector of its own, Playwright (5.6), held to the same rules: the `container` connector `playwright` of the UI/UX Designer's kit, `roles/ui_ux_designer/kit.yaml` (changed in 0.44, from `crates/roles/connectors/playwright.yaml`), pins its image by digest (`@playwright/mcp` 0.0.82 on 2026-09-30), names the folder its Playwright is kept in, and tags every tool the image lists, the browsing tools `network` and every other `denied`. A test in Docker lists the pinned image's tools against the kit, and a tool a new pin adds goes in as `denied` in the same change, until a plan tags it ("add each as denied in roles/ui_ux_designer/kit.yaml"). `builtin_connector(name)` answers what the kit holds; the team file still names it `{ name: playwright, source: builtin }`.

The Marketing Specialist's kit (added in 0.51; ADR 0035, ADR 0036, ADR 0037, ADR 0040). Two creative services, each the service's official server over `http` and signed in to by route 1, with nothing pasted, and each spending the user's credits; the posting and email services follow in the next paragraph. Higgsfield (`https://mcp.higgsfield.ai/mcp`, asking for `openid`, `email` and `offline_access`) needs a paid plan, and every generation through an agent uses credits whatever the plan, which its setup copy says. Recraft (`https://mcp.recraft.ai/mcp`, asking for `openid`, `email` and `profile`) has no `offline_access` scope and no revocation address, so its grant may lapse when it expires and the agent then shows "Sign in again", which its setup copy says too. A tool that makes one image, clip or edit is `paid` with an allowance (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061; it was `external_effect`): Higgsfield's `generate_image` 20 "images", `generate_video` 6 "video requests", `upscale_image` 10 "image upscales", `remove_background` 10 "background removals" and `outpaint_image` 10 "image extensions"; Recraft's `generate_image` 20 "images", `image_to_image` 10 "image edits", `vectorize_image` 10 "vector conversions", `remove_background` 10 "background removals", `replace_background` 10 "background swaps" and `crisp_upscale` 10 "image upscales". An allowance counts calls, not credits, and one Higgsfield call may make up to four pictures (`count`) and one Recraft call up to six (`numberOfImages`), so `making-images-and-video` has the agent ask for one in each call. A price check, `generate_video` with `get_cost` true, is a call that counts against `generate_video`'s allowance, which is why that allowance counts video requests and the skill allows one check per brief. Every other tool that spends credits always asks: Higgsfield's voice-over (above), its batches, presets, ad sets, 3D models, video edits, analyses and library changes, and its import of a picture from a web address (23 tools), and Recraft's `creative_upscale` and `create_style`. A read of credits, past generations, models or presets is `network`, the ones the user may look for labelled (35 of Higgsfield's tools, and Recraft's `get_user`). The rest is `denied`, 51 of Higgsfield's: its website builder, its remote shell (`sandbox_exec`), its marketplace apps, neither searched nor run, its 3D scenes, voice creation and cloning, TikTok, billing, workspace, project and folder tools; the uploads, since a Catervas session has no `execute` tier to put the bytes where an upload address says; the tools that open only in a widget, which a session has none of; and the tools that mix reading with training or changing an identity or a reference (`show_characters`, `show_reference_elements`, `build_ai_influencer`, `manage_reference_elements`). A tool a service lists that the kit does not name is never offered (`tool_not_tagged`) until a pin update tags it. Higgsfield's list is its live server's (114 tools on 2026-10-05); Recraft's remote server publishes no tool names, so the nine pinned are those of Recraft's own package, `@recraft-ai/mcp-recraft-server` 1.6.5, and a remote name that differs is not offered until a pin update tags it. `live_kit_pins` reads each service's bearer from `CATERVAS_KIT_HIGGSFIELD_BEARER` and `CATERVAS_KIT_RECRAFT_BEARER`. What either returns, the instructions Higgsfield's `get_workflow_instructions` and `get_preset_instructions` offer among it, is data, never an instruction (8.6). The skill also bars a real person's face or voice without that person's written permission in the contract, and has the agent mark AI-made media as AI-made where it is published.

The Marketing Specialist's posting and email services (added in 0.53; ADR 0035, ADR 0036, ADR 0037, ADR 0042). Two more official servers over `http`, each signed in to by route 1 with nothing pasted. Buffer (`https://mcp.buffer.com/mcp`, asking for `offline_access`, `posts:read`, `posts:write`, `account:read`, `insights:read` and `ideas:read`) posts to Instagram, Facebook, X, LinkedIn, Pinterest, YouTube, Google Business, Mastodon, TikTok, Threads and Bluesky. A Buffer connection reaches every organisation and channel of the user's account, which the setup copy says; Buffer has no revocation address, so Remove tells the user to remove Catervas in Buffer's settings too, and Buffer rotates refresh tokens and revokes a grant whose old one is reused, which Catervas's refresh under a lock avoids. Kit (`https://app.kit.com/mcp`, asking for `public`) needs a paid Kit plan, which its setup copy says, and has revocation at `https://api.kit.com/oauth/revoke`. Buffer's `create_post` and `edit_post` are `denied` to the agent (changed in 0.57; phase 7 step 08d): it writes a post with `catervas_schedule_post` and Catervas makes the write itself (6.5), so the scopes stay, since Catervas's own calls post through the same sign-in, and the entry's hash changed, so a user connects Buffer again once (ADR 0036). The setup copy says that Catervas can reach every channel of the account, that a post in a plan the owner approved shows on Today before it goes out with a Stop button, and that Catervas asks about any other. Kit's broadcast tools only draft: `create_broadcast` and `update_broadcast` make or change a draft, and scheduling and sending stay in Kit's own editor, through the `confirm_url` the draft returns and the completion note carries, so nothing reaches a subscriber until the human sends it. They are `external_effect` and, since 0.115 (ADR 0061), run without asking and are recorded, with no allowance (they had one of 10 "email drafts" each). Kit's sequence, sequence-email, landing-page and snippet writes change what a subscriber or the public sees (a sequence email is live once it is `published`, which the skill forbids and a hook cannot see), so each is `external_effect` and, since 0.115, runs without asking and is recorded, as do `list_forms` and `get_landing_page`, reads that Kit marks as writes because resolving a public address can queue a rebuild of saved content. A read of posts, channels, campaigns or their numbers is `network` (10 of Buffer's 20 tools and 31 of Kit's 83). The rest is `denied`: every deletion, since a post or an email cannot be taken back; Buffer's idea and template writes and its generic `introspect_schema`, `execute_query` and `execute_mutation`, which reach the whole API and so cannot be tagged, and, since 0.57, `create_post` and `edit_post` (10 of Buffer's); and, in Kit (40 of its 83), every write to subscribers, tags, custom fields, products, colours or webhooks, `unsubscribe` among them, every bulk tool, `list_tax_codes` and `list_webhooks`, and every read of a subscriber's or a buyer's own data, for the reason the Product Manager's kit denies Amplitude's end-user tools: a campaign needs totals, not people. A tool a service lists that the kit does not name is never offered (`tool_not_tagged`) until a pin update tags it. Buffer's twenty tools are those of its published guide to its server and Kit's 83 those of its help centre's list of its connector's tools (both read 2026-10-05); `live_kit_pins` reads their bearers from `CATERVAS_KIT_BUFFER_BEARER` and `CATERVAS_KIT_KIT_BEARER`. The role's words change with them: its prompt, its `forbidden` list and its skills no longer say it never publishes. Since step 08c (changed in 0.55) its `forbidden` list says it publishes, sends or spends money except through a `paid` call the owner allows or the owner's approved marketing plan (6.5), and since step 08d (changed in 0.57) its skills say that a social post goes out through `catervas_schedule_post`, in the plan or outside it with a Stop on Today (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061), that an email is a draft the human sends, and that otherwise the human publishes; the plan's ads are Google Ads' (added in 0.68). The ninth skill, `posting-and-email`, is the email skill since 0.57 (its posting rules went to `running-social-channels`, the kit's fourteenth skill, which has the agent read `list_channels`, fill the active plan's slots with `catervas_schedule_post` at least three hours ahead and on the slot's day in the business's own offset, with `details` for YouTube and Pinterest, use only the business's own pictures, ones the owner gave it or ones it made, and read results with `get_aggregated_post_metrics` before the next plan). It has the agent hand over a broadcast's `confirm_url`, keep a series' emails unpublished, keep each email or page under the 64 KiB input limit, a longer one becoming two emails in a series or a shorter page, since Kit's updates replace the whole body (`tool_input_too_large`), and never put a subscriber's details in a prompt or a note. Search-engine data (Semrush) is not in the kit: it publishes no tool names and its access goes in the request body, which Catervas's header cannot set; per-network servers are not in it either, since X's own server cannot post and charges per post, Meta admits only listed clients, and LinkedIn, TikTok and YouTube have none.

The Finance Specialist's kit (added in 0.67; ADR 0019's amendment of 2026-10-07, ADR 0035, ADR 0036). Six skills, `categorising-expenses`, `closing-the-month`, `forecasting`, `unit-economics-and-pricing`, `recommending-a-budget` and `using-finance-sources`, and three services, each the service's official server over `http` and signed in to by route 1, with nothing pasted. Stripe (`https://mcp.stripe.com`) asks for the one scope `mcp`, pinned because with none named Catervas would ask for every scope the server advertises, a wider one added later among them; Digits (`https://api.digits.com/mcp`) names none; Kick (`https://use.kick.co/mcp`) asks for `mcp:read` alone, which Kick documents as the scope for any call that only looks up data, so a write is refused at Kick as well as here. Digits and Kick are bookkeeping services a business may already keep its books in, which the role reads in place of rebuilding them, and are not Kit, the Marketing Specialist's email service; each is the business's own account, and Catervas adds nothing to its cost. The role only reads: seven of Stripe's ten tools, nine of Digits' ten and seventeen of Kick's 39 are `network`, each with a label, and the rest are `denied`, which is every tool that writes whatever it writes (`stripe_api_write`, Kick's `*_act`, `*_create` and `*_update` tools and `activity_undo`), `send_stripe_feedback`, which sends something to Stripe's company, `stripe_implementation_planner`, which builds an integration and reads no numbers, `list_business_users`, the people with access to the books, which the role does not need, and Kick's `list_kick_skills` and `load_kick_skill`, which load Kick's own instructions into the session, where the role's instructions are Catervas's skills and a service's words are data (8.6). No tool is `external_effect`, so no service has an allowance. A service lists the tools its grant allows (Kick: “Available Kick tools can vary by token scope”), so a pinned tool a grant does not list costs nothing (ADR 0036), and the live pin test lists each service with a bearer from a sign-in granted widely, which the kit never asks for. The skills' rules: a category is one line of the books' `Categories` sheet, and a new one has a reason in its row's note, with no tax category given as advice; a month is closed only when every difference between Stripe, the ledger, Catervas's costs and the books of more than one per cent is explained in a row's note with both figures, by a `Status` cell on the month's `Monthly summary` row reading `closed`; a forecast has a method named, a range, its assumptions on a sheet of their own, and its date and inputs; a price change and a budget are recommendations the user decides, a daily limit in Settings (5.5); and every figure from a service names its source and its dates. Stripe's tools are those of its documentation, Digits' of its help page for its server and Kick's 39 of its tool reference (each read 2026-10-07); `live_kit_pins` reads their bearers from `CATERVAS_KIT_STRIPE_BEARER`, `CATERVAS_KIT_DIGITS_BEARER` and `CATERVAS_KIT_KICK_BEARER`. QuickBooks Online is not in the kit: whether its registration accepts Catervas is for a later step to probe, and Xero's server registers no client by itself, so it waits for Catervas Cloud.

The Procurement Specialist's kit (added in 0.75; ADR 0039 and its amendments of 2026-10-07, ADR 0035, ADR 0036, ADR 0038, ADR 0043; phase 7 step 10d). Fourteen skills (twelve when it was added in 0.75; `requesting-a-data-pipeline` since 0.76 and `contacting-sellers` since 0.77, in 6.10), `defining-the-need`, `finding-sellers-and-makers`, `comparing-offers`, `reading-terms-and-pricing`, `checking-a-seller`, `checking-product-safety`, `estimating-landed-cost`, `checking-a-used-vehicle`, `keeping-the-vendor-register`, `reviewing-renewals`, `writing-purchase-orders`, `using-procurement-sources`, `requesting-a-data-pipeline` and `contacting-sellers`, each written for any product, and seven services (five when it was added in 0.75; `recalls` and `ebay` since 0.78), in this order, none of which can buy, check out, sign or send. `fx`, `recalls` and `ebay` are Catervas's own (above). Exa (`https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp`, its official server, with no key and no sign-in) is searched and never asked for a page: `web_search_exa` is `network`, and `web_fetch_exa` is `denied`, because Exa fetches on its own servers and follows a redirect to another site, which the approved-sites check cannot see (8.6). SerpApi (`https://mcp.serpapi.com/mcp`, its official server) takes the user's own key, pasted and sent as a bearer header; its `search` takes any engine's parameters, the shops' engines being `google_shopping`, `amazon`, `ebay` and `walmart` (the skill uses `google_shopping`, `amazon` and `walmart` and reads eBay only through `ebay`, 6.10, changed in 0.78; the lens and reverse-image engines, `google_lens`, `yandex_images`, `google_reverse_image`, `bing_reverse_image` and `google_ai_mode`, make SerpApi fetch an address on its own servers, which its setup says in plain words and 8.6 records; added in 0.75 after review), and spends one of the user's searches, so it is `paid` (changed in 0.115; it was `external_effect`) with an allowance of 50 calls, "shopping searches", and a search past the allowance asks the human before it reaches SerpApi; `search_table` and `search_dashboard` are `denied`, being on-screen versions of `search` that take the same parameters and spend searches too. Brex (`https://api.brex.com/mcp`, its official server) is signed in to by route 1, asking for `offline_access`, `vendors.readonly`, `expenses.card.readonly` and `departments.readonly`, so a write is refused at Brex as well as here (its bills scope, `expenses.bill`, also writes and is not asked): eleven of its 43 tools are `network` (vendors, bills, merchants and their categories, expense categories and analytics, card charges and departments), each with a label, and thirty-two are `denied`, every one that writes, the people tools, which carry card holders and limits, and the card, limit, bank, reward, travel, accounting and set-up tools; before anyone signs in, an account admin or card admin in Brex accepts its Developer API agreement. AWS Pricing (`uvx awslabs.aws-pricing-mcp-server==1.1.1`, AWS Labs' official server, which needs the program `uv`) takes the user's `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, of a user allowed only the five pricing reads: six of its nine tools are `network`, and `analyze_cdk_project`, `analyze_terraform_project` and `generate_cost_report` are `denied`, since they read or write a path the agent names on the user's computer, where a server run on the host runs. Its first run downloads Python and the package and may outlast the 30-second listing limit, so the user connects again, and the second run is served from `uv`'s cache. Every service is optional, and the kit carries no credential of Catervas's (ADR 0043). The skills' rules: the rule that the agent never places, pays for, confirms or cancels an order is said in `writing-purchase-orders` alone, where an order is written; the skills no longer speak of approved sites, the agent may open any page (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061); the agent never recommends a product with an open recall and never says a car is sound; with "Safety recalls" connected it searches a product's recalls by name, then by type, then by its maker's name, and reads a used car's VIN by `decode_vin`, then `vehicle_recalls`, `vehicle_complaints` and `vehicle_safety_ratings`, keeping the request for the agencies' own pages as the fallback (changed in 0.78); from Brex it reports vendors and amounts, never people; it never sets Exa's `category` to `people`; and without `fx` it keeps each price in the seller's currency and converts nothing by guess. Exa's and SerpApi's tools are from their keyless `tools/list`, AWS Pricing's from its package's registrations (read 2026-10-08) and Brex's from its documentation (2026-10-05 and 2026-10-07); `live_kit_pins` reads Brex's bearer, an API token which its server accepts, from `CATERVAS_KIT_BREX_BEARER`, SerpApi's key from `CATERVAS_KIT_SERPAPI_SERPAPI_KEY` and AWS's from `CATERVAS_KIT_AWS_PRICING_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `CATERVAS_KIT_AWS_PRICING_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, and `fx`, `recalls` and `ebay` are pinned offline, the last two with `live_catervas_servers_answer` called by hand.

Catervas calls a connector's tool itself (added in 0.57; phase 7 step 08d, ADR 0042's amendment). `connectors::call_tool` makes one call of one tool of a server, beside `list_tools`, with the same start (a `stdio` server in its folder with only its keys and a few safe variables, an `http` one with its filled headers and bearer): one MCP session for the call, opened, `tools/call`, cancelled, within 30 seconds, past which it is `ConnectorError::Timeout`. It answers the result's structured content when there is one, else its first text block read as JSON, else `{ "text": <text> }`; a result marked as an error, and a JSON-RPC error to the call, are `ConnectorError::ToolError` with the text cut at 500 characters, which Catervas passes on only as untrusted words. Only a fixed list of Catervas's own calls is ever made, `OWN_CALLS` (`daemon/own_calls.rs`): Buffer's `get_channel`, `create_post` and `delete_post`; any other pair is refused before anything starts, and a later step that has Catervas call a service itself adds its pairs to the list and calls through `call_as`, never beside it. `call_as(state, agent, server, tool, arguments)` takes the named agent's kit entry from the team file, requires that the entry still matches its role's kit and that the connection is kept (`NotConnected` otherwise), runs it in the connector folder with Catervas's own program, and refreshes a signed-in entry first as a session's start does, within 60 seconds of its expiring, falling back to a token still good (a lapse is `SignInAgain`); an entry with keys is used as kept. Its errors are `NotListed`, `NotConnected`, `SignInAgain`, `Failed`, `Timeout` and `Tool`. A call of Catervas's is not the agent's: it passes no hook, may name a tool the kit tags `denied` (Buffer's `delete_post`), and is recorded as the `social_post.*` events (6.5), so it charges none of the agent's tool-call limit for an act that is the owner's; it uses the connection of the agent whose post it is, and a post of an agent whose Buffer entry is gone, lapsed or changed fails at hand-over, saying so.

A user's own connectors (added in 0.38; ADR 0030). Before any kit, the user can give one agent any MCP server: a program Catervas starts on this computer (`stdio`) or a web address spoken to over streamable HTTP (`http`; the older SSE transport is not accepted). Its entry in the agent's `mcp_servers` is `{ name, source: custom, transport, command, args, url, headers, credential_keys, tools }`, checked by `validate_team`, each refusal at its own field: `transport` is required with `source: custom` and absent with `builtin`, which takes none of these fields; `command` and `args` go with `stdio` alone and `command` is required there, a bare name found on `PATH` or a full path, so a `command` holding a `/` that does not start with one, such as `./server` or `bin/mcp`, is refused (`command_not_absolute`), `url` and `headers` with `http` alone and `url` is required there; `catervas` and a built-in's name are `connector_name_reserved`; a `url` starts `http://` or `https://` and holds no userinfo and no query (`url_holds_secret`), because it is written to the committed team file as it is, so a service whose address holds its key cannot be added yet; `headers` (at most 16) are templates that may hold `{KEY}` for a key in `credential_keys` and nothing else (`header_key_unknown`), and a header with a word, split at `-` and `_` in any case, of `authorization`, `cookie`, `key`, `apikey`, `token`, `secret`, `auth`, `password`, `passwd`, `pass`, `credential` or `credentials` in its name must hold one and no value beside it: split at spaces and `;`, each piece is a `{KEY}`, a `name={KEY}`, or, first, a scheme of a letter then letters and digits such as `Bearer` or `OAuth2` (`header_holds_secret`; beside a placeholder, and `Cookie`, added in 0.38 after review), so no secret is in the file; an argument is refused at its place (`arg_holds_secret`, added in 0.38 after review) when it is the value given to a flag that names a key, as `--api-key abc`, `--token=abc` or `--api-key -abc`, the value not a number and not a flag starting `--`; when it is `NAME=value` with a name that names a key, as `API_KEY=abc`; when it is a credential header with its value, as `mcp-remote` takes after `--header`; or when it is shaped like a well-known service's key (`sk-`, `sk_live_`, `sk_test_`, `rk_live_`, `rk_test_`, `ghp_`, `gho_`, `ghs_`, `github_pat_`, `glpat-`, `xoxb-`, `xoxp-`, or `AKIA` and 16 capitals and digits). A name names a key when its last word at `-` and `_` is `token`, `password`, `passwd`, `pass`, `secret`, `auth`, `pat`, `apikey`, `credential` or `credentials`, or its last two are `api key`, `access key` or `secret key`, and its first is not `no`: `--key`, `--sort-key`, `--primary-key`, `--max-token 4096` and `--no-auth` are settings, its value never quoted, since a server's key goes in `credential_keys` and reaches it in its environment; `credential_keys` are at most 8 names matching `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$`; and `tools` maps each tool to `network`, `external_effect`, `paid` or `denied` (`paid` added in 0.115; ADR 0061). Connecting lists the server's tools: Catervas starts it, or reaches it, with the agent's keys, through the launcher's clean environment (8.2), and gives up after thirty seconds. A tool whose name falls outside `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$`, which Claude Code would rewrite, is shown as one Catervas can't use and is not written, so a call to it is `tool_not_tagged`. The user labels each other tool; one left unlabelled is written `paid` (changed in 0.115; it was `external_effect`), so a tool whose cost nobody stated still asks. The tools written at connect are the server's pin: a tool it lists later is `tool_not_tagged` until the user connects it again. The agent's keys are its own, never another agent's: Catervas keeps them in the OS keychain, service `catervas`, account `connector:<project_id>:<agent_id>:<server>`, where `<project_id>` is the project's id on this machine: 32 random hex digits made the first time it is needed and kept in the user's Catervas state folder at `projects/<sha256 of the project's canonical path>` (the folder 0700, the file 0600, refused unless it holds 32 hex digits), never in the project, and not the log's `project_id`, which is the folder's name, so two projects in folders of one name, a clone into a folder of the same name, or a copy of the project's folder never find each other's keys (changed in 0.38 after review). A project moved to another path is a new project here, and its connectors are connected again. Keys are kept as one JSON object `{ spec_sha256, keys }` holding only the keys the entry names, and a server with no keys still gets one. On a computer with no keychain they go to `connectors.json` in the user's Catervas state folder under the same account, the folder 0700 and the file 0600, written beside and renamed over while a lock file, `connectors.json.lock`, holds off any other process; Catervas reads both stores, so an entry kept in the file before a keychain appeared is still found. With neither, connecting is refused `no_secret_store`. `spec_sha256` is the sha256 of the canonical JSON (compact, object keys sorted at every depth) of the entry's `transport`, `command`, `args`, `url`, `headers`, `credential_keys` and `tools`; the name is not in it, being part of where the keys are kept. What was connected on this machine is what runs: an entry the team file changed since, by a clone, a pulled branch, a template or a hand edit, or one never connected here, is unconfirmed, and runs nothing and is sent no key until the user connects it again (8.2), so a commit can neither move a server's address nor relabel a `denied` tool `network`. A `stdio` server runs on the host as the user, with the user's rights, in sandbox mode too, and always in a folder Catervas keeps for it outside the repository, `connectors/<project id>/<agent>/<server>` in the user's Catervas state folder, removed and made again, empty and 0700, each time its tools are listed and each time a session starts it (changed in 0.38 after review). When that state folder is inside the project, as when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` points into it, no stdio server is listed or started, and the refusal `state_inside_project` says so on the page and at the command line (added in 0.38 after review). Connecting a server again while a session runs it removes and remakes the folder it runs in, so that server's writes into its folder fail until it next starts; this fails closed, and an agent runs one session at a time, the folder being the agent's (changed in 0.118; ADR 0064). Never in a task's worktree, which agents write to, nor anywhere in the repository: git checks out a file committed there on a clone or a pull, and `npx`, `uvx` and `uv run` look upward to the repository's root, so a planted `node_modules/.bin`, `.npmrc`, module, `pyproject.toml` or script would run on the host with the agent's keys.
