With no state folder (`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `HOME` and `APPDATA` all unset), no stdio server is listed or started. Outside the repository is all the folder promises: a command on `PATH` that itself reads a project, say one given the repository's path as an argument, is the user's own choice. A relative path in `args` resolves in that folder, so a script of the user's is given by its full path. The program is the one the user named: a bare name is found on `PATH`. On the command line (unix), `catervas connect <agent> <name> (--command <program> [--arg <a>]... | --url <url> [--header '<Name>: <template>']...) [--key <NAME>]... [--tag <tool>=network|external_effect|paid|denied]...` checks the entry against the team, reads each key's value from a line of standard input, without echo at a terminal, never from an argument, and refuses `--key NAME=value` without printing the value. It lists the tools in its own process, prints each with its tag, or that Catervas can't use it, labels a tool no `--tag` names `paid`, refuses a `--tag` for a tool the server did not list or one Catervas can't use (`tag_unknown_tool`, naming the tools it lists), so a misspelling never leaves the tool meant `paid` unsaid, and keeps the keys in its own process, so a key never crosses a socket. It then writes the team file and records `connector.connected` here, holding the run lock, when nothing drives the project, or else sends the command `connector_connect { agent, server, spec_sha256 }`, `server` the entry with no value in it; and it ends with "Kept in your computer's keychain" or "Kept in a private file only you can read". `--json` prints `{ tools, stored_in, said }`. `connector_connect` is refused when the entry breaks the team's rules, is not a custom server (`connector_not_custom`), or does not hash to `spec_sha256` (`connector_not_confirmed`). `catervas disconnect <agent> <name>` sends `connector_disconnect { agent, server }` first, which removes the entry and records `connector.disconnected` and is not found unless the agent has a custom server of that name, so a refused one deletes nothing; it then deletes that agent's keys from both stores and touches no other agent's. Keys are kept before the command runs, so a command refused after its check leaves keys with no entry, which run nothing and are replaced by the next connect. Retiring an agent, or removing it from the team by a save or a saved team applied, deletes its keys for each of its custom servers, and no other agent's; a save that takes one custom server from an agent deletes that agent's keys for it (added in 0.38 after review). A server that fails to answer, or to list its tools, is said to have failed in Catervas's words alone: its own error text, which may quote what it was sent, is not repeated. The web app does the same through three RPCs (F9).
Signing in to a service (added in 0.41; ADR 0033). An `http` server, or Catervas's own connector (a `stdio` entry that is exactly `catervas connector <name>`, ADR 0038; amended in 0.59), may be signed in to instead of given keys: its entry then holds `oauth: { client_id?, callback_port?, scopes? }`, and the presence of `oauth` means "signed in". `client_id` is a public client the service's app registration gave Catervas, at most 200 characters; `callback_port`, from 1024 to 65535, goes with `client_id` alone (`callback_port_without_client`); `scopes` are at most 16, each of RFC 6749's scope characters, so none holds a space or a quote. `validate_team` refuses `oauth` on a `stdio` server (`oauth_on_stdio`) unless it is exactly Catervas's own connector's pair, the command `catervas` and the arguments `connector` and a word matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$` (the kit loader holds the word to Catervas's own connectors), on which `client_id` and `callback_port` are refused (`catervas_connector_client`: the app's id and port are Catervas's); it refuses `oauth` beside `credential_keys` (`oauth_with_keys`) and beside a header named `Authorization` in any case (`oauth_header_conflict`), each at its field. `spec_sha256` holds `"oauth": { client_id, callback_port, scopes }` only when `oauth` is present, so every entry connected before keeps its hash, and a change to one of the three makes the server "Connect again". Catervas runs the sign-in, in the daemon for the web app and in `catervas connect`'s own process for the command line, through `rmcp`'s OAuth client with Catervas's own checks around it, because Claude Code's `-p` cannot sign in and keeps its tokens by its config folder, not by agent. It asks the server to initialize without a token and follows the `resource_metadata` of its 401's `WWW-Authenticate` (RFC 9728) and nothing else: a server that does not point to its metadata is `sign_in_not_offered`, and no endpoint is guessed. The authorization server must say it does PKCE with `S256` (`pkce_not_supported` otherwise, before anything is registered), name an `issuer`, and offer either a `registration_endpoint` or have the team file's `client_id` (`sign_in_not_supported` otherwise); every URL it names, the server's own, and every redirect Catervas is sent along must be `https`, or `http` on this computer's loopback, which the tests need, or the sign-in fails naming it. Registration, in order: the `client_id` of the entry, with no registration request, else dynamic client registration (`client_name` `Catervas`, `application_type` `native`, `token_endpoint_auth_method` `none`, this attempt's redirect), once per sign-in, else `sign_in_not_supported`. Catervas takes no client secret from a team file or from a user: it is a public client. No build uses a secret of Catervas's: from phase 11 Catervas Cloud adds one where a service needs it (below; changed in 0.61, ADR 0044). The redirect is `http://localhost:<port>/callback`, `localhost` because authorization servers match a registered address exactly; the listener binds `127.0.0.1` and, where there is IPv6, `[::1]`, never every address, on a free port tried up to five times, or on `callback_port` (33418 when none is given) for a given client, which fails `sign_in_failed` naming the port when it is taken. It answers the first `GET /callback` whose `state` is the attempt's, a random single-use value, with a plain page, the Catervas mark, a headline and a sentence, that says how it went from Catervas's own reason and quotes nothing the service sent, no link and no script, `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; img-src data:`, `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, and closes; another path is 404 and another `state` 400, neither ending the attempt. An attempt lasts ten minutes (`sign_in_timed_out`), and a new one for the same agent and server ends the old. So does the page's Cancel: `connector.sign_in_cancel { attempt }` stops the attempt's polling or its listener, waits for that, and drops the attempt with whatever the service gave it, a grant approved already included, so a sign-in the person says yes to after Cancel is never kept; an attempt already gone or used up is not a refusal, and the answer is `{}`. `iss` (RFC 9207), when the callback carries one, must equal the metadata's `issuer`, and must be there when the metadata says `authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported`, else `sign_in_mismatch`, an error callback with another `iss` included, whose `error` is then not shown; `error=access_denied` is `access_denied`. `resource` (RFC 8707) is the protected-resource metadata's, which must be the server's address or a path above it, and is sent on the authorization, token and refresh requests. The grant, `{ issuer, resource, client_id, token_endpoint, revocation_endpoint?, access_token, refresh_token?, issued_at, expires_at?, scopes, lapsed }`, is kept in the agent's entry, in the keychain or `connectors.json` beside any keys, under the same account, and never prints. Refresh and revocation are Catervas's own form requests to the grant's endpoints, through the same check: a session setup refreshes a token that would expire within the session's wall clock and five minutes, the launch route one that would within a minute, saving a rotated refresh token before the new access token is used, under one lock per entry that connect, disconnect and the deletes of removing an agent or a server also take, so a token refreshed while the entry is removed is not kept. A refresh the service refuses with `invalid_grant`, `invalid_client` or `unauthorized_client` lapses the grant: the server is left out of sessions and `team.get` says `sign_in_again`; any other failure uses a token that is still good, and leaves the server out of that session alone when it is not. Remove deletes the entry and then asks the service, within five seconds and without failing the removal, to forget the grant (RFC 7009), the refresh token first; connecting again over another grant asks it to forget the one replaced, unless that is the grant just kept or its client's. A refreshed grant is not saved over an entry that was deleted or changed outside the daemon's lock, and the token just rotated is revoked instead. The page says "Signed in to <host>" for a signed-in row; a lapsed row says "<host> ended Catervas's sign-in. Sign in again to use it." with "Sign in again", which opens `ConnectorAdd` filled in from the team file at the sign-in; Remove says Catervas deletes the sign-in and asks the service to forget it, or, where the service has no revocation endpoint, that to remove Catervas completely the user also removes it in the service's settings. On `ConnectorAdd`, Next for a web address with no key typed asks the service first: where it offers signing in the page shows "Sign in with <issuer host>", with "for <address host>" beneath it when the two differ, opens the page in a new tab in the click itself, and checks every two seconds, then "Signed in to <host>" and on to labelling; "Use a key instead" shows the key fields, and a service that does not offer, or cannot be signed in to, shows them, with a sentence for the last two. On the command line, `catervas connect <agent> <name> --url <url> --sign-in [--client-id <id> [--callback-port <port>]] [--scope <s>]... [--tag <tool>=...]...` conflicts with `--key` and `--command`, writes `Sign in to <host> in your browser: <url>` to the error stream, opens it with the system's opener (an opener that fails is no error), waits ten minutes, writes `Signed in to <issuer>.` there, then prints the tools and where the sign-in is kept; `catervas disconnect` asks the service to forget a sign-in it held. The loopback redirect assumes the browser and the daemon share a computer, which the daemon's serving `127.0.0.1` alone guarantees (8.6).

Catervas's own apps (added in 0.58; ADR 0035, route 2; phase 7 step 03b). A service that registers no client by itself but takes a public one is signed in to with an app Catervas registered with it, so that the user makes none. `catervas_runtime::registered_apps::REGISTERED_APPS` is a static table with one `RegisteredApp` per app: its `id`, its `name` (what the screens call it), the one `host` it serves (none for an app that signs in for one of Catervas's own connectors, which serves no address), the `catervas_connector` it signs in for (if any), its `flow`, its public `client_id`, the `client_secret` a service insists on for a client it calls public (if any), the `scopes` it asks for, its `issuer`, its `token_endpoint`, a `revocation_endpoint` when it has one, an `install_url` when the app must be installed on what an agent is to read, and a `settings_url`, the page where the user removes the app at the service. It ships with no entry (changed in 0.61, ADR 0044): Catervas's GitHub App (host `api.githubcopilot.com`) and Catervas's Google app are registered in phase 11 and held by Catervas Cloud, never in a build, so no sign-in runs on the table yet, and for GitHub's address `ConnectorAdd` falls to the key fields, where a fine-grained token is pasted; the tests pass tables of their own, which the daemon takes from `DaemonState::set_registered_apps` and the command line from `CliIo`. An app is matched by the server's address alone, before any discovery, and never by what the server's metadata says, since a server could name another authorization server and receive a token from Catervas's app: the address is parsed as a URL, its scheme is `https` on port 443 (or `http` on a loopback host, which the tests need), it holds no user name or password, and its host equals the app's, ignoring ASCII case, with no trailing dot. A `client_id` of an app's in the team file is used only for the address that app serves: for any other it is refused `sign_in_failed` ("this sign-in is only for <name>'s own servers") before any request; on that address, with no `client_id` of the user's own or with the app's, the app signs in and the team file's `scopes` are ignored; any other `client_id` runs the sign-in above unchanged. GitHub's flow is the device flow (RFC 8628): Catervas posts the `client_id` with no `scope`, since a GitHub App's permissions are set on the app, to the device endpoint; the answer's `verification_uri` must be the app's own page, else `sign_in_failed` before anything is polled; the user types the `user_code` on that page and says yes; and Catervas polls the token endpoint from inside `SignIn::finish`, so that dropping the attempt, as the daemon does to an old attempt for a new one, stops the polling, first after the answer's `interval` (5 seconds when it gives none, never under 1) and then at every interval, adding 5 seconds to every later wait for each `slow_down`. `authorization_pending` waits, `access_denied` is `access_denied`, `expired_token` and ten minutes from the start are `sign_in_timed_out`, and any other `error` is `sign_in_failed`. A poll whose answer is not the service's, a connection that fails, a reply that is not a JSON object (a gateway's 502 page) or a server error with no `error` code in it, does not end the sign-in: Catervas waits the interval and polls again, and ends it `sign_in_failed` after three such answers in a row, an address refused as not `https` ending it at once. Every request to the device and token endpoints, a refresh included, sends `Accept: application/json`, since GitHub otherwise answers form-encoded, and an `error` in an answer is read before its status, since GitHub answers one with 200. The device code never leaves Catervas, and no listener, `state` or PKCE is involved. The grant is step 03's with `app` (the app's `id`; a grant kept before this has none), an empty `scopes`, the app's issuer and token endpoint, the server's address as `resource` and no revocation endpoint, since revoking needs the client secret, which is never shipped or sent; so Remove cannot ask GitHub to forget it and says where to remove Catervas. A refresh of a grant with an `app` sends no `resource`, and `bad_refresh_token` and `incorrect_client_credentials` lapse any grant, as `invalid_grant` does. GitHub keeps at most 10 tokens for a user, an app and a scope and ends the oldest, so a grant replaced by "Connect again" more than ten times can lapse an older agent's, which then shows "Sign in again". `connector.sign_in` answers `{ attempt, authorize_url, issuer, provider?, user_code?, install_url? }`, the last three only when an app signs in, `authorize_url` then being its `verification_uri`; `team.get`'s connector rows say `provider?` and `settings_url?` for a kept grant whose app the daemon's table has. On `ConnectorAdd`, where an app signs in, the page says "<Provider> lets you sign in." with "Sign in with <Provider>", no "for <host>" line, and "Catervas shows you a short code to type on <Provider>'s page."; the button shows the code in a card, "Enter this code on <Provider>:", the code large in the code face, "Only enter a code that this page shows you. Catervas never sends you a code in a chat.", "Copy the code", "Open <page>" (the page's host and path, `github.com/login/device`), which opens it in a new tab in the click itself, and "Waiting for you on <Provider>…", checking every two seconds for up to ten minutes; once the user has said yes, "Signed in to <Provider>." and, where the app has an `install_url`, "To let <Name> read private repositories, install Catervas on them on <Provider>." with the link "Install Catervas on <Provider>" in a new tab. An agent's row says "Signed in to <Provider>" in place of the address's host, a kit service's "Signed in to <Provider>." in place of its title, and Remove, where the service cannot be asked to forget the sign-in, says "To remove Catervas completely, also remove it in <Provider>'s settings." with the name a link to `settings_url` in a new tab (naming the connector for one with neither a provider nor a web address). On the command line, `catervas connect` writes `Open <verification_uri> and enter the code <user_code>.` and the same warning sentence to the error stream, opens the page, waits ten minutes, and writes `Signed in to <Provider>.`.

Signing in with Google, for Catervas's own connector (added in 0.59; ADR 0035's amendments of 2026-10-05 and 2026-10-06, ADR 0042; phase 7 step 08e). Catervas's Google app, a Desktop client in a Google Cloud project the founder owns and Catervas Cloud holds from phase 11 (changed in 0.61, ADR 0044; ADR 0048), signs an agent in for Catervas's own `google-ads` connector with the one scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords`; the connector itself is the next paragraph's (added in 0.68), and `google-ads` is among Catervas's own connectors, so an entry that names it matches the table's entry for it. `app_for_catervas_connector(table, command, args)` answers an entry only when `command` and `args` are exactly `catervas connector <name>` for one of Catervas's own connectors and `<name>` is the entry's `catervas_connector`; a `stdio` entry with `oauth` that no entry answers is `sign_in_not_supported`, as Google's is in every build, since no build has a Google entry (changed in 0.64). The entry's flow, `AppFlow::Loopback { authorization_endpoint }`, is Catervas's own requests and not `rmcp`'s, since there is no MCP server whose metadata to discover: the listener of the sign-in above (`http://localhost:<free port>/callback`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]`, five tries, the first `GET /callback` with the attempt's `state`, a plain page that names the provider, ten minutes), a random `state`, a verifier of 64 characters and its S256 challenge, and an authorization address that carries exactly `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `response_type=code`, `scope` (the entry's scopes joined by a space), `state`, `code_challenge` and `code_challenge_method=S256`, with no `resource`, since there is no MCP resource, and no `access_type`. The team file's `oauth.scopes`, when given, must each be among the entry's, else `sign_in_failed` ("Catervas's <name> sign-in asks only for <the entry's scopes, joined by a comma and a space>") before any request; none means the entry's. The callback must carry an `iss` equal to the entry's issuer, else `sign_in_mismatch`; `iss` is required here, and step 08g's live check settles whether Google sends it; `error=access_denied` is `access_denied`. The exchange posts `code`, `client_id`, `client_secret`, `redirect_uri`, `grant_type=authorization_code` and `code_verifier`, asking for JSON, and is refused `sign_in_failed` when `token_type` is not `Bearer` (ASCII case ignored: "<name> did not give Catervas a bearer token"), when there is no `refresh_token` ("<name> did not give Catervas a lasting sign-in") and when the granted `scope` lacks one that was asked for ("you did not allow Catervas all it asks of <name>; sign in again and tick every box"). The grant is step 03's with `app` the entry's `id`, the entry's issuer and token endpoint, the issuer as `resource` (bookkeeping, which nothing reads for an app's grant), no revocation endpoint and the granted scopes. A refresh of a grant of an app that has a `client_secret` sends it, looked up by `app` in the daemon's table (the command line's is `REGISTERED_APPS`) on each refresh and never kept in the grant, and sends no `resource`; a grant whose `app` the table lacks, as in every build before Catervas Cloud (phase 11), has lapsed at once, with no request. Google's Testing status ends a refresh token after 7 days, which `invalid_grant` makes "Sign in again", and its consent screen warns that the app is unverified until Google has verified the scope, which waits for Catervas's website (phase 11; ADR 0042's amendment, ADR 0048). Remove deletes the local grant and cannot revoke it, since Google's revocation ends every agent's grant of the project at once; it says where to remove Catervas, `https://myaccount.google.com/connections`. The daemon and `catervas connect` sign a Catervas connector in as any server that signs in: `connector.sign_in` answers `provider` and no `user_code`; an attempt is bound to the agent, the server's name and the server's whole transport, so one made for the pair serves neither an `http` server of the same name nor the pair with other settings (`sign_in_unknown`); and `connector.sign_in_status`'s words name the provider where an app signs in. The launch route answers a signed-in Catervas connector with its command and an empty environment, never a token, after refreshing a grant that expires within a minute, and 403 `sign_in_again` for a lapsed one; a session's setup refreshes it as it does an `http` one's and leaves a lapsed one out; its tools are listed with no token, since a `stdio` server takes no bearer; and `team.get` says `auth: oauth`, `provider` and `revokes: false`. On the command line, `catervas connect <agent> <name>` writes `Sign in to <provider> in your browser: <address>` and then `Signed in to <provider>.` to the error stream.

Google Ads, Catervas's own connector (added in 0.68; ADR 0038, ADR 0042, ADR 0044; phase 7 step 08f). `google-ads` is one of `CATERVAS_CONNECTORS` (`osv`, `google-ads`, and since 0.75 `fx`), and the Marketing Specialist's kit lists it after Kit as `catervas connector google-ads` with `oauth` for the one scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords`: `list_accounts`, `report` and `keyword_ideas` are `network` ("list ad accounts", "read ad results", "find search words"), and its seven writes, `create_search_campaign`, `add_ad_group`, `add_keywords`, `add_negative_keywords`, `add_responsive_search_ad`, `set_campaign_budget` and `set_campaign_status`, are `paid` (changed in 0.115; it was `external_effect`) and `plan_approved` (5.6), none with an allowance. The server is a shim: `catervas connector google-ads` lists the ten tools itself, so its list is pinned offline, and forwards each call to the daemon, which holds the grant, checks the plan against the log, calls Google and records what it created. It reads `CATERVAS_CONNECTOR_URL` and `CATERVAS_CONNECTOR_TICKET` from its environment, which the launcher (`catervas connector run`) sets beside `KEPT_ENV` and the entry's keys, and nothing else: the ticket from the launch route's answer and the address `http://127.0.0.1:<the port daemon.json names>/connector/call`. With neither set it still lists its tools and a call is the tool error "Google Ads runs only inside a Catervas session". At each call it refuses an address that is not exactly that form, follows no redirect, uses no proxy, waits at most 120 seconds, reads at most 4 MiB, sends `{ tool, arguments }` with `Authorization: Bearer <ticket>`, and answers the daemon's `{ ok }` as the tool's text and its `{ error }` as a tool error. The launch route answers a Catervas connector that signs in `{ command, args, env: {}, cwd, ticket }`: the ticket is 32 random bytes in hex, its sha256 kept on the session by server until the session ends (`end_session`), never a token. `POST /connector/call` sits outside the daemon-token layer, behind `require_project`; it compares the ticket's sha256 with every live session's in constant time (401 otherwise), refuses a stopped session (`session_stopped`), and runs the call as that session's agent. The route's checks, in order: the session's connector `google-ads` and a ticket made for it (`connector_not_in_session`); the agent's entry being the kit's, `matches_kit` (`google_ads_not_kit`, so a custom entry naming the same command reaches nothing, whatever its tags); the tool tagged by the session, not `denied`, and for a write `paid` and plan-marked (`tool_not_tagged`, `tool_denied`, `tool_not_plan_marked`); for a write, an active plan (`no_active_marketing_plan`); the agent's grant, refreshed when it will not last 120 seconds, waiting at most 10 (`sign_in_again`, `connector_not_confirmed`, `sign_in_failed`); the input (`google_ads_input`); for a write, what the plan covers (`not_in_marketing_plan: <why>`); then Google (`google_ads_refused`, `google_ads_failed`). A write holds one daemon-wide lock from reading the plan and the campaigns made through Google's answer and the record of `marketing_campaign.created`; reads take none. Just before it sends anything to Google it reads the plan again, and sends nothing (`no_active_marketing_plan`) when the active plan is no longer the one the write was checked against; and whatever ends or replaces a plan (the owner's end, an approval that replaces one, the dates' rule, and the pause on a plan's end, 6.5) takes the same lock first, so a write in flight finishes before the end is recorded (amended in 0.68, from step 08f's landing review); so does a removal of an agent's Google Ads sign-in (6.5), from its pause through its write of the team, so that no enable runs between them (added in 0.72 after review). The writes' lock is always taken before the team's, never after it. Calls to Google never go through `call_as` (ADR 0042's amendment): the daemon is the server. Google's API is v25 over REST at the fixed `https://googleads.googleapis.com/v25` (a Catervas release moves it), never an argument or an input, with the grant as the bearer and no developer token (Google ended them on 2026-09-09) and no `login-customer-id`, so only accounts the sign-in reaches directly; it follows no redirect, uses no proxy, waits 25 seconds, reads at most 4 MiB in chunks, and says Google's refusal in Catervas's words with Google's `message` cut at 300 characters and quoted, a `PERMISSION_DENIED` on keyword ideas being "Google has not yet allowed Catervas's app to give keyword ideas." (Explorer access blocks that service; the access level is Catervas Cloud's project's, ADR 0044). GAQL is built only from fixed text and checked values (an account is `123-456-7890`, a resource name `customers/<ten digits>/(campaigns|adGroups)/<id>`, a day `YYYY-MM-DD`), never a free query, and a search sends `{ query }` alone. The reads: `list_accounts` (at most 20 accounts, each `{ account, name, currency, time_zone, manager }`), `report { account, kind, from, to }` (`campaigns`, `ad_groups`, `keywords`, `search_terms` or `ads`, the days at most 366 apart, at most 500 rows, `more` when cut, the cost a decimal of the account's currency) and `keyword_ideas { account, words, language, locations }` (1 to 10 words, Google's numeric constant ids, at most 100 ideas of `{ text, avg_monthly_searches, competition, low_bid, high_bid }`). The writes: `create_search_campaign { account, plan_campaign, name, bidding, max_cpc?, locations, languages }` makes, in one atomic `googleAds:mutate`, a budget and a campaign named `<plan id> <key>: <name>`, a `SEARCH` campaign created `PAUSED` on Google Search alone with its dates (`start_date_time` the later of the plan campaign's first day and the UTC date two days after today at `00:00:00`, so no time zone, east of UTC included, makes it the past, `end_date_time` its last day at `23:59:59`, in the account's time zone), `DOES_NOT_CONTAIN_EU_POLITICAL_ADVERTISING`, `maximize_clicks` (Google's `target_spend`, `max_cpc` its ceiling) or `maximize_conversions` (no `max_cpc`), and a criterion for each of 1 to 20 locations and 1 to 10 languages; `add_ad_group`, `add_keywords` and `add_negative_keywords` (1 to 50 words of 1 to 80 characters, `exact`, `phrase` or `broad`) and `add_responsive_search_ad` (3 to 15 headlines of at most 30 characters, 2 to 4 descriptions of at most 90, an `https` address with a host and no user information, paths of at most 15) create what they name `ENABLED`, only the campaign being created paused; `set_campaign_budget` and `set_campaign_status` (`paused` or `enabled`) change one campaign. The budget Google keeps (`campaign_budget`, `catervas-core`): over the campaign's run, from its first day to its last, both included, a run of 3 to 90 days takes a total budget (`CUSTOM_PERIOD`, `total_amount_micros`), the plan campaign's budget, which Google never bills past (a key has one campaign across a plan's whole lineage, so nothing of its budget was spent before the campaign was made), and any other run a daily budget of what is left divided by the days, rounded down to the hundredth, which bounds Google's own charging while Catervas is not running; every budget is `STANDARD` and not shared; a currency with no minor unit (`ZERO_DECIMAL`) takes whole units, rounded down; a create, a change of budget and enabling a campaign each read the ad account's currency first and are refused when it is not the plan's (a plan in another currency cannot replace one, `marketing_plan_currency` in 6.5's proposal, and the check holds beside it). What the active plan covers (`check_ads_write`, pure, refusing in a sentence after `not_in_marketing_plan: `), with the plan's lineage being the active plan and every plan it replaces through the whole chain: every write is in the plan's `google_ads_account`; a create is for a key the active plan has, with no campaign recorded for that key under any plan of the lineage, and its last day is not before its first possible day; a write under a campaign (an ad group's campaign is read from Google), a new budget or enabling needs the campaign recorded for a key the active plan has under a plan of the lineage; a total budget's new amount is from what the campaign spent to the plan campaign's budget and a daily one at most what is left divided by the days left; enabling needs today within the plan campaign's dates, its spend below its budget, the plan's Google Ads spend below the plan's, and what Google holds for the campaign no more than the active plan gives its key, since a plan that replaces another and lowers a key's budget or shortens its dates leaves Google's total budget and end as the first plan made them: a total budget at most the plan campaign's budget, a daily one at most what is left of it over the days Google still runs the campaign (from its own first day, or today, to its own last), and an end no later than the plan campaign's, which Catervas cannot change; a figure Google did not give refuses it (amended in 0.68, from step 08f's landing review); pausing covers any campaign recorded under a plan of the lineage, the active plan having dropped its key or not, and with no active plan the hook refuses it first (`no_active_marketing_plan`). Spend is read from Google for the call, one `Search` for each ad account the lineage's campaigns are in (changed in 0.72, so that enabling and the cap count one spend) of those campaigns' `cost_micros`, with each campaign's budget amounts and its start and end, from the day before the first was made to tomorrow, rounded up from micros to hundredths; a spend read that fails refuses a budget change and enabling, and pausing needs none. The hard stop's reads and pauses (6.5, added in 0.72) are not a session's calls: the watch and the removals of a sign-in (`connector.disconnect`, a save, a start, a template and a retirement, 6.5) take a Marketing Specialist's grant in the daemon (the entry that `matches_kit`, its stored sign-in, no ticket) and send only a fixed status query and a `PAUSED` mutation for each campaign, under the same lock. Nothing here deletes, or touches billing, who may use the account, conversion tracking, another campaign type or a campaign Catervas did not make for the plan. The kit row before the launch: until Catervas Cloud signs customers in to Google (phase 11, ADR 0044, ADR 0048), `team.get`'s kit row carries `at_launch: true` for an entry whose `oauth` is on Catervas's own connector when the daemon's table has no app for it, and the agent's page shows the service's About and "{service} comes with Catervas’s web launch." in place of Connect. The founder's live check is phase 11's.

Catervas Cloud (added in 0.61; ADR 0044; it replaces 0.60's paragraph on the user's own sign-in apps, which were dropped with phase 7 step 03f before they were built). Catervas is open source, so no build carries a credential of Catervas's, before or after the launch (8.6). Until Catervas Cloud runs (phase 11), nothing that needs an app of Catervas's is offered: no build has an entry in the table above, GitHub's server (`https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/`) is connected with a pasted fine-grained token, sent as `Authorization: Bearer`, and Catervas's own `google-ads` connector cannot be signed in to (`sign_in_not_supported`). The code read `CATERVAS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` at build time until phase 7 step 08e's Task 8 removed it (changed in 0.64): `REGISTERED_APPS` is empty in every build, a test fails for any source that reads a variable at build time with `env!` or `option_env!`, bar the names Cargo itself sets for a build (`CARGO_PKG_*`, `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`, `CARGO_BIN_EXE_*`, `CARGO_CRATE_NAME` and `CARGO_BIN_NAME`), and the loopback sign-in with PKCE, the refresh and the table's matching stay, for the sign-in through Catervas Cloud to build on. From phase 11, before the web launch (ADR 0048), Catervas Cloud, a service Catervas runs, signs users in; the service and its hosting are planned separately in `catervas-ops`, Catervas's private operations repository (changed in 0.73, ADR 0047). Its free tier holds Catervas's GitHub App and Catervas's Google app and their secrets, server side. The local Catervas starts each sign-in through it and refreshes each grant through it, with the user's Catervas account; Catervas Cloud answers the authorization address, adds the secret on the exchange and each refresh, and hands the tokens straight back, storing none, and they are kept with the agent's keys, as every grant is. A Catervas account is signed in to once per computer, in the browser; its session is the user's own credential, kept in the OS keychain, and Catervas Cloud's fair-use limits are per account. Phase 11 plans how the account signs in, GitHub's flow, which the founder wants to be a single click, and the screens.

GitHub with a pasted key (added in 0.65; ADR 0044; phase 7 step 07c). Until Catervas Cloud signs users in (above), the Product Manager's and the Architect's kits each carry GitHub's official server, `https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/`, as an `http` connector named `github` with `credential_keys: [GITHUB_KEY]`, `Authorization: Bearer {GITHUB_KEY}`, a `key_page` and no `oauth`, so `team.get`'s row says `auth: keys` and the connect page shows its key field. The kit format takes a sign-in or keys, never both (`oauth_with_keys`, `oauth_header_conflict`), and a sign-in would be `sign_in_not_supported`, since GitHub registers no client by itself. The key is a fine-grained personal access token: with one, GitHub's server lists every tool and its API enforces the key's permissions (GitHub's changelog of 2026-01-28), so the listing is the same for every user's key and a pin can hold; a classic key reaches every repository the user can and the server hides tools by its scopes, which differ by user, so the kits do not take one. The entries narrow the server with headers, which the listing and every session send as they send the key: the Product Manager's `X-MCP-Toolsets: issues,projects`; the Architect's `X-MCP-Toolsets: repos,pull_requests` and `X-MCP-Readonly: true`, which keeps only the read tools. Neither entry names `X-MCP-Tools`, since GitHub makes the server fail to start on a tool name it does not know, so one tool GitHub removed would stop every user's GitHub until a Catervas release, whereas a toolset that loses a tool only drops it, which the live pin test reports; nor `X-MCP-Exclude-Tools`, since a `denied` tool is never offered already, the pin comparison runs both ways and GitHub's page is silent on an unknown name there; nor `X-MCP-Lockdown`, which hides the public issue details of users without push access, the reports a Product Manager imports, and which GitHub calls a best-effort content filter, not a security boundary. Three fences hold what an agent may do: GitHub refuses what the key may not do; the headers keep other toolsets off the listing; and the tags decide what is offered, so a `denied` tool and a tool the kit does not name (`tool_not_tagged`) are never offered, and nothing that deletes, administers, touches secrets or workflows, merges, pushes or changes a file is. A tool GitHub lists that the kit does not name is never offered until a pin update tags it, and the update's rule is `denied`, with no label. The Product Manager's tags: eight reads are `network` (`issue_read`, `list_issues`, `search_issues`, `list_issue_types`, `list_issue_fields`, `get_label`, `projects_list` and `projects_get`); `issue_write` and `add_issue_comment` are `external_effect` with no allowance, so since 0.115 (ADR 0061) each call runs without asking and is recorded, although an issue or a comment is published to everyone who can see the repository (it waited for the human, who saw its whole input, until then); `sub_issue_write`, `update_issue_comment` and `projects_write` are `denied`. A kit tags a tool, not an argument, and both writes reach pull requests too, a pull request being an issue to GitHub's API (`issue_write`'s `update` method edits, closes and reassigns), so the skill `using-product-sources` forbids giving either a pull request's number, and whether a key with Issues write alone can close one is recorded by the live check, not fixed. The Architect's tags: fifteen reads are `network` (`search_code`, `get_file_contents`, `list_branches`, `list_commits`, `get_commit`, `search_commits`, `list_tags`, `get_tag`, `list_releases`, `get_latest_release`, `get_release_by_tag`, `search_repositories`, `list_pull_requests`, `pull_request_read` and `search_pull_requests`) and `list_repository_collaborators`, a list of who may change a repository, is `denied`; GitHub refuses `pull_request_read`'s `get_status` and `get_check_runs` to its key, which `using-architecture-sources` says. The two entries share the address, the key's name and `about`, and differ in headers, `key_page`, tools, labels, `why` and `setup`, so they hash differently, and a team file that gives an Architect the Product Manager's wider entry fails `matches_kit`. "Get your key" opens `key_page`, GitHub's template address for a fine-grained key (`name`, `description`, `expires_in`, and `<permission>=<level>`, which GitHub's form validates), with a life of 366 days, GitHub's longest dated one: the Product Manager's asks for repository Issues read and write, the Architect's for Contents and Pull requests read. Neither sets the resource owner, which is the user's to choose, nor organisation Projects, which GitHub's form accepts only when the owner is an organisation, and most users' owner is their account, so the Product Manager's setup says to add it for an organisation's boards. A fine-grained key has one owner, the user's account or one organisation, so a user whose code sits under both connects GitHub for one of them per agent until the sign-in; an organisation that requires approval leaves the key `pending`, reading public resources only, until an administrator approves it; it does not reach Projects owned by a user account, so the Product Manager reads an organisation's boards only; an organisation may cap a key's life below a year, or need the user signed in to its single sign-on when the key is made, which both setups say; and every key reads all public repositories. GitHub's documentation (read 2026-10-06) says its server is available to every GitHub user whatever the plan and lists Copilot as a prerequisite only for Copilot's own editors, which Catervas is not, so the setups say nothing about Copilot; a key GitHub refuses shows the connect page's words for a refused key, and the founder's live check (step 07c, Task 6) settles whether an account that never turned Copilot on connects. Remove deletes the key from the keychain, as for every keyed service, and the key works at GitHub until it ends or the user deletes it there. The live pin test reads `CATERVAS_KIT_GITHUB_GITHUB_KEY` once for both kits, since they share a connector name. From phase 11 (ADR 0048) each entry signs in through Catervas Cloud instead: it loses `headers.Authorization`, `credential_keys` and `key_page`, gains `oauth: {}` (the table's GitHub entry, matched by host) and keeps its `X-MCP-*` headers; its hash changes, so every agent connected with a key sees "Connect again"; and Catervas's GitHub App then asks for repository Contents and Pull requests read, Issues read and write, and organisation Projects read (ADR 0044's amendment of 2026-10-06), or the Product Manager's two writes stop at the switch.

A user's own skills (added in 0.40; ADR 0034). Before any kit, the user can give one agent, or the whole team, a skill in the Agent Skills format: a folder with a `SKILL.md` and the files it refers to. The team's lives in `.catervas/skills/<name>/` and one agent's in `.catervas/agents/<agent_id>/skills/<name>/`, both read from the project's root, never a task's worktree, as `team.yaml` is; agents cannot write `.catervas/` (5.3). A name resolves agent, then team, then role. An agent's pin replaces the team's skill of that name whatever its state, so a skill waiting for review never falls back silently to the team's. A team or agent skill whose name is one of the shipped skills replaces it only when the person said so: `skill_save` and `skill_confirm` with such a name are refused `skill_name_taken` unless they carry `replace_shipped: true`. While such a replacement is `in_use`, the sessions that load skills (8.2) leave the shipped skill out of the prompt and load the replacement on demand; the sessions given one Catervas tool alone have no `Skill` tool, so they keep the shipped skill in their prompt.

A skill is instructions an agent follows, so the person reads all of it before it is used: adding or editing one shows the whole `SKILL.md` and every file first, and the add is the confirmation. `team.yaml` pins each skill, `skills: [{ name, sha256 }]` at the top level for the team and on each agent for that agent, at most 20 in a list and a name once in it (`skill_name_twice`). `sha256` is `skill_sha256`: the sha256, in lower-case hex, of the canonical JSON (compact, keys sorted at every depth) of `{ <relative path>: <sha256 of the file's bytes> }` over every file in the folder. As a connector is (ADR 0030), a skill is confirmed on this computer, because `.catervas/` travels with the repository and a clone, a pull or a hand edit could change a skill's instructions and its pin together. The states, checked in this order as `skills.list` computes them for one agent: `replaced`, a team row when the agent pins a skill of that name and a role row when a team or agent skill of that name is `in_use`; `missing`, a pinned folder that is not there; `review`, the folder exists but its hash differs from the pin, or the newest `skill.added`, `skill.changed` or `skill.confirmed` for it in this machine's log (8.4, never committed) does not carry the pin's hash, or a `skill.removed` follows it, or there is none, or reading the folder or the checks below refuse it; and `in_use` otherwise, the only state a skill loads in. `skill_confirm`, with the hash the person saw, reads the folder, refuses `skill_hash_mismatch` unless its hash is that one, refuses whatever the checks refuse with that refusal's code, writes the hash as the pin when it differs, then records `skill.confirmed`, so a skill whose folder or pin changed outside Catervas is used again only after the person has read the folder as it is now. Shipped skills are Catervas's own, neither pinned nor confirmed. In the browser's key mapper the paths of a command's or answer's `files` are names, not wire keys, and cross unchanged (added in 0.42).

The checks, which hold in `skill_save`, `skill_confirm` and when a session assembles its skills. `SKILL.md` opens with a `---` line and closes its frontmatter with another (CRLF is read as LF); the frontmatter is a YAML mapping read under ADR 0007's options. `name` and `description` are strings: a missing `SKILL.md`, no frontmatter, a frontmatter that is not a mapping or a missing `name` is `skill_frontmatter_invalid`; `name` is lower-case letters and digits joined by single hyphens, at most 64 characters, and its folder's (`skill_name_invalid`, `skill_name_mismatch`); `description` has 1 to 1,024 characters, counted in Unicode scalar values (`skill_description_invalid`). Limits: `SKILL.md` at most 32 KiB; at most 16 files, `SKILL.md` among them, each at most 64 KiB, UTF-8 text with no NUL; 256 KiB in all; a path of at most 3 parts, the file's name included, each part matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,99}$`, so none starts with a dot, and no link anywhere (`skill_too_large`, `skill_too_many_files`, `skill_file_not_text`, `skill_path_invalid`). A skill may not run commands or attach files, because Claude Code does both when a skill loads, and an attachment is read by its own code, which no hook sees: a `SKILL.md` holding `` !` `` or ```` ```! ```` anywhere, or a line whose first characters after spaces are three or more backticks or tildes followed by `!`, is refused `skill_runs_commands`; one with an `@` is refused `skill_attaches_files` unless the character before it is an ASCII letter or digit or one of `._%+-`, as in an email address (Claude Code attaches `@<path>` after any whitespace, a byte order mark included, and after 。、？！). A skill names a bundled file as a path or a Markdown link, which the agent reads with `Read`, which the hook judges. Every other frontmatter field (`allowed-tools`, `hooks`, `model`, `context` and the rest) is accepted, dropped from the session's copy, and listed to the person ("Catervas ignores: allowed-tools, hooks").

The commands (sent through `here_or_sent` from the command line and as `command` through the RPC from the browser) are `skill_save { level, agent?, files, replace_shipped? }`, which adds a skill, or replaces the one of its name, `files` mapping each relative path to its text; `skill_remove { level, agent?, name }`; and `skill_confirm { level, agent?, name, sha256, replace_shipped? }`; `level` is `team`, or `agent` with the agent's id. A save writes the new folder beside its place as `.<name>.new-<random>`, moves any old folder to `.<name>.old-<random>`, renames the new one into place (`rename(2)` will not replace a folder that is not empty), deletes the old one, then writes the pin in the team file, then records `skill.added`, or `skill.changed` for a name already pinned; the pin is written before the event for a confirmation as well. A removal deletes the folder, unpins it and records `skill.removed`, and for a `missing` skill it unpins and records and does not fail. The refusals are `skill_unknown`, a name not pinned there, `skill_hash_mismatch`, `skill_name_taken`, `skill_limit_reached`, the twenty-first of a list, `agent_unknown`, and each check's code; a refusal writes nothing. A whole-team write keeps the pins: `team.save` and `agent.replace` keep the top-level `skills` and each kept agent's `skills` as the team file holds them, whatever the browser sends (an agent a save adds has none), and `template.apply` keeps the top-level `skills` and the skills of each agent it keeps, an agent it removes losing its pins as removing an agent does; only the three commands change a pin. Removing an agent leaves its skill folders, which are the user's files, unpinned and unused. A saved team template carries no skills. `catervas skill list [--agent <id>]`, `catervas skill show <name> (--team | --agent <id>)`, `catervas skill add <folder> (--team | --agent <id>) [--yes] [--replace]`, `catervas skill remove` and `catervas skill confirm <name> (--team | --agent <id>) <hash> [--replace]` are F9's.

What stays: a confirmed skill can steer its agent within the agent's own tiers and connectors in every later session, and its description is listed in each; the reading before adding is the defence against the instructions themselves (8.6). A skill that runs scripts is not supported.

The kit file (added in 0.44; ADR 0036). `roles/<role>/kit.yaml` holds `role` (the folder's), `skills` (names, at most 20) and `connectors` (at most 20), validated by `docs/schemas/kit.schema.json` and then by the loader in `catervas-roles`, which embeds the file with its skills and refuses, naming the field as a JSON pointer and a code, a `role` that is not the folder's (`kit_role_mismatch`); a skill with no `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (`kit_skill_missing`), one `role.yaml` names too (`kit_skill_in_role`; it stays in the prompt there), or one the checks of a user's skill refuse, with that refusal's code (6.7, ADR 0034); a connector name twice (`kit_connector_twice`). A connector is `stdio`, `http` or `container`. A `stdio` or `http` one takes the team file's fields (`command`, `args`, `url`, `headers`, `credential_keys`, `oauth`), each refusal `validate_team` gives the same entry (so a kit cannot ship a key in a header or an argument), and the setup copy: `title`, `about`, `why`, `setup`, `key_page` (an `https` address, required when it takes keys: `key_page_missing`) and `labels`, a tool to what it does in the user's words (`label_not_a_tool` for one that is not a tool); a field a transport does not take or lacks is `kit_field_not_allowed` or `kit_field_missing`. Every connector has `tools`, each `network`, `external_effect`, `paid` or `denied`, never `read`, and a tool with no value is a schema error. A `stdio` connector starts only `npx`, `bunx`, `uvx` or `pipx run` (also by path or as `.cmd`/`.exe`), with its first non-flag argument the package at an exact version, `name@1.2.3` or `name==1.2.3`, and none of `-p`, `--package`, `--from`, `--spec`, `--with`, `--registry` or `--index-url`; or an absolute path to a binary Catervas ships (`catervas`, `catervas-…`). Any other command, every shell and every other runner (`sh`, `pnpm`, `npm`, `yarn`, `bun`, `uv`, `deno`, `docker`, `node`, `python`) is `package_not_pinned` (at `command` or `args`), so the code Catervas runs changes only with a Catervas release and its pin review. A `container` connector, a server Catervas runs in Docker itself with an `image`, `module_root` and `args` and no copy, is only the UI/UX Designer's built-in browser (`container_not_builtin`) with its image pinned by `@sha256:` (`image_not_pinned`). `allowances` map a tool tagged `paid` to `{ calls, what }` (`allowance_not_paid`; changed in 0.115); phase 7 step 05b reads them. Catervas's own words never say "MCP", "OAuth" or "token", so no field of the copy holds one in any case (`copy_word_refused`), with one exception the founder made on 2026-10-02: `setup` may quote a service's own label so the user finds it on the service's page ("On Slack's page, copy the value labelled ‘Bot User OAuth Token’."). A quoted label is the text after `‘` up to `’`, after `“` up to `”`, or after `"` up to `"`, on one line, at most 60 characters; the ASCII apostrophe never opens one, an opening mark with no closing one quotes nothing, and a longer span is checked as the rest is. Every role ships a `kit.yaml`; none has a service before step 06, and only the Designer's has the browser.

Kit skills and kit connectors (added in 0.44; ADR 0036). A kit's skills live in the role's `skills/` folder, are Catervas's own (neither pinned nor confirmed) and load on demand after the agent's and the team's: one name resolves agent, team, kit, a pin of the name at either level standing for the kit's skill whatever its state. They count among the shipped names (a team or agent skill of that name needs `replace_shipped`), `skills.list` lists one as a `role` row after the role's rows, `replaced` while the agent's or the team's skill of that name is in use, and `skill.get`'s role level answers its `SKILL.md` as the session's copy holds it. A kit's `stdio` or `http` connector is connected by name: `catervas connect <agent> <name>` with neither `--command` nor `--url`, or the browser's `{ name, source: "kit" }`. The entry is written whole into the team file, `{ name, source: kit, transport, ... }`, with every field from the kit and the kit's tags as its `tools`, held to every rule of a custom entry and hashed with `"source": "kit"` added so that every kept hash stands and a relabelled entry needs "Connect again". `connector_connect` refuses a `source: kit` entry that is not exactly the one its agent's role's kit gives (`connector_not_in_kit`), which also refuses a service of another role's kit. Connecting lists the service's tools to prove the key or the sign-in works, and writes the kit's tags: a tool the service lists and the kit does not tag is `tool_not_tagged`, and a pinned tool the service dropped costs nothing. A request for a kit service carries `tags: {}` (`kit_names_these` otherwise), and the command line refuses `--arg`, `--header`, `--key`, `--tag`, `--client-id`, `--callback-port`, `--scope` and `--sign-in` with it, reads a value for each of the kit's keys from standard input after "Make a key at <key_page>, then paste <KEY>:" on the error stream, and signs in when the kit's service does. A kit entry that is not what its role's kit says now (a release tagged a tool `denied`, or changed a field) is left out of the session's `mcp.json` and registration and shown `connect_again`; one whose service the kit no longer has is shown `not_in_kit`, with "Remove" alone. A team file or a clone that forges a `source: kit` entry with wider tags hashes differently from anything kept and is refused at connect and left out at session setup; the launch route and the hook take only what a session's registration holds and re-check the kept hash. Every shipped `stdio` and `http` kit connector is pinned: `crates/runtime/tests/live_kit_pins.rs`, run with `CATERVAS_LIVE_TESTS=1` and each key from `CATERVAS_KIT_<NAME>_<KEY>` (a bearer from `CATERVAS_KIT_<NAME>_BEARER` for one that signs in), fails naming the connector and the unset variable, and on any drift with "a pin update re-reviews every tag"; `pin_drift` names the tools a service added and dropped.

**Service logos and info buttons (added in 0.79; standalone plan `agent-page-logos`).** On the agent page every connected service shows its logo beside its name: a mark bundled with the web app under `apps/web/src/assets/services/`, named for the kit connector (`notion.svg`, `google-ads.svg`), never fetched from the service, so no company learns the user's address and the page works offline. Playwright has its own mark; a connector with no mark, a user-added one included, shows a plug. The logo is decorative: the service's name stands beside it. A kit service's row reads logo, name, its `about` and an info button (ⓘ). `about` is the row's visible line, at most six words; `why` sits behind the button, at most twenty, and a test holds both (a kit from elsewhere is not held to it). Every other note on the agent page (what each permission means, what the effort levels cost, the custom connector's warnings, pause, replace and retire, skills and each skill's description (changed in 0.80), and the Procurement Specialist's orders, sites and mailbox) sits behind an info button too, which opens on hover, focus or tap and closes on Escape; on Settings (changed in 0.84) the detail of the preview's four fields (on setup's card too) and the notes under Your team's rules, Saved teams and Catervas on this computer sit behind an info button as well, and those explanations, like the preview's lead above its fields, are bullet points, never a paragraph; headings, labels, statuses that ask for action, counts and buttons stay visible. Rewording this copy asks nobody to connect again, because it sits outside the entry the connector is hashed by.

**Suggested connections on Today (added in 0.105; standalone plan `suggested-connections`).** Today lists, after What moved (changed in 0.123), the services of a role's kit that an active agent could use and does not have. For each active agent, in the team file's order of agents, each service of its role's kit, in the kit's order, that the agent has no `mcp_servers` entry for is suggested. A service the agent already holds in any state (connected, `connect_again`, `sign_in_again`, `not_in_kit`) is left out, and so is a service the build cannot connect yet (one offered at launch), the Designer's built-in browser, any service of a paused or retired agent, and any pair the user said Not now to. Each row shows the service's logo and title, then the agent's name and the kit's `about` ("Mira · Schedules social posts"), the kit's `why` behind the info button, **Connect** and **Not now**. Two rows show at first (changed in 0.123) and a button reads "Show all N"; with nothing suggested there is no section. **Connect** opens `/team/<agent>?connect=<service>`; on arrival the agent page opens that service's connect dialog once when the role's kit offers the service, the agent does not hold it and it is not waiting for the launch, and otherwise ignores the parameter. **Not now** sends `connector_suggestion.hide { agent, server }`, which answers `{}`, records no event, and keeps the pair on this computer in `.catervas/local/connector-suggestions.json` as `{ hidden: [{ agent_id, server }] }`, a file that is not shared with the team or the repository, written once per pair. `team.get` answers the pairs as `hidden_suggestions: [{ agent, server }]`, read from the file each time, an unreadable or absent file counting as empty. The command is refused `suggestion_not_offered` for an agent not in the team or a service its role's kit does not list, and then writes nothing. The row goes at once and returns with a plain message when the command fails. A service connected and later disconnected is suggested again until the user says Not now.

**An agent asks for a connection (added in 0.117; ADR 0063).** `catervas_request_connection { server, why }`, tier `read`, is offered to every session that is given every tool (not to chat, explore or ceremony sessions). `server` is a service of the agent's role's kit and `why` is 20 to 300 characters once trimmed. It is refused, in this order and with nothing recorded, `connection_why`, `connection_not_in_kit` (the service is not one the kit offers) and `connection_held` (the agent already has an `mcp_servers` entry of that name, whatever its source). It records `connection.requested { server, why }` and answers `{ requested, next }`, where `next` tells the agent to carry on without it and not wait. `catervas_ask_human` was rejected for this, since a question holds the task until answered. `team.get` answers `requested_connections`, one `{ agent, server, why }` for each (agent, server) pair with the newest `why`, ordered by each pair's newest event. Today lists a requested pair first, in that order, with "<Agent> asks: <why>" in place of the kit's line and the same **Connect** and **Not now**; a pair the owner said Not now to stays hidden, and a held pair is never shown.

### 6.8 UI/UX Designer (added in 0.31)

Mandate: a developer focused on the interface (ADR 0026; `docs/design/designer-chats-templates.md`). It explores the app, plans a change to it, and implements the change once the plan is approved, which Catervas records at once (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: the Product Manager decided it before). With the Software Developer it is the only role that changes code, beside the DevOps Engineer's incident fixes (6.9; changed in 0.32): its tasks are not held to the team's `document_paths` (5.3), and they work on `feature/CTV-<n>` or `fix/CTV-<n>` by the contract's `change` (5.14). The team builder suggests one (4.1), named Iris, "Makes it clear, calm and easy to use", with the `extra-1` picture and the tag "UX" in its own colour, pale clay; the user may untick it (the founder's choices of 2026-09-30).

Produces: design plans, diffs, commits on task branches, completion notes; its folder `docs/catervas/design/` (added in 0.91, 5.17): the UI inventory and design notes.

Cannot: change code before its plan is approved (Catervas records the approval when the plan is proposed); modify contracts; accept work; push to shared branches without the `git_remote` grant; touch files outside the contract's allowed paths.

Default tools: read, write_workspace, execute, git_local, the Developer's, and the team's two permission answers apply to it as to the Developer (5.6). Default model: the Developer's, Claude Opus 5.5 at `high`. It ships six skills: `ux-review-heuristics`, `wcag-accessibility-checks`, `brand-and-design-tokens`, `plain-language-interface-wording`, `writing-mockups`, and `responsive-and-phone-checks`. Its `brand-and-design-tokens` reads `docs/catervas/marketing/brand/brand-kit` first when it exists and takes the colours and the voice from it, then finds where the project keeps its design tokens (added in 0.55; the kit is the Marketing Specialist's, 6.5).

Its flow. Every task assigned to a Designer runs this way, whatever its risk. The task's latest `design_plan.*` event, read from the log at every tick, decides which session runs next:

1. Explore. With no plan yet, or with the last one returned, Catervas starts the Designer's `explore` session (8.2) in the task's worktree. It holds the read tier's built-ins whatever the agent's tiers, its every call is held to the read tier by the hook and Catervas's tool server, and a call to its browser to `network` (changed in 0.33), it runs no commands, and it has six Catervas tools: `catervas_read_task`, `catervas_read_board`, `catervas_read_rules`, `catervas_read_criteria`, `catervas_read_decisions`, and `catervas_propose_design_plan`, and a seventh, `catervas_check_page`, with the browser (added in 0.33). With its Playwright connector on and the app's preview set (5.6), it reads the project's files and also opens the app in the browser, and its message says so; browsing before the plan is approved is intended, since the plan gate holds only writes, commands, git and, from 0.39, a connector's `external_effect` or `paid` call (changed in 0.33, from no browser; and in 0.115). When the last plan was returned, the message holds the Product Manager's reason as untrusted text (8.6). The session ends with `catervas_propose_design_plan { plan }`, which records `design_plan.proposed`. The plan is plain text of 200 to 8,000 characters. It opens with a summary for the user of 20 to 600 characters and a blank line, as a note does (5.4), and says what the agent saw, what it will change, and what it will leave alone. The tool is refused with `design_plan_refused` outside the Designer's `explore` session of its task, and for a plan outside those bounds.
2. Catervas's approval (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061; until 0.114 the active Product Manager's `verify` session decided each plan with `catervas_decide_design_plan { approve, reason }`, which is gone with its prompt and message). When a plan is proposed, the orchestrator records `design_plan.approved` at once, with no agent and no session on the envelope and the reason "Catervas approved it: no agent approves a design plan, and the finished change is reviewed (ADR 0061)", and starts the `implement` session in the same tick; a plan an older log left proposed is approved on the first tick after the upgrade. No Product Manager or user is asked, and a team with no active Product Manager no longer makes the task wait. `design_plan.returned` stays in the protocol so that older logs read.

3. Implement. With the plan approved, Catervas starts the Designer's `implement` session with the agent's full tiers and the approved plan in its message. From there the task is an ordinary one: a completion note, `verifying`, the review (5.4), and acceptance.

A session that ends without its one answer, an explore session with no plan, is started again, and each restart counts toward the contract's sessions allowance (5.5). Each returned plan counts against the task's iteration limit, and when the returns reach it the governor escalates the task with `iterations` (5.2). The order is the governor's to enforce, not the prompt's. In any session of a Designer's task whose latest plan is not approved, the hook and Catervas's tool server refuse the Designer's `write_workspace`, `execute`, `git_local` and `git_remote` calls with `design_plan_not_approved`, and the hook refuses its `external_effect` and `paid` connector calls the same way, before any is asked about (5.6; added in 0.39; changed in 0.115). They read the plan from the log at each call, so a plan proposed during a session closes the gate at once. A Designer's session that is about no task is held as not approved.

Its reviewer is the Architect, else a Developer (5.1, 5.4); with neither active, its tasks are not ready (5.3; changed in 0.103).

What the web app shows. Setup and the Team page draw each agent's picture in a ring of its role's colour. On the Team page, when the team has a Designer and a Developer, the cost section says that the Designer uses the Developer's model, so the Designer adds to what a day costs, and that planning costs a little too, and it links to Costs. The board says "Planning" for a Designer in its `explore` session, and `team.activity` says "Planning" and the task's title for it too. A plan no longer waits for anyone, so no activity line says so (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061: it read "Waiting for" the active Product Manager "to approve a plan"). Each card on the Team page says its agent's activity line in place of "On the team", and "Paused" for a paused agent. A Designer's task page opens its plan tab with the latest plan, signed with its day and time and read from `task.get`'s `design_plan` (`plan`, `state` `proposed`, `approved` or `returned`, and the `reason` once decided; null when there is none). A card above it says one of two things since 0.115 (ADR 0061; it said three): the plan was approved, or only proposed, so the Designer is changing the page as the plan says, "Being built", the decision line naming "Catervas" when the approval has no agent and the Product Manager's name for an older log's, with the time and the reason; or it was sent back, so the Designer is looking again and will write a new plan, with the time, the reason, and how many plans have been sent back of the number that stops the task ("If a third is sent back"). A decision counts only for the plan it followed. Times say "today" for the day the page is read, in UTC. While the task is in progress, the page's heading says the same, and its lead counts the plans ("First plan.") in place of the tries. The task's history words the three `design_plan.*` events.

Its browser and its design review (added in 0.33; ADR 0026). The Designer opens the app in the preview Catervas runs in Docker's sandbox (8.3), through the Playwright connector (5.6), in its `explore` and `implement` sessions and in its design review of a Software Developer's change to the interface (5.4). It cannot be assigned a task while it cannot open the app: the governor refuses the assignment with `preview_not_set` when the team has no preview and with `designer_needs_sandbox` when the sandbox is off or Docker cannot be reached (checked once a minute at most), and with `designer_needs_browser` when its Playwright connector is off, so that Catervas gives it no work, as the agent page says. A process that has not said what runs previews, a command handled in its own process among them, runs none, so the assignment is refused there too (both added in the step's fix wave). What the web app shows of it: a task whose design review is due shows "Checking the screens" on its page, as its board card does while the Designer's design review session runs, and "Waiting on the Designer" on both while every Designer is paused, the page with a link to resume it, or "The Designer's browser is off" on both while its Playwright connector is off, the page saying so and linking to the Designer's page to turn it on, the active Designer's when a paused one is also on the team (added in the step's fix wave). The task page and the gate of a task whose change is to the interface show the Designer's letter, "<name>, your UI/UX Designer, checked the screens first", with its reasons and whether it passed the change on or sent it back, and "The four checks", one figure per width and theme with the screenshot, the width in pixels, and "No problems found" or each problem's help, rule and impact; on the gate the letter and the checks come before the Architect's review. The letter is signed by the Designer who recorded the review, not the team's first Designer. The Designer's earlier send-backs fold under "<name> sent it back once, on <day>" (or so many times, last on a day), with their reasons. The gate's "About this task" gains "Screens checked", the day of the passing review and its Designer, "Code reviewed", the day of the latest review that passed the code and its reviewer, and "Who looked at it, in order": Catervas's checks, then each design review and code review in time order with its outcome, then "Now you decide" while the work waits on the person. Once the Designer passed the screens, the reviewer's letter is headed "<name>, your <role>, reviewed the code after <Designer> passed the screens", and the send-backs end with "<builder> changed it, and the next look passed." No wire carries what the builder changed in answer to a send-back, so the line does not say it; the builder's letter above it is its latest completion note. `task.get` carries `ui_change` and `design_review`, null for a change that is not to the interface, else its `state` (`not_needed`, `waiting`, `waiting_on_designer`, `preview_missing`, `designer_needs_sandbox`, `designer_needs_browser`, `passed` or `failed`), its `reasons` once recorded, and its `checks`; and `design_reviews`, every `design_review.recorded` of the task oldest first, each with the Designer's `agent_id`, `pass`, `reasons` and `recorded_at`; `tasks.list` gives a task in `verifying` whose change is to the interface its `design_review_state`, the same `state`, which the board's card reads, and leaves it out for a task whose review cannot be read rather than failing the whole list (changed in 0.37); the query `task.screenshot { task_id, file }` answers `{ png_base64 }` for a file one of that task's `page.checked` events names, and `not_found` for any other. A Designer's task page has a side panel, "How <name> works", with the flow's five steps marked done or now and the plans sent back of the number that stops the task.

Bug hunt (added in 0.117; ADR 0063). In an existing repository's Catervafication the Designer hunts once for bugs in the app's screens (5.16) when its browser is ready: it opens the app in the preview at phone and desktop sizes, files each problem with `catervas_file_bug` and writes `docs/catervas/design/ui-bug-hunt`. A hunt runs no explore or design-plan stage and is not reviewed by an agent.

Kit (added in 0.101; ADR 0051; phase 8 step 07): the Designer's first kit skill, `catervafying-the-repository`: write the project's UI inventory, `docs/catervas/design/ui-inventory`, from the code that draws the interface and, with the preview running, the screens, each entry with where it was read. Documents are named by stem, without an extension, and written in the team's format (changed in 0.108).

### 6.9 DevOps Engineer (added in 0.32)

Mandate: deploy what the team integrated, watch production, restore the service when it fails, and fix the cause (ADR 0027; `docs/design/devops-engineer.md`). It is optional: the team builder offers it and does not suggest it. It changes code only in an incident's fix task and in the project's deploy configuration a task names.

Produces: deployments, incident notes, fixes on `fix/CTV-<n>` branches, completion notes.

Cannot: deploy anything but the commit the team integrated; call a platform's write tool itself; change secrets, environment variables, access rights, or scaling, or delete anything in production; open a shell in a production container.

Default tools: read, write_workspace, execute, git_local and network, the Developer's model, and three Catervas tools only it may call, each of the `external_effect` tier and each taking no version or service: `catervas_deploy`, which deploys the commit the default branch holds after the integrations its task depends on; `catervas_restart`, which restarts the service's pods or redeploys the same version where there are none; and `catervas_roll_back`, which returns the service to the last deployment Catervas recorded as healthy. Its reviewer is the Architect, or the Developer when the team has no Architect. Its kit (6.7) connects the one platform the project runs on (AWS ECS or EKS, Kubernetes, Vercel or Netlify, Render, Railway or Fly), with the read tools `network` and every other tool `denied`.

Approval. The three tools are `external_effect` (5.6), and their approval is given in one way until phase 14 is planned: an open incident pre-approves `catervas_restart` once and `catervas_roll_back` once, as below. Every other call asks the human.

Deploys. A deployment is a task whose `change` is `deploy`. How a deploy is approved is decided when phase 14 is planned (ADR 0062). Phase 14 step 05 adds `deploy` to the contract's `change` field (5.11), and holds the DevOps Engineer's other tasks, its fixes and its deploy configuration, to the rules 5.3 and 5.12 set for the roles that change code. `catervas_deploy` is refused outside a deploy task's session and an incident's fix. The task reaches `verifying` when the platform reports the deploy live and the service stays healthy for the project's settling period (five minutes by default): its health URL answers `2xx` and, where the connector offers one, the log error rate stays under the project's threshold.

Watching. While Catervas runs, a watch tick asks the connected platform for its deployments and health once a minute, through the read tools, with no model and no session; it records `health.changed` only when the health changes. On the user's own computer Catervas watches only while it runs; on the hosted service Catervas runs the watch.

Incidents. A failed deploy or an unhealthy service records `incident.opened` and starts a DevOps Engineer session in which `catervas_restart` is pre-approved once. If the service is not healthy within the settling period after the restart, `catervas_roll_back` is pre-approved once. The session then investigates and files a fix task with `catervas_create_task`, which, in an incident session alone, files a standalone task with the incident as its request and skips triage; the Definition of Ready (5.3) and the Definition of Done (5.4) still apply to it, and, as 0.115 (ADR 0061) took the human's acceptance of a `high` risk task and the judgment away, a `high` risk fix waits for neither. It runs under the usual spending limits, as any task does (changed in 0.116; ADR 0062); phase 14 step 05 adds the mark of an incident's fix, since until then nothing marks a contract as one; one agent reviews it, and once integrated the DevOps Engineer deploys it, which resolves the incident when the deploy settles healthy (`incident.resolved`). A second restart or rollback in one incident, an incident opened while another is open, and a spent budget ask the human, who may stop any step. Production logs are untrusted content (8.6): a log line answers nothing, approves nothing, and causes no call beyond these.

### 6.10 Procurement Specialist (added in 0.49)

Mandate: research any product or service the business needs, technical or not, a software subscription as much as stock to resell, a used car or a baby car mirror: list the sellers and makers, find their prices, ask them for quotes, check the sellers and the products (open recalls, the safety standard a product must meet, a used car's VIN), compare the offers in one currency with their landed cost, and set up a purchase order for the founder's decision; keep the register of sellers and subscriptions, and review each renewal before its decision date (ADR 0039; `docs/design/procurement-specialist.md`; the founder's decisions of 2026-10-05). What it produces is a buying recommendation and an order for the founder to decide, not legal advice, a contract or a payment. It is optional: the team builder offers it and does not suggest it.

Produces: in `.catervas/local/procurement/`, never committed: `vendors.xlsx`, the register; `evaluations/<name>.md`, one comparison per need; `orders/PO-<n>.xlsx`, each purchase order, written by Catervas; and `mail/`, its messages to sellers and their replies; the completion note that explains them.

Cannot: pay, buy, bid, check out, sign up, start a trial that takes a card, accept terms or sign; place, pay for, confirm or cancel an order, or mark one placed or received (added in 0.74); send a message itself (changed in 0.77): Catervas sends what it drafts on the founder's press, and an order's message only on the press of its order (`auto`, phase 12 step 01, will send the others without it); promise a seller to buy; write application code or anything in the repository; write outside its procurement folder; change Catervas's budgets or the books.

Default tools: read and network (to read sellers' pages, prices and terms), and Catervas tools, each of the `read` tier, that only it may call except where noted: `catervas_read_sheet` and `catervas_write_sheet` as the Finance Specialist has them (6.6), given its own folder, `catervas_write_sheet` refusing `orders/`, where Catervas alone writes a purchase order (`orders_are_catervas_s`, the first part of the path compared without regard to case; added in 0.74), and not `catervas_read_costs`, since the team's AI costs stay the Finance Specialist's (the founder's answer of 2026-10-07 to step 10b's readiness review); `catervas_write_evaluation`; `catervas_draft_purchase_order`, `catervas_read_purchase_orders` and `catervas_update_purchase_order` (added in 0.74, below); `catervas_request_data_pipeline` and `catervas_read_data_pipelines`; `catervas_draft_seller_message`, `catervas_read_seller_messages` and `catervas_read_seller_replies`. Its reviewer field names the Product Manager, who reviews nothing: Catervas accepts its tasks on their criteria (5.4; changed in 0.115; ADR 0061). Every role may read the folder's workbooks with `catervas_read_sheet` and `folder: "procurement"`, the Finance Specialist's `vendors.xlsx` rule and the reviewer's among them being gone (6.6; changed in 0.115).

As built (added in 0.70; phase 7 step 10b). The role is `procurement_specialist`, "Procurement Specialist", tag "PROC", with the persona "Finds the best seller at the right price", the model `claude-sonnet-5-5` at `medium` effort and the default session limits, tiers exactly `read` and `network`, the Product Manager as the reviewer field's value, and no code to change (5.12). A procurement task names the Product Manager alone as its reviewer, as a finance task does, and readiness refuses a contract that names another (5.3, `private_folder_reviewer`; the founder's decision of 2026-10-07); since 0.115 (ADR 0061) nobody reviews it, Catervas accepting it on its `artifact` criteria.
