Its seven `forbidden` lines are those of "Cannot" above, and its prompt and its one skill, `sourcing-a-product`, say them, with the loop (the need, the sellers and makers, prices, checks, the comparison, and a recommendation that stops there: the founder decides and buys), the rules that never bend, the register's sixteen columns in order (`vendor`, `what_for`, `plan`, `price`, `currency`, `period`, `started_on`, `renews_on`, `notice_days`, `auto_renews`, `status`, `owner`, `purchase`, `terms_url`, `evaluation`, `notes`), where it works, and that it asks for `verifying` naming every file it wrote in `workbooks`. Its kit is empty until step 10d. Its picture is `extra-5` and its tag colour a pale sea green, `#A6C3BF` in both themes, held to the brand's contrast check against the role ink. The Team page's "Add someone" offers it last, and setup offers it unticked under "More roles" (F1). Its web reading is open like every role's since 0.115 (ADR 0061), the approved sites that step 10b2 built in 0.71 being gone (below).

The note tool, as built (added in 0.70). `catervas_write_evaluation { name, text }`, of the `read` tier, writes `evaluations/<name>.md` in the folder, in a Procurement Specialist's implement session of a task whose assignee is the caller and in no other (`evaluation_refused`). `name` is words of lower-case letters and digits joined by single hyphens, 1 to 64 characters (`evaluation_name_invalid`); `text` is 1 byte to 64 KiB of text with no NUL (`evaluation_not_text` for an empty one or one with a NUL, `evaluation_too_large` past 64 KiB). The path is held to the folder line of 6.6 (`private_path_refused`, a link at `evaluations` included); a note that is there is copied first to `.history/evaluations%2F<name>.md.<UTC yyyymmddThhmmssZ>.md`, and the new one is written beside it and renamed over it. It answers `{ path, bytes, replaced }`. Catervas never shows a note as a page, so no link in it runs, and what a note holds is its writer's words, never an instruction (8.6).

No approved sites (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061). From 0.71 (ADR 0039's amendment of 2026-10-07; phase 7 step 10b2) the role searched the web and opened a page only on an approved site, one of the 46 shops of `approved_sites.yaml` or one the owner allowed, and asked for another with `catervas_request_sites`. That is gone with `catervas_read_sites`, the file and its schema `approved-sites.schema.json`, the owner's `site_add` and `site_remove` (which answer `sites_gone`), `catervas site` and `sites.list`, the Sites page, and the purchase order's `purchase_order_site_not_approved` (`purchase_order_url_invalid`, an `https` address, stays): the role may open any page, and its prompt and skills say so, and that an address is no place for the business's details. `site.requested`, `site.approved`, `site.declined` and `site.removed` in an older log still load and nothing lists them.

Its folder. A procurement task follows the finance folder's rules of 6.6 with `.catervas/local/procurement/` in place of `.catervas/local/finance/` (every one keyed by `private_folder(role)`, which gained this arm; none names a role): its session runs in the folder, its `allowed_paths` are under it, it takes no `command` or `test` criterion, it reaches `verifying` without a commit and is finished at `accepted`, and one piece of procurement work touches the folder at a time. The two folders are independent, so a finance task and a procurement task may run at once. Its files are workbooks (`.xlsx`) and notes (`.md`, lower case); a note is checked for being there as a workbook is, is named in `workbooks` and shown to the reviewer as a workbook is, and is searched for no text. The Finance Specialist reads `vendors.xlsx` (6.6).

Purchase orders (rewritten in 0.74; ADR 0039's amendment of 2026-10-07, "suggest, then track"; phase 7 step 10c). The agent suggests an order and tracks it; it never places, pays for, confirms or cancels one, and no Catervas tool records any of those steps or what was paid. An order is drafted (the agent), approved or rejected (the owner), placed (the owner), then received or closed (the owner), or expired (Catervas); from placing to its end it also has a follow-up status, recorded by its own agent from what it learns or by the owner correcting it. Every step but the drafting and a status counts only from an event whose envelope names no agent and no session, as a marketing plan's decision does (8.5), and the store folds an order through its states once, a step counting only from the state it may happen in.

The draft. `catervas_draft_purchase_order { seller, seller_contact, lines, currency, period, delivery, terms, url, evaluation, why }` is a tool of the `read` tier, offered to a Procurement Specialist in the `implement` session of a task it is the assignee of and refused `purchase_order_refused` in any other. It does not end the session, hold the task or ask before running, since nothing outside Catervas happens (5.7). Its input is checked in this order, each refusal named, with nothing written or recorded on any: `seller` 1 to 100 characters on one line with no control character (`purchase_order_seller_invalid`), `seller_contact` 0 to 200 likewise; `lines` 1 to 50 (`purchase_order_lines_invalid`), each `{ item, quantity, unit_price, unit }` with `item` 1 to 200 characters on one line, `quantity` an integer from 1 to 1,000,000, `unit_price` a number with at most eight whole digits and two decimals and no sign or separator, and `unit` 0 to 20 characters (`purchase_order_line_invalid`, with the line and the field); the total, exact in hundredths, at most 10,000,000.00 (`purchase_order_too_large`); `currency` three capital letters (`purchase_order_currency_invalid`); `period` `once`, `month` or `year`, a subscription's lines being per period; `delivery` and `terms` 0 to 600 characters each (`purchase_order_delivery_invalid`, `purchase_order_terms_invalid`); `url` empty or an `https` address that names a site (`purchase_order_url_invalid`, with 5.6's words for why not; the approved-sites rule `purchase_order_site_not_approved` of 0.74, from the founder's answer of 2026-10-07, "Yes, approved sites only", is gone since 0.115, ADR 0061); `evaluation` `evaluations/<name>.md` by the note tool's rule that exists (`purchase_order_evaluation_invalid`, `evaluation_missing`); `why` 20 to 600 characters (`purchase_order_why_invalid`); then no open order for the same seller, without regard to case, on the same task (`purchase_order_open`), an order being open until it is rejected, received, closed or expired; then at most 20 orders waiting for the owner in the project (`too_many_purchase_orders`). An empty `url` is a seller with no page, met by phone or in person.

The number and the workbook. One lock is held from the first read of the orders to the record that changes them, by the draft, by each of the owner's commands, by a status and by the expiry, so that two of them never take one number, decide one order twice or expire an order being placed. The number is one more than the highest among the log's drafted orders and the files `orders/PO-<n>.xlsx`, and is the order everywhere: `PO-<n>`, every command's `order`, the waiting row's, `catervas order approve <n>`. Catervas writes the workbook as a new file in the folder, never replacing one (`purchase_order_file_exists`), then records `purchase_order.drafted`, and removes the file if the log refuses the record; once the log has the order it is recorded and its file stays, whatever the projections do (changed in 0.74 after review). It has one sheet, `Order`: a header block (order number, date, buyer, seller and contact, currency, period, delivery, terms), then a line table (item, quantity, unit, unit price, line total) and the total. Quantities, prices and totals are number cells Catervas computes, never formulas, and text is text, so that the seller and the owner read the same numbers in any program. The buyer is the team's name. The agent never writes `orders/`, and reads the orders with `catervas_read_sheet`.

The owner's steps. Five commands (a sixth, `purchase_order_send`, is under "Contacting sellers"; changed in 0.77), on `POST /command` behind the daemon's token and in the browser's RPC behind its session, each checking and writing under the one lock: `purchase_order_decide { order, decision: approve | reject, note? }` (5.7); `purchase_order_place { order, placed_on?, paid?, currency? }`, the owner placed the order and paid for it themselves; `purchase_order_receive { order, received_on?, paid?, currency?, renews_on? }`; `purchase_order_close { order, note? }`, for a placed order that will not come, one the seller cancelled or refunded or that was lost; and `purchase_order_update { order, status, note?, expected_on? }`, the owner's correction of the follow-up status. The days are ISO days, `placed_on` and `received_on` today (UTC) when absent; `paid` follows `unit_price`'s rule up to 10,000,000.00 (`purchase_order_paid_invalid`) and `currency` three capital letters, the order's when absent beside a `paid` (`purchase_order_currency_invalid`), and a currency with no amount is never recorded; the latest `paid` given, at placing or at receiving, is what was paid; a `note` is at most 600 characters (`purchase_order_note_too_long`). Refusals by state: `unknown_purchase_order` for a number that is no drafted order; `purchase_order_expired` for any step on an order Catervas closed by itself; `purchase_order_decided` for deciding an order not drafted; `purchase_order_not_approved` for placing one not approved and `purchase_order_placed` for placing one placed already; `purchase_order_not_placed` for receiving, closing or correcting one not placed; and `purchase_order_ended` for any step on one received or closed. Under `auto` (ADR 0041) an order still waits: only `purchase_order_decide` from the daemon's token or the browser's session records an approval, and placing, receiving and closing stay the owner's in both positions. The owner does these on the agent's page (F1), which lists every order of the project with the agent that set it up (changed in 0.74 after review), and with `catervas order placed`, `received`, `status` and `close`, which take `<n>` as `12` or `PO-12` and record alone, filing no request.

The follow-up. `catervas_update_purchase_order { order, status, note, expected_on? }` is a `read`-tier tool offered to the Procurement Specialist in the `implement` session of a task it is the assignee of, refused `purchase_order_update_refused` in any other session or role. A status is one of `preparing` ("Being prepared"), `shipped`, `delayed` and `problem` ("A problem": out of stock, a payment refused, cancelled by the seller); `placed`, `received`, `paid` and the rest are `purchase_order_status_invalid`, the agent never saying that the owner placed an order or that it came. A `note` is 0 to 300 characters on one line, 1 to 300 for `delayed` and `problem`; `expected_on` is the day the seller expects the order, ISO and not before the day it is recorded, and `delayed` needs it. An order another agent drafted is `purchase_order_not_yours`, one not placed `purchase_order_not_placed`. It records `purchase_order.updated` with the agent's envelope, so it never counts as the owner's, and the owner's correction, which the owner records with the same body, replaces it while the order is placed. Following up is the agent reading the seller's pages; it sends nothing. A follow-up happens in a task: "Mark placed" offers to ask the agent to follow up until the order arrives, ticked, and a placed order has "Ask for a follow-up", each filing the owner's request (`request.file`, 5.16) in words the owner reads and may change first, which the Product Manager triages as any other. A problem that needs the owner reaches them as the agent's question in its task. `catervas_read_purchase_orders {}`, of the `read` tier, offered in the implement session of a task and in the role's chat, gives every order, oldest first, with its state (`drafted`, `approved`, `rejected`, `placed`, `received`, `closed` or `expired`), lines and total, the owner's notes as written (their own words, not wrapped as untrusted, ADR 0011), `placed_on`, what was paid and its currency, `received_on`, `renews_on`, its latest status with who recorded it (`agent` or `owner`), its note and `expected_on`, and `overdue`.

When an order ends. An order not decided within 30 days of its drafting, or approved and not marked placed within 30 days of its approval, closes by itself: on every tick not scoped to a task, before the pause is read, so that it starts no session and a paused team has it too, Catervas records `purchase_order.expired { order }` for it, whatever its task's state, a cancelled task's included. A placed order never closes by itself: the owner has paid, and an order that closed by itself would hide money spent on goods that never came, so it is `overdue` once its expected day (the latest status's `expected_on`, else 30 days after `placed_on`) has passed, and the owner ends it with "Mark received" or "It won't come". The agent's page lists orders to place, placed orders, and the five that ended last (F1).

Contacting sellers (as built in 0.77; phase 7 step 10f). The mailbox. The owner connects one address of their own for buying (a mailbox of its own, or an alias of the main one) with `procurement_mailbox.connect { address, name, provider, imap, smtp, username, password, folder, signature, disclose_ai }`, a method of the browser's RPC behind its session (and `catervas procurement mailbox connect`, which reads the password without echo or from standard input and refuses while another process drives the project), `provider` `gmail`, `icloud`, `fastmail` or `other` (the servers of the first three are Catervas's, those of `other` typed, `host:port`); `microsoft` is refused `mailbox_provider_unsupported` before anything is read, as is an address at Outlook.com, Hotmail, Live or MSN, since Microsoft no longer lets a mail program sign in with a password. Connecting logs in to both servers over TLS (the platform's certificates, always checked; a server that does not offer TLS is refused `mailbox_needs_tls`, an untrusted certificate `mailbox_certificate`, an unreachable server `mailbox_unreachable`, a refused login `mailbox_login_failed`), selects the folder read-only to read its `UIDVALIDITY` and `UIDNEXT`, sends nothing, keeps the password as a `Secret` (whose `Debug` prints `[redacted]`) in the keychain under `mailbox:<project id>:procurement` or, on a computer with none, in `connectors.json`, writes `mail/mailbox.json` and `mail/ledger.json` and records `mailbox.connected`. `procurement_mailbox.disconnect` forgets the password and deletes `mail/mailbox.json`, keeps `mail/out/` and `mail/in/`, and records `mailbox.disconnected`; `procurement_mailbox.check` reads now; the query `procurement_mailbox.get` answers `{ connected, address?, name?, provider?, folder?, signature?, disclose_ai?, checked_at?, error?, restarted_at?, sent_today, cap }`. Drafting. The agent writes to a seller or a maker only by `catervas_draft_seller_message { seller, to, subject, body, purpose, purchase_order? }`, a `read`-tier tool offered to the Procurement Specialist in the `implement` session of a task it is the assignee of that has a contract and in no other (refused `seller_message_refused`), with `seller` 1 to 100 characters, `to` one address with no display name and no list, at most 254 characters, on a domain `site_of` accepts and not the procurement mailbox's own, `subject` 1 to 200 characters on one line and `body` 1 to 8000 characters of plain text; `purpose` `quote_request`, `question` or `purchase_order`, the last requiring `purchase_order`, one drafted order of the caller that has no message yet, `question` allowing one the owner placed, and `quote_request` refusing it. At most 20 messages wait in a project. It writes `mail/out/<n>.txt` and records `seller_message.drafted { message, seller, to, subject, purpose, purchase_order?, sha256 }`, sending nothing; the message's number is one more than the highest among the log's and the files' in `mail/out/`, taken under the mail lock and counted from 1 (changed in 0.77 after review). The tool refuses with Catervas's words (`seller_message_field_invalid`, `seller_message_too_long`, `seller_address_invalid`, `seller_message_order_invalid`, `seller_order_message_waiting` for an order that has a message already, and `seller_drafts_full`). Sending. Only the owner sends: `seller_message_send { message, subject, body }` (`catervas procurement send <n>`, which prints the message whole first, or Today's "Send" or the dialog's after "Edit") adds the owner's signature and, unless turned off, "Written with an AI assistant and sent by <name> after reading it.", sends it from the procurement mailbox over SMTP and records `seller_message.sent { message, message_id, sha256, edited }`, keeping what went out whole as `mail/out/<n>.sent.txt`; `edited` says the owner changed the subject or the words, and the agent reads what was sent, not its draft. A server that refuses the message records `seller_message.failed { message, why }` with Catervas's sentence and the message waits, tried again by the owner's next press. `seller_message_discard { message }` records `seller_message.discarded`. At most 50 messages go in a UTC day, an order's included (`seller_send_limit`). Refusals: `unknown_seller_message`, `seller_message_sent`, `seller_message_discarded`, `seller_message_closed` (an order's message whose order was decided without it; added in 0.77 after review), `seller_message_is_an_order` (an order's message goes with its order), `mailbox_not_connected`, `seller_message_failed`. A send claims its message in memory, holds no lock while the servers answer, and records after; a claim dropped by a command cut off gives the message back. Approve and send. For an order whose message was drafted (`purpose` `purchase_order`), `purchase_order_send { order, message, subject, body, note? }` (the sixth owner's command of the orders, in the browser as "Approve and send to <seller>") emails the message with the order's workbook, `orders/PO-<n>.xlsx`, attached, to the seller and only then records `purchase_order.approved` (with the note), `seller_message.sent` and `purchase_order.placed` (today, UTC), each with no agent and no session; a failed send records `seller_message.failed` alone and the order still waits, and a second "Approve and send" of an order whose email is on its way is refused `seller_message_sent` ("This message is being sent."), while `purchase_order_decide` on an order being emailed is refused `purchase_order_sending` (changed in 0.77 after review). An order's message is sent by this command alone, never by `seller_message_send`, and the owner pays the seller outside Catervas: Catervas never pays. Replies. Every 15 minutes while a process drives the project, on a tick not scoped to a task and before the pause is read, so that a paused team reads mail too, with no model and no session, and on `procurement_mailbox.check`, at most one check at a time, Catervas reads the mailbox. It selects the folder read-only and fetches with `BODY.PEEK`, so it marks nothing read, moves nothing and deletes nothing, and it opens a message only when it is for the procurement address (named in To, Cc or Delivered-To), answers a Message-ID Catervas sent or comes from an address Catervas wrote to, and is at most 25 MB. An alias that shares the user's whole mailbox therefore shows Catervas only what the rule lets through. Each such message is kept under `mail/in/<yyyy-mm>/<n>/`, the month of the check that read it, which also stamps its record (changed in 0.77 after review): `text.txt` (plain text, an HTML-only message with its markup removed, at most 64 KiB) and the attachments that are PDFs or pictures of at most 10 MB, numbered from 1 and named by their number (`1.pdf`); any other file is listed by the name the sender gave it and not kept, and at most 100 attachments are listed, the first ones; a message with no sender is listed as "unknown sender" (changed in 0.77 after review). It records `seller_reply.received { reply, message, from, subject, date?, attachments: [{ name, kept, media_type?, bytes }] }` for the message of Catervas's it answers (by `In-Reply-To` and `References`, else the latest message to that sender). If the provider renumbers the folder (`UIDVALIDITY` changes) Catervas starts again after the last message and says so in `restarted_at`. A check that cannot read the mailbox keeps Catervas's sentence in `error`. A reply that cannot be kept or recorded ends the check there (changed in 0.77 after review): the replies before it are recorded once and passed, the ledger stays just before it with the time of the check and Catervas's own sentence in `error` ("Catervas could not keep a reply from the mailbox; it tries again in 15 minutes.", never the store's words, which repeat the seller's), the refusal is `mailbox_files`, and the next check, 15 minutes later, tries it again. Queries `seller_messages.list` and `seller_replies.list` answer the messages and replies with the seller and the subject Catervas sent (the subject shown for a reply is never the reply's own); a message that waits after a try that failed carries `why` and `failed_at`, the time of the latest failure the mailbox recorded (added in 0.77 after review); `seller_reply.attachment { reply, index }` answers a kept file as base64; `seller_reply_dismiss { reply }` records `seller_reply.dismissed`, and the reply stays kept. What the agent reads. `catervas_read_seller_messages` lists every message of the project with its state (`waiting`, `sent`, `discarded` or `closed`), why the last try failed, whether the owner edited it and its text (what was sent, for a sent one); `catervas_read_seller_replies { message? }` lists the replies, each reply's sender, subject, date, text and file names inside the untrusted-content notice of 8.6 (at most 80 KiB), and the paths of the files Catervas kept, which `Read` opens. Both are `read`-tier tools offered to the Procurement Specialist in the `implement` session of its own task (one it is the assignee of) and in its chat, and refused `seller_mail_refused` anywhere else, another Procurement Specialist's task included (changed in 0.77 after review). No tool of an agent sends, discards or records a send, a failure, a reply or a connection, and the log counts those only from an event whose envelope names no agent and no session. The command line: `catervas procurement mailbox connect|disconnect|show`, `check`, `messages`, `send <n>` and `discard <n>`; `send` and `discard` are commands sent to the process driving the project, and an order's message (`purpose` `purchase_order`) is sent from the browser alone, while a follow-up question, which names an order but is no order's message, is sent from the command line like any other (changed in 0.77 after review). Today shows each message that waits, whole, and each reply not dismissed, and the agent's page the mailbox (F1, F3). The user's main mailbox is never read beyond the alias rule, for 6.6's reasons. Under `auto` (ADR 0041; phase 12 step 01) a message will go as drafted within the daily cap; until then every message goes on the owner's press.

Data pipelines (the founder's decisions of 2026-10-05; rewritten in 0.76, phase 7 step 10e). When a source of prices or seller data it lacks would change a recommendation, the agent asks with `catervas_request_data_pipeline { name, what, source_url, why, cost, needs_account, sends_project_data }`, a tool of the `read` tier offered to a Procurement Specialist in the `implement` session of a task it is the assignee of and refused `pipeline_refused` in any other (`catervas_read_data_pipelines`, which gives its requests with their states, is also in its chat). `cost` is `free`, `paid` or `unknown`; `name` is one line of 1 to 100 characters, `what` and `why` 20 to 600 and `source_url` an `https` address of at most 2000 characters (changed in 0.76 after review) with no credential in it (`pipeline_field_invalid`, `pipeline_url_invalid`); three requests may be open at once (`pipeline_limit_reached`), and a name asked for twice, compared without regard to case, is refused while the first is open or approved (`pipeline_already_requested`). The tool records `data_pipeline.requested` on the task and holds no task: the session goes on, the task keeps its status, and a `source_url` is accepted and approves nothing. Nobody decides a request in a session any more (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061): the decision session of the Product Manager, `catervas_decide_data_pipeline`, its prompt and message, and the skill `deciding-data-pipelines` are gone. The tool itself answers at once. A request that is free, whose cost is known and that sends no project data out is filed as an ordinary request and approved by Catervas (`data_pipeline.approved { by: "catervas" }`); one that `pipeline_needs_owner` holds, because its `cost` is `paid` or `unknown`, or because it has `sends_project_data` (the founder, 2026-10-16: "Still ask me"), is recorded `data_pipeline.escalated` at once, with no agent and no session on the envelope and a reason in plain words: "It costs money, or its cost is not known, so you decide (ADR 0061).", or, for one that is free and sends data out, "It sends your project's data to another service, so you decide (ADR 0061)." An escalated request waits for the owner (5.7), who approves or declines it on Today or with `catervas pipeline approve <n>` and `catervas pipeline decline <n>`; a number that is no request is `unknown_pipeline`. `data_pipeline.approved` files an ordinary request (5.16) for the team to set the source up, titled "Set up <name> for the Procurement Specialist.", `created_by` `catervas` when Catervas approved it and `human` when the owner did, whose text holds the source's name, what it gives, its address and why, and, when the name is a connector of the role's kit, "Connect <title> on the Procurement Specialist's page."; approval connects, pays for and builds nothing, and approves no site. A decision names no task. The Procurement Specialist's skill `requesting-a-data-pipeline` says that a free source is filed at once and one that costs money, whose cost is unknown or that sends the project's data out waits for the owner. This step builds no `auto` mode: under ADR 0041's `auto` (phase 12 step 01) a `paid` or `unknown` source may be approved without the owner, recorded `by: auto`, but one that sends the project's data out is refused in both modes.

Renewals (rewritten in 0.74; phase 7 step 10c). While a process drives the project and the team has an active Procurement Specialist, a tick with no model and no session reads the `Vendors` sheet of `vendors.xlsx` once a UTC day and records `renewal.flagged { vendor, renews_on, decide_by }` for a row that is due, and `renewal.checked { due, unreadable }` for each day's run, which is how the next tick knows the day's check ran. The columns are found by their heading in the sheet's first row, `vendor`, `renews_on`, `notice_days` and `status`, case and surrounding spaces aside, so a column the user moved still reads; a date cell is read as its day. A row is read only when its `status` is `active` or `trial`; any other is neither due nor counted. The decision date is `renews_on` less `notice_days` (blank is 0); a row is due when today (UTC) is from 14 days before its decision date to `renews_on`, inclusive, and no `renewal.flagged` exists for that vendor, without regard to case, and that `renews_on`. A blank `renews_on` is no renewal; a `renews_on` that is not an ISO date, a `notice_days` neither blank nor an integer from 0 to 365, and a `vendor` blank, over 100 characters or holding a line break or control character are each counted and never guessed. A workbook with no `Vendors` sheet, or whose first row lacks any of the four headings, counts as one row it cannot read, or as many as the rows below the first that hold something; a register Catervas cannot open, or one past 10 MiB, counts as one row it cannot read and never stops the team, and one that is a link is not read at all, as the folder's other files are not. Today lists the renewals open, oldest first: `renewals.list {}` answers `{ open: [{ renewal, vendor, renews_on, decide_by, flagged_at }], unreadable }`, `renewal` the sequence number of its `renewal.flagged`, `open` every one with no `renewal.dismissed` the owner recorded, and `unreadable` the last `renewal.checked`'s (0 before any); a renewal is not a `waiting.list` row, which needs a task. "Ask for a review" opens the request "Review <vendor> before it renews on <renews_on>; decide by <decide_by>." in a field the owner reads and may change, and "Send to the team" files it (`request.file`, 5.16) and then dismisses the renewal, a refused request dismissing nothing; "Dismiss" records `renewal.dismissed` at once, and the register is unchanged. The owner's `renewal_dismiss { renewal }` is refused `unknown_renewal` for a number that is no `renewal.flagged` and `renewal_dismissed` for a second. `catervas renewal list` prints the open renewals and how many rows it could not read, and `catervas renewal dismiss <n>` dismisses one.

Kit (6.7; built in 0.75 to 0.78, phase 7 steps 10d to 10g): fourteen skills and seven services, none of which can buy. The services: Catervas's own `fx` (exchange rates over Frankfurter), `recalls` (US product and vehicle recalls, complaints, crash ratings and VIN decoding, over the CPSC and NHTSA, with no account) and `ebay` (eBay's listing search over its official API, with the user's own free developer keys); Exa (web search, no account), SerpApi (shopping prices across Google Shopping, Amazon and Walmart, its `search` `paid` with an allowance, since each search spends the user's; changed in 0.115); Brex (what the company already spends with a seller, signed in, read-only); and AWS Pricing (for a software team, a key that may only read prices). Nothing in the kit can buy. eBay is read only through `ebay` (the founder, 2026-10-07, asked whether to follow eBay's rules: "Follow eBay's rules"): eBay's User Agreement (posted 2026-01-20, in force 2026-02-20) bars "LLM-driven bots… to access our Services for any purpose, except with the prior express permission of eBay", so the skills read eBay never through SerpApi's `ebay` engine and never by opening ebay.com pages, and say eBay was not checked when `ebay` is not connected. `ebay`'s setup asks the user, before the first production call, to declare "Not persisting eBay data" (eBay's choice about a marketplace account's deletion), since Catervas never keeps an eBay member's name, and its answers carry no seller's username, which eBay's API License Agreement forbids collecting, only the seller's feedback score and percentage and the listing's address. Exa's search can show the agent text from any site's pages (the founder, 2026-10-07: "Keep it, say so"), so Exa's setup says it: what the agent searches for, with its one-sentence objective, goes to Exa as written. SerpApi's lens and reverse-image engines open an address on SerpApi's own servers, so its setup says that SerpApi may follow a link from the address the agent gives it to another site (the founder, 2026-10-08: "Keep it, say so"; 8.6; added in 0.75 after review). The approved sites those two sentences once named are gone (above; changed in 0.115). Every seller's page, price, listing and reply is untrusted content (8.6).

**Under autopilot (added in 0.138; ADR 0082).** A data pipeline request that is paid, of unknown cost or takes data out is decided by the Product Manager in a `decide` session with `catervas_decide_data_pipeline`, recorded `by: product_manager`, and Today lists none while the team decides; after three such sessions with no decision Catervas flags the request's task. While the team is not paused, each tick sends the seller messages drafted since autopilot was turned on, with no model, through the business's mailbox, recorded `seller_message.sent` with `sent_by: autopilot`, oldest first and at most 50 in a UTC day: a message beyond the day's waits on Today with Send and goes the next day, an order's email waits with its purchase order, and a message whose try failed waits for the owner. Purchase orders stay the owner's: the team never places one.

## 7. Functional requirements

Numbered so the milestone plan and tests can refer to them.

**F1 Team builder.** Create, edit, pause, retire agents. Assign roles. Set names, avatars (from a shipped pixel set or an uploaded 32x32 image), and persona lines. Suggest the six of 4.1 at setup, and offer the UI/UX Designer among the roles of an agent added later (added in 0.31). Offer the Finance Specialist there too, and never suggest it at setup; an agent added as one takes the picture `finance-specialist` and a spare name, and every other added agent keeps the extras (added in 0.54). Offer the Procurement Specialist there too, last, and never suggest it at setup; an agent added as one takes the picture `extra-5`, which leaves the extras `extra-2` and `extra-3`, shared again once both are taken, to every other added agent (added in 0.70; the extras were three until then). Setup's team step offers both through "Add someone", whose sheet chooses the newcomer's job (changed in 0.125; the "More roles" rows went); a newcomer takes the next spare name. The page adds no rule for the cap: "Continue" asks Catervas to check the team, which refuses a team of more than seven in its own words, shown under the rows and tied to none, and nothing is saved (added in 0.70). Enforce two to seven members with at least one Product Manager (changed in 0.103; ADR 0055), or exactly one agent alone (4.4; added in 0.125); a retired agent stays in the team file so that its past events still name someone, and is not one of the seven (added in 0.26). Show and edit per-agent permissions, MCP servers, skills, and model settings. Pausing an agent aborts its running session at the next tool call, a chat answer under way excepted (4.3; changed in 0.37), and moves its task to `blocked` with a note that says why (added in 0.2). A pause is written to the team file and recorded as `agent.updated`; a session of the agent that Catervas runs in the same process is aborted at once, and one run elsewhere at its next tool call, which the hook denies; each of the agent's `in_progress` tasks moves to `blocked` on its behalf with the blocker "agent paused by the user" ("agent retired by the user" for a retirement, which the human resolves by reassigning). Making the agent active again moves each task a pause blocked back to `in_progress` as the human, resolved "agent resumed by the user"; a task blocked for any other reason stays blocked. A pause longer than the blocked limit escalates its tasks as any block does (added in 0.8). An agent asleep at its model provider's limit (5.5) is not paused: it stays `active`, nothing is written to the team file, and its tasks keep their status (added in 0.13). The team editor meets section 10's foolproof configuration: a change that leaves the team without an active Product Manager (changed in 0.103), is refused before it is saved, in words that say what to change (added in 0.10). A team template (3) holds two to seven agents with at least an active Product Manager (changed in 0.103), by the same rules (added in 0.35; the judge it once had to hold is gone, 0.115). The browser reaches templates through two queries, `templates.list {}`, answering `folder`, null without a state folder, which the query no longer refuses, `builtin`, each ready-made team whole by its `slug`, each saved template whole by its `slug`, by name regardless of case, and each unreadable file's `slug`, a saved file under a built-in's slug among them (changed in 0.103), and `template.preview { slug }`; and four methods, `template.save { name, replace? }` and `template.rename { slug, name }`, each answering the `slug`, `template.apply { slug, digest }`, and `template.delete { slug }`. A preview and an apply answer the team, the ids that stay, are retired, are removed and join, the change in words, the team's refusals (`errors`, the codes the team editor uses, such as `needs_product_manager`), and the `digest`, the sha256 of the template file's bytes as they were read; an apply whose result is refused is refused with those errors and writes nothing, and an apply given a digest the file no longer has is refused with `template_changed` at `/digest` and writes nothing (added in the 0.35 fix wave). A template refusal carries its `code` and `path`: `template_exists` at `/name`; `template_name` at `/name`, a name with no letter or digit; `template_unreadable` at `/slug`, a file that is not a template, which can be deleted but not previewed, used or renamed; `template_builtin` at `/name`, a name a ready-made team has, which a save and a rename are refused (added in 0.103), with the words "Catervas comes with a team called <name>. Choose another name."; and `no_state_folder` at `/`; a slug nothing is saved under is not found. The page words each refusal from its code, never from the daemon's message. The Procurement Specialist's page has "Orders" directly before "Sites it may read" (added in 0.74; 6.10): a lead that says the agent suggests orders and follows them up and that Catervas never orders or pays; "Approved, for you to place", each order with its number, seller, total and period, the day it was approved, the day it closes by itself, "Mark placed" and "Download PO-<n>.xlsx"; "Placed", each with the day it was placed and what was paid, its latest status as a tag ("Being prepared", "Shipped", "Delayed" or "A problem", or "No news yet."), who recorded it, the agent's note in a frame that says whose words they are or the owner's correction as they wrote it, the day it is expected, "Overdue" when that day has passed, and "Mark received", "Correct the status", "Ask for a follow-up" and "It won't come"; and "Recent orders", the five that ended last, each with how it ended. The section lists every order of the project, not only those of the agent whose page it is, and each order says which agent set it up ("Set up by <name>."); a status says whose follow-up it was, and "Ask for a follow-up", "Mark placed"'s and "Mark received"'s tick boxes and the other steps name that agent, the one whose follow-ups count, so that the paid orders of a retired agent stay in sight (changed in 0.74 after review). "Mark placed" asks for the day, what was paid and in which currency, both optional, and offers "Ask <name> to follow up until it arrives", ticked, over the request in the owner's words; "Mark received" asks for the day it came, what was paid (what was said at placing, else the total), the day it renews, and offers "Ask <name> to update the register", ticked; "Correct the status" asks for one of the four statuses, what the owner knows (needed for "Delayed" and "A problem"; at most 300 characters, said at the field when it is longer) and the day it is expected (needed for "Delayed"; today or later, the picker starting there, and said at the field when it is earlier), and what the daemon still refuses as `purchase_order_status_invalid` is worded for all of those rules together, not for "Delayed" alone (changed in 0.74 after review); "It won't come" asks first. Each acts at once, not through "Save changes", sends its command and then, when the box is ticked, the request, and a refused command files no request. The section is only on this role's page. The Procurement Specialist's page no longer has "Sites it may read" (added in 0.71; 6.10; gone in 0.115, ADR 0061), nor the Sites page and the waiting row for a site request. The Procurement Specialist's page has "Procurement mailbox" before "Orders" (added in 0.77): where it writes from, when Catervas last read the replies or why it could not, and "Check now", "Change" and "Disconnect" (which asks first), or "No mailbox yet" and "Connect a mailbox", which opens the page that takes the address, the provider, the app password and the servers, says what an alias lets Catervas read, and sends nothing when it connects. Prove which found projects work together before any is made one team (added in 0.149): the proofs, shared work among them (added in 0.154), and hints of 3, `linking.pairs`, `linking.maybe`, `linking.groups` and `linking.answer` of 4.4, and the page "Do these work together?"; no link is made without the owner's Yes to a proof that holds. Make teams from the proposal (added in 0.150): `proposal.create` makes each card's team paused, adds a linked project to a team that exists as a repository, and `teams.undo` takes a team back until it first starts (4.4).

**F2 Projects.** Open an existing git repository or create a new one. Produce and store the project scan. Initialize `.catervas/`. Detect the project's test and build commands and add them to the criterion library (F16). Make a project folder of several repositories (4.1; added in 0.110). The daemon's `repos.list {}` answers `{ repos }`: `null` for a one-repo project, else the members in file order, each `{ name, path, integration_branch, missing }`, `integration_branch` as written or `null` and `missing` true when the path is not a directory or git's top folder of it is not the path itself. `repo.add { name, path, integration_branch? }`, with `path` relative to home, appends a member after the checks of 4.1 and records `repo.added`; it is refused as `not_a_project_folder` (`/`, "This project is one repository; adding another comes later.") on a one-repo project. `repo.remove { name }` removes one, leaving its folder untouched, and records `repo.removed`; `repo_in_use` (`/name`, "<n> of the project's tasks still work in <name>: <ids, joined by \", \">; finish or cancel them first"; added in 0.113) refuses a member that a task on the board names while that task is neither `cancelled` nor `accepted` and integrated, checked before `last_repo`, so an epic, which names none, never holds one, and a contract that cannot be read answers -32603 with the files' sentence and removes nothing; `last_repo` (`/name`, "A project keeps at least one repository.") refuses the only member, and an unknown name is -32002. `repo.locate { name, path }` records where a member is now, whether or not it is missing, under the same checks with the member left out of the others, and records `repo.moved`; it also runs `git worktree repair` in the located member (added in 0.113), so that the worktrees of its open tasks, which link to its old folder, work again, and a repair that fails leaves the folder recorded and writes git's words to the daemon's standard error. Each answers `{}`. The daemon knows home from `HOME`, else the folder `catervas serve` was run in, and without one answers -32603 "the home folder is not known" to `repo.add` and `repo.locate`. The teams on the computer (added in 0.144; ADR 0059): `teams.list {}`, answered by the hub on `/hub/rpc` and on `/rpc` while there is no current team, answers `{ teams, current, account_asleep_until }`, each team `{ slug, name, root, status, failed?, working_agents, waiting, today_usd, month_usd }` with `status` `running`, `paused`, `elsewhere`, `missing` or `failed` (and `failed` its sentence), `working_agents` the sessions running, `waiting` what `waiting.list` counts, `today_usd` and `month_usd` what its sessions cost this UTC day and since the first of the UTC month; `teams.current { slug }` sets the team `/rpc` answers and answers `{}`, an unknown slug being refused `team_unknown`; `teams.remove { slug, confirmed }` needs `confirmed: true` (else `confirmation_needed`), stops that team's drive as `catervas stop` does, forgets its project and deletes no file, and answers `{ removed: true }`; `computer.get {}` answers `{ agents_at_once, daily_cap_usd, spent_today_usd }` and `computer.set { agents_at_once?, daily_cap_usd? }` writes `state.json` and applies at once, `null` clearing a field, an `agents_at_once` outside 1 to 16 being refused `agents_at_once_out_of_range` and a `daily_cap_usd` of 0 or less, or over 100000, `daily_cap_out_of_range`.

**F3 Board.** Kanban view of the task lifecycle, with tasks grouped under their epics and standalone tasks on their own. Filter by agent, risk, epic. Open a task to see its contract, events, diff, notes, and cost. Create a request by hand (it enters as `draft` and is triaged; added in 0.3) and overrule a triage. On the command line (added in 0.8), `catervas task show` gives each event a summary of what it said (a move's statuses, who asked and why; a triage's size and reason; a question and its answer; an escalation's reason; a criterion's result; a note's first line; a session's purpose; a cost), cut at 200 characters; what the task has cost against its budget, in dollars, sessions, and tokens; an epic's tasks; and with `--diff` its branch's diff against the integration branch, against the merge commit's first parent once it is integrated, which an epic, having no branch, and a task not yet assigned refuse. `catervas task create <file> --parent <epic>` files a task under an epic in progress, as the human, triaged small at filing; it is judged against the Definition of Ready and assigned by the epic's assignee as the breakdown's tasks are. In the web app (added in 0.28), the board has six lanes, in order Planning (`draft`, `refining`, and an `escalated` task awaiting the human's approval of its plan), To do (`ready`, `assigned`), In progress (`in_progress`, `rejected`), Stuck (`blocked`, and any other `escalated` task), Review (`verifying`), and Done (`accepted`, and `cancelled` only when "Show cancelled" is on); a phone shows one lane at a time. Each row carries its assignee, its title linking to the task page, its id, and at most one mark: "Needs your help" or "Waiting on you" when the human is waited on, else what the working agent is doing (Writing, Building, Reviewing), else its status when it is accepted, cancelled, being reworked, or escalated; a row the lane already describes has none. A card of a task that waits on others says so in its meta, "Waits on CTV-1 (cancelled)": `tasks.list`'s rows carry `waits_on` (added in 0.134; ADR 0079), the contract's dependencies that are not yet accepted, each with its status, left out when there are none. The filters are by agent, "Only what is waiting on me", by epic (the epic and its tasks), by risk, and "Show cancelled". The task page has five tabs (summary and checks, history in plain words with each event's kind, leaving out the tool calls a session makes but keeping one Catervas refused, the plan, the code changes, and the notes, which are the latest note of each kind in the log, signed by its writer, falling back to the contract's own), its cost split into Planning, Building, Checking, and Meetings and talk against its limit, whether it was added to the project, and Stop and Cancel while they apply. The board has no line or lane for held-back work and no filter for a period of work (changed in 0.116; ADR 0062): a ready task is assigned as soon as an agent of its role is free, `tasks.list`'s and `task.get`'s rows carry no `backlog`, and the queries that answered it are gone (8.5). An agent with a stuck task and another under way shows as working (5.2). After "Waiting on you", Today lists the renewals coming up (added in 0.74; 6.10) as "Renewals coming up (<n>)", each with a calendar mark, "<vendor> renews on <day>", "Decide by <day> if you want to change or cancel it. It is in the register <name> keeps.", "Ask for a review" and "Dismiss", and, when the last check could not read some rows, "<n> rows in the register have a renewal date Catervas can't read, so Catervas can't remind you of them." ("1 row ... of it" for one), which stands alone under "Renewals coming up" when no renewal is open, and the section is left out when there is nothing to say. The vendor is shown as text. A day to come reads "today", "tomorrow" or the date, and one that has passed "today", "yesterday" or "on 2 October", with the year added when it is not this one. Today lists a data source the Procurement Specialist asks for and the Product Manager passed on (added in 0.76): why it comes to the owner in Catervas's words, the Product Manager's reason, what it would give and why in the agent's, the source's site in bold and its address as text with "Open", and "Approve" or "Decline", each opening a dialog with a note, the approving one showing the request the team will get. Today lists, after "Waiting on you", "Messages to sellers (<n>)" and "Replies from sellers (<n>)" (added in 0.77): each message that waits whole, with From, To (its domain in bold, and a note when nothing went there before), the subject, the body in a frame that says whose words they are, what Catervas adds, and "Send", "Edit" and "Discard", Send unavailable with no mailbox or at 50 a day; each reply with its seller, the subject Catervas sent, its From address as text and the warning, how many files were kept, "Read", "Ask for a comparison" (or "Ask for a follow-up" for an order's) and "Dismiss"; and the order's row offers "Approve and send to <seller>" with a dialog showing the email whole. Today lists, after the waiting rows, the card "Product plan changes to approve" only for proposals an older log holds (added in 0.95; 5.7; changed in 0.115; ADR 0061), and a folder change waiting to be merged is a row of "Waiting on you" under every team file (5.14). A new project's Today says in its band that the team waits for the product plan (4.1, 4.2; added in 0.100); the card "Your product plan to approve" and its place are gone (0.115). On a task's page (changed in 0.123) the Summary tab leads with the agent's latest note, then what the task is for, then its checks as one line ("2 of 3 checks passed.") with each check under "Show each check"; the try count shows from the second try; "Adding it to your project" shows once the task is accepted, waits to be added, was added, or works in a private folder. A board card shows its title in at most three lines and its id and epic on one line; Done shows every task waiting on the owner and the five with the highest numbers, then "Show all n". A card an agent has a session on (`team.activity`: working, with a session and the card's task) shows "<Name> · <Role> — thinking" with three quiet moving dots, still under reduced motion; it names the working agent (the reviewer on a card in review), not the card's assignee, and a task under way with no session shows no such line (changed in 0.124). While an agent's chat fork runs beside its work session, its activity and the card keep the work (ADR 0064).

**F4 Contracts.** Editor for the contract schema with validation against the JSON schema. PM authoring flow. Definition of Ready results displayed inline. The web UI's plan editor adds and removes a requirement or an exit criterion, but never the last of either, and a removed requirement leaves every criterion's `satisfies` (changed in 0.37).

**F5 Governor.** Everything in section 5, exposed as a library with no UI dependency, with a test suite that covers every transition in the table and every budget. It holds a new project to its product plan: `product_plan_first` refuses every task and epic but the plan's own until the two documents are on the integration branch, and `product_plan_approved` decides it from the paths git gives (5.3; added in 0.99).

**F6 Runtime.** Start, resume, and end agent sessions. Inject identity, memory, contract, and tools. Stream events to the UI. Compute cost per session from usage.

**F7 Channel.** Team chat with agent posts, user posts, mentions, ceremony threads, and a link from any message to the task or event it refers to. On the command line (added in 0.14), the user posts with `catervas say <text>`, whose `@<id>` mentions start the agent's conversation session, and reads the channel with `catervas channel [--last <n>] [--json]` (section 3); each message's JSON carries its `seq` and `task_id`, which are its link to the event and the task. A ceremony's messages are shown with their thread, `<time> <author> [<thread>] <text>` (5.9; changed in 0.15), and the channel's view comes with the web app (phase 6; changed in 0.18 from the desktop app in phase 5). In the web app (added in 0.29), the Channel page, between Board and Team on the rail (the rail's "Chats" from 0.34, where the channel is the chat list's first chat, "Team", at `/channel`, F8), reads the newest 100 messages through the query `channel.messages { before_seq?, limit }` (1 to 200, default 100; the newest page, oldest first within it), pages back with "Show earlier messages" (a page that cannot be read is said in plain words, and the button stays), and appends each new `message.posted` as it is recorded, without asking again, keeping it however many other events follow. An agent's post shows its avatar, name, role, and time; Catervas's system lines are small and muted; the user's own posts are labelled "You". `@human` is shown as "@you" and an agent's mention as "@<Name>", highlighted; `CTV-n` in a text, and a message's `task_id`, link to the task, followed by "waiting on you" when the task waits on the user; a reply says "Replying to <name>". Ceremony messages sharing a thread and a UTC day form one block, "<Review | Looking back>, <weekday>: N people posted" (N counts authors), collapsed (changed in 0.116; ADR 0062), with the anchor `#thread-<thread>-<date>`, paging back as "Show earlier messages" does while the pages read are no older than the meeting's day; a meeting the channel no longer holds is said in plain words. "Post to the team" sends `message_post { text }`, and Enter sends while Shift+Enter makes a new line (added in 0.34); typing `@` offers the team's agents, and a text over 2000 characters, counted in code points, is refused before it is sent. Today's "In the channel" shows, from the newest 20 messages, the last two that are not Catervas's own lines, then "Open the channel". Attaching documents (added in 0.131; ADR 0076; standalone plan `attached-documents`): the box has "Attach a document" and chips as Today's has (4.2), `message_post { text, attachments }` carries them, and a sent post shows each as a link to its document on Files (5.9, 5.17). The one-to-one chat's box does the same with `chat_message_post` (F8, 4.3).

**F8 One-on-one.** Direct conversation with an agent, read-only with respect to the project, with an offer to file a request (5.16), "Send as a task" and `catervas_take_task` (4.3; added in 0.117; ADR 0063). In the web app (added in 0.34; ADR 0026), "Chats" on the rail opens a list, `chats.list {}`: Team first, the channel (F7), then each agent in team order with its avatar, name, role and its chat's last line, and the agents that have retired under "Past teammates", their chats kept to read and with no box; on a phone the list is one row of faces above the open chat, Team first and past teammates last. The page fills the window and the list and the open chat scroll apart: the chat keeps its title at its top and its box at its bottom (on a phone the box's hints are read by screen readers alone). A chat opens at its newest message and follows new ones while the user is at its bottom; otherwise it stays where it is and shows "New messages", which goes to the newest, and the user's own message always goes there. Reaching the top reads the page before, as "Show earlier messages" above the first message does, the channel's and a one-to-one's alike, keeping what the user sees in place; a failed read stops until the button is pressed. Below 1440 pixels wide the Team chat's meetings fold under its intro (added in 0.104). `/channel/<agent_id>` opens that agent's chat, "Talking with <Name>" with a line saying the agent answers from memory and from reading the project and changes nothing but the work it takes on as its own task (ADR 0063; changed in 0.122), and "Back to Team"; an id that names no agent shows "No such teammate". The chat is read through `chat.messages { agent_id, before_seq?, limit }` (1 to 200, default 100; oldest first within the page), the user's lines labelled "You", their line breaks kept, and the agent's text rendered as Markdown (raw HTML off, unsafe links left as text), its task ids linked. "Message <Name>" sends `chat_message_post { agent_id, text }`, which has no author: Catervas writes `human`. Enter sends and Shift+Enter makes a new line, and a text over 4,000 characters, counted in code points, is refused before it is sent. A reply that proposes a request shows it in an editable box, its title and text, with "Send as a request", which calls `request.file { text, from_chat_message }`: the link must name an agent's reply that proposes a request not already sent, checked and filed under the one lock every filing takes, so two tabs cannot send one proposal twice; otherwise the call is refused with a sentence. The reply then shows "Sent as CTV-n", linked, from `chat.messages`' `sent_as` or from the `task.created` that names it. A new message of the open chat is appended as it is recorded, and the chat asks again on its agent's `chat` session's start and on any end of its agent's sessions. `chat.messages`' `waiting` says why the user's newest message has no answer yet, the first that applies: `retired`; `key_refused`, the team paused for the key ("<Name> cannot answer: your AI provider refused the key.", linking to Settings); `day_spent` ("Today's spending limit is reached, so <Name> will answer tomorrow. Your message is kept.", linking to Costs); `asleep`, with `until`; `answering`, pending or a session running ("<Name> is thinking…"); and `no_answer`, a session that ended without a reply ("<Name> could not answer. Ask again."). No event is written for a chat that did not run. An agent the user has chatted with is retired from the Team page, not removed, so its chat stays under "Past teammates". A new project's Product Manager interviews the owner there (4.3; added in 0.99): `chat.messages` answers each message's `heard`, `null` when it has none, the five parts of what the Product Manager heard; the command `product_plan_draft {}` files the plan's task; and the query `product_plan.state {}` says whether the project is new, whether its plan is approved, its task, and, while the task is `verifying`, its two documents. The chat shows the interview as 4.3 says: its own intro, "What I heard" under a reply that has it, and "Draft the product plan" under the Product Manager's newest message (added in 0.100).

**F9 MCP and skills.** (Changed in 0.117; ADR 0063: an agent asks for a connection with `catervas_request_connection`, and `team.get` answers `requested_connections`, 6.7.) Per-agent configuration of MCP servers (stdio and remote), tool tagging (5.6; changed in 0.38, from by tier), credential storage in the OS keychain, or in a private file on a computer without one (changed in 0.38). Per-agent, per-role, and team-wide skill folders (changed in 0.40; 6.7, ADR 0034). Skills are given through three commands, `skill_save`, `skill_remove` and `skill_confirm` (6.7), which the browser sends as `command`, and read through two queries: `skills.list { agent }`, which answers `{ skills: [{ level, name, description, state, bytes }] }`, the agent's skills as 6.7 computes them, `level` `role`, `team` or `agent` and `state` `in_use`, `replaced`, `review` or `missing`, role rows read-only, and an agent the team does not have is `not_found`; and `skill.get { level, agent?, role?, name }`, which answers `{ files, sha256, ignored_fields }`, `files` mapping each path to its text as the folder holds it (a file that is not UTF-8 text is refused with `skill_file_not_text`, as `skill_save`, `skill_confirm` and the checks refuse it, so the text shown is the text hashed; changed in 0.43), `sha256` the folder's `skill_sha256` that `skill_confirm` is given, and `ignored_fields` the frontmatter keys Catervas drops, a folder that does not exist being `not_found` and one the checks refuse being refused with that refusal's `skill_*` code at the start of its message. A `role` level, `{ level: "role", role, name }`, answers the `SKILL.md` Catervas ships for that role as `{ files: { "SKILL.md": text }, ignored_fields: [] }` with no `sha256`, since a shipped skill is trusted and pinned in the program; `role` and `name` are checked before anything is looked up, a role Catervas does not ship or a bad name being refused and a name the role does not ship `not_found` (added in 0.43). `catervas skill list [--agent <id>]` prints one line per skill, `<level>  <name>  <state>`, the states as `in use`, `replaced`, `review` and `missing`, the team's alone without `--agent`; `catervas skill show <name> (--team | --agent <id>)` prints every file, escaped, and the hash; `catervas skill add <folder> (--team | --agent <id>) [--yes] [--replace]` reads and checks the folder in its own process, prints what `show` prints, and on a terminal asks "Add <name> for <whom>? [y/N]", while without a terminal it needs `--yes`, a shipped name needing `--replace`; `catervas skill remove <name> (--team | --agent <id>)`; and `catervas skill confirm <name> (--team | --agent <id>) <hash> [--replace]`, the hash all of what `show` printed or its first 12 hex digits. The agent page's Skills section (added in 0.42) lists the rows of `skills.list` in three groups, "Comes with <role>" (read-only, each with its description), "For the whole team" and "Just for <Name>", each team or own row with "Edit" and "Remove". A `review` row says "Changed in the project. Review before <Name> uses it" with "Review"; a `replaced` team row says, muted, "<Name>'s own <skill> replaces this one for <Name>", and a `replaced` role row "Your team's <skill> replaces this one", or "<Name>'s own <skill> replaces this one" when the agent's own skill is the one in use; a `missing` row says "<skill> is in the team file but its folder is gone" with "Remove". "Remove" asks "Remove <skill>?", saying the agent (or the whole team) stops using it and its folder is deleted from the project, with "Keep it" and "Remove <skill>", and sends `skill_remove`. After any skill command the page reads `skills.list` and the team again, so a later Save cannot write back pins it did not know of. "Add a skill" and "Edit" open `SkillEdit`: who it is for ("Just <Name>" or "Everyone on the team"), a name, "When should <Name> use it?" and the instructions, or "Upload a SKILL.md instead", which replaces them with the file's text in one field. Edit reads the folder with `skill.get`; a skill whose `SKILL.md` holds anything but its `name` and `description` (any `ignored_fields`, or a frontmatter the dialog would not write back byte for byte) opens as its whole file, so nothing the person did not see is dropped, and a skill's other files are listed by name and size and sent back as they are. The dialog writes `SKILL.md` as `---`, `name: <name>`, `description: <a JSON string>`, `---`, then the instructions. A changed name, or a changed "Who is it for?", saves a new skill and leaves the old one, which the dialog says. "Next" shows every file of the skill, each in its own `untrusted` frame under its path, with "Catervas will follow these instructions and use these files. Read them before adding." and, when there are any, "Catervas ignores: <fields>"; "Add skill" is only there and sends `skill_save` with every file. When the name is one the role ships it adds "This replaces <role>'s own <skill> for <whom>." and the button reads "Replace and add skill", which alone sends `replace_shipped`. A name another role ships, which the page does not know until the daemon refuses it with `skill_name_taken`, stays on this step and adds "This replaces the skill Catervas comes with of that name, <skill>, for <whom>." with the same button (changed in 0.43). A name quoted in an uploaded file is read without its quotes. A refusal returns to the first step, said under its field and in Catervas's words, never the daemon's: `skill_runs_commands`, `skill_attaches_files`, `skill_too_large` and `skill_file_not_text` under the instructions, the name's and the description's under theirs. "Review" opens `SkillReview`, which reads the folder with `skill.get` and shows every file in an `untrusted` frame under its path, then the files with their sizes, with "Use this skill", which sends `skill_confirm` with the `sha256` it showed (and `replace_shipped` for a shipped name, with the same sentence, which for a name another role ships appears once the daemon has refused it with `skill_name_taken`), and "Remove"; a folder `skill.get` refuses shows "This skill can't be used: <reason>." with "Remove" alone. A role's own skill has "Read" (added in 0.43), which opens `skill.get`'s role level read-only: its text as shipped, with no `untrusted` frame, since Catervas ships it, and "Close". In the web app (added in 0.33), the agent page's Connectors section switches the built-in Playwright connector on and off for the agent (5.6), showing the change before it is saved. A user's own servers (added in 0.38; 6.7, ADR 0030). The browser reaches them through three methods: `connector.tools { agent, server, keys }`, which lists the server's tools with the agent's keys and keeps nothing, answering `{ tools: [{ name, description, usable }] }`; `connector.connect { agent, server, keys, tags }`, which lists them again, labels each usable tool by `tags` or else `paid` (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061), refusing a tag for any other name (`tag_unknown_tool`), keeps only the keys the entry names, and handles `connector_connect`, answering `{ stored_in: keychain | file, tools }`; and `connector.disconnect { agent, server }`, which handles `connector_disconnect` and then deletes that agent's keys, answering `{}`. `server` is the entry as 6.7 describes it, without `source` and `tools`; the keys travel to the daemon, which keeps them as 6.7 says, and a refusal of either method that carries keys has no `data`. A refusal of the entry carries the team's errors, each at its field. `team.get` answers `connectors` beside `team`: each agent's custom server with its `state`, `connected` when the definition kept on this machine is the team file's and every key it names is kept, `connect_again` when none is kept or the team file changed since, and `store_unavailable` when the keychain or the private file could not be read the last time it was, and, whenever keys are kept for it, `stored_in`, `keychain` or `file`; the daemon reads the store once per connect and disconnect, at session setup, and the first time a server is asked about, so a keychain is not asked at every `team.get`. It also answers `sandboxed`, whether sessions run in Docker's sandbox (added in 0.38 after review): true when the project's sandbox setting is `docker` (8.3), whether or not Docker answers at that moment, since a session does not start without it, and false in no-sandbox mode. It is read from the setting and never by asking Docker, so that `team.get`, which Today asks first, is not held up behind `docker info` (changed in 0.63). The agent page lists them under "Added by you" ("connectors Catervas has not checked; you labelled their tools"), each with "Started by a command on this computer" or "Reached at a web address", where its keys are kept when some are ("<Name>'s keys are in your keychain" or "in a private file on this computer"), and its tools counted by label. A `connect_again` row says "Connect again to use it", that its settings in the project changed since it was connected on this computer, and offers "Connect again", which opens `ConnectorAdd` filled in from the team file with the keys empty, every header on a line of its own, "Where the key goes" first, each one changeable and removable (changed in 0.38 after review, from the others sent unseen); a `store_unavailable` row says "Catervas cannot read <Name>'s keys for <server> right now", with a note to choose "Always" when the computer asks whether Catervas may use the keychain, and offers no Connect again. "Remove" asks "Remove <server> from <Name>?", saying Catervas deletes the keys from the keychain or the private file that keeps them, with "Keep it" and "Remove <server>", and says a refusal in plain words. Under Advanced, "A custom connector" says Catervas has not checked it, so the user labels each of its tools, that a connector started by a command runs on this computer with the user's rights, and that it runs in a folder Catervas keeps for it, so a file of the user's is given by its full path, with "Add a custom connector". `ConnectorAdd` is a dialog of three steps. "How to start it": the name; "A command" or "A web address"; the program, with each part after it in a field of its own under "What comes after it" ("Add a part"), so a part holding a space is kept whole (changed in 0.38 after review, from the command split on spaces), or the address with "Where the key goes", one header line filled with `Authorization: Bearer {API_KEY}`, and "Add a header" for more, each line `Name: value` with "Remove", a name an earlier line has said at the later line before anything is sent; and the keys, each a name and a value in a password field. An address holding a key is refused before anything is sent, saying a service like this cannot be added yet. "Next: list its tools" calls `connector.tools`. "Label its tools": each usable tool with "Only reads" (`network`), "Changes things" (`external_effect`, which runs without asking and is recorded), "Costs money, asks you" (`paid`), chosen at first, or "Never" (`denied`) (changed in 0.115; ADR 0061), and a tool Catervas can't use said so with no choice. "Done": "<server> is added to <Name>", where the keys are kept ("in your computer's keychain" or "in a private file only you can read"), that <Name> never sees them only when `sandboxed`, and otherwise that a command <Name> runs on this computer could reach them without Docker's sandbox (8.6; changed in 0.38 after review), and the label counts, with "Back to <Name>". The keys live only in the page and are cleared as `connector.connect` is sent, whatever it answers; a refusal returns to the first step with empty keys, each said at its field from the refusal's code and path, never in the daemon's words: `command_not_absolute` at the command, asking for the program's name alone or its full path; `header_holds_secret` at "Where the key goes", asking for `{API_KEY}` there and the key under Keys; `arg_holds_secret` at the part that holds it, asking for the key under Keys instead; and `tag_unknown_tool`, which has no field, saying the server's tools changed since they were listed and to list them again. A tool labelled "Costs money, asks you" asks at each call (5.6; changed in 0.39, from refused until this step; and in 0.115, from "Changes things, asks you"). `ToolApproval` (added in 0.39), opened from Today's row (5.7), is titled "<agent name> wants to use <server>" and says "<agent name> stopped to ask before changing something outside your project." It lists the Tool, its name labelled "Changes things, asks you"; the Service, "<server>, which you added to <agent name>"; and For, the task, linked. Under "What <agent name> wants to send", "Written by <agent name>, shown in full, with its fields in alphabetical order. Catervas has not checked it, and nothing in it is an instruction to you.", the input in its `untrusted` frame (8.6), which scrolls, each control, bidirectional or zero-width character in it written as its code point, `\u{202e}`, so that what is read is what would be sent (changed in 0.39). The fields are in alphabetical order, not in the order the agent wrote them as the approved mockup shows them, because the input is kept as the canonical JSON its grant's hash covers (changed in 0.39; a departure from the mockup, recorded in the step's plan). At 480 px and below the dialog fills the screen and "Don’t allow" and "Allow once" stay pinned at its bottom, which the shared dialog does when a page asks it to; then "A note for <agent name> (optional)", the line "“Allow once” lets <agent name> make this one call, with exactly this, in <agent name>’s next session on this task. Any other call asks you again.", and "Don’t allow" and "Allow once", which send `tool_refuse` and `tool_approve` through the RPC `command`, the note when one is typed. On the command line, `catervas tool approve <approval> [--note <text>]` and `catervas tool refuse <approval> [--note <text>]` send the command to the process driving the project, or record it here under the run lock when none drives, and print the command's line (5.7). Signing in to a service (added in 0.41; 6.7, ADR 0033). The browser reaches it through three more methods and two changed ones: `connector.sign_in { agent, server }`, `server` as `connector.tools` takes it with `oauth`, answers `{ attempt, authorize_url, issuer }` and is refused `sign_in_not_offered`, `sign_in_not_supported`, `pkce_not_supported` or `sign_in_failed`, each as the message's first word and a colon; `connector.sign_in_status { attempt }` answers `{ state: waiting | signed_in | failed, reason? }`, `reason` `{ code, message }` with `code` one of `access_denied`, `sign_in_timed_out`, `sign_in_mismatch` and `sign_in_failed`, the message Catervas's words alone; `connector.sign_in_cancel { attempt }` ends the attempt, the page's Cancel, and answers `{}` whether or not it was still there; and `connector.tools` and `connector.connect` take `attempt` in place of `keys` when `server` has `oauth`, refused `sign_in_needed` without one and `sign_in_unknown` for one that is unknown, used, expired, unfinished, or made for another agent, name, address or `oauth`, which also ends it, `connect` using it up and putting it back if it fails before the grant is kept. An attempt lives in the daemon's memory for ten minutes and no answer carries a token. `team.get`'s `connectors` rows gain `auth`, `keys` or `oauth`, `revokes`, for a signed-in row whether the service can be asked to forget the grant, and the state `sign_in_again`. `connector.connect` answers as before and `connector.connected` carries `issuer`. A role's kit on the agent page (added in 0.44; 6.7, ADR 0036). `team.get` answers `kits`, each role on the team (not retired) whose kit has a `stdio` or `http` service, `{ role, connectors: [{ name, title, about, why, setup, key_page?, labels, auth, credential_keys }] }`, no `container` connector among them; each `connectors` row gains `source`, `custom` or `kit`, and its `state` may be `not_in_kit`. `connector.tools`, `connector.sign_in` and `connector.connect` take `server` as `{ name, source: "kit" }`, a form of its own with nothing else in it, so a browser cannot send fields the kit decides, and `connector.connect` then takes `tags: {}`. The agent page's Connectors section shows "From the <role>'s kit" ("services Catervas checked; each tool is already labelled") above "Added by you": each service's title and why, with "Connect", or "Connected" and "Remove", or, when the kit changed since, "Catervas updated this service. Connect it again to keep using it." with "Connect again" and "Remove" (or "Sign in again"), or, for a service the kit no longer has, "Catervas no longer offers this service" with "Remove" alone. "Connect" opens `ConnectorAdd` from the kit, a dialog of two steps, "Connect" and "Done", with no labelling step: the service's about, "Why <Name> wants it" and "What to do" (its setup, which may quote the service's own label), "Get your key" opening the key page in a new tab, and one field per key, "Your <Service> key", "For <Name> only, and never shown again. Catervas checks it with <Service> before keeping it.", or, for a service that signs in, "Sign in with <Service>", whose page is asked for when the dialog opens so the click opens it, and a finished sign-in connects at once. "Done" lists the tools by their kit label, or by their name with `_` and `-` read as spaces, in "<Name> can now" (`network`), "<Name> asks you first before" (`paid`) and "Catervas never offers" (`denied`), where the key or the sign-in is kept, and "Only <Name> has <Service>. To give it to someone else, connect it from their page." Saving the agent keeps a kit connector connected meanwhile, as it keeps a custom one. A kit connector's spending tools carry allowances (6.7; ADR 0037). A service that takes a public client but registers none is signed in to with an app of Catervas's own (6.7; added in 0.58): `connector.sign_in` then also answers `provider`, `user_code` and `install_url`, and `team.get`'s connector rows `provider` and `settings_url`. Suggested connections on Today (added in 0.105; 6.7): `connector_suggestion.hide { agent, server }` answers `{}` and `team.get` answers `hidden_suggestions: [{ agent, server }]`.

**F10 Pixel office.** A single scene: desks, agents, a meeting table for ceremonies, a door for the user. Agents move between desk, table, and a whiteboard based on state. Clicking an agent opens its panel. The scene is decorative and informative, never the only way to do anything; every action is also reachable from the board.

**F11 Audit.** Event log viewer with filters. Export as JSON lines. Cost report per task, agent, day. Replay an exported log into a fresh set of projections, for debugging and for demonstrations (added in 0.2).

**F12 Notifications.** Notifications for escalations and deliveries, from the desktop app, and from the web app when the user's browser allows them (changed in 0.18). Configurable quiet hours. The daily reminder (added in 0.151; ADR 0059): once a day, at a time the owner picks (9:00 on their computer's clock by default), Catervas gathers what needs them into one digest and tells them once, in a browser notice when a Catervas tab is open and otherwise from the operating system (4.4, 8.6).

**F13 Premium hooks.** License check, hosted-run toggle, and cloud sync are stubs in the open-source build. They must be present so the premium build is the same codebase with features enabled, not a fork.

**F14 Contract authoring assistant (added in 0.2).** Write an epic or a standalone task contract alone, with the Product Manager, or from a brief or issue link, with the Product Manager's questions answered first, Definition of Ready results shown live, criteria from the library, a lock that makes the contract human-owned (5.11, 5.13), and the approval that lets it be broken down (5.16). Questions from agents are shown and answered in the same place (5.7).

**F15 Team rules (added in 0.2).** Edit the rules in 5.12 from the team editor and the command line; every refusal they cause names the rule. Every setting it edits meets section 10's foolproof configuration (added in 0.10; the editor's edit of the readiness judgment's policy is gone, 0.115, ADR 0061).

**F16 Criterion library (added in 0.2).** List, add, edit, and remove named criteria in `.catervas/team/criteria.yaml`; seed it from the project scan; reference criteria by name when authoring.

**F17 Harness metrics (added in 0.2).** Compute from the log, per project: first-pass acceptance rate, human interventions per accepted task, cost per accepted task split by session purpose (refine, implement, verify, ceremony, conversation, and, added in 0.130, goal), the share of exit criteria verified by command or test rather than by review or human, and active weeks. Shown on the command line and in the app; these are the five numbers `docs/PRODUCT_ANALYSIS.md` says to track from Milestone 0. Each is defined over the whole project, from the projections of the log and, for the criteria, the contract files (added in 0.8).
